Run against 122bafe (before the descriptor answered `checkSidName`), 6 of the 7 rows in RoleSidValidationTest failed; T-02-106 passed there as intended, because it pins the unchanged 918 `checkName` behaviour.

194. **Request Change Permission link with one parameter (T-UI-10/15, e2e-06 DEF-01).** The new job page's menu escaped the `&` of `?scopeType=JOB&scopeFullName=...`, so the form lost the job. The link now carries `scopeFullName` only and the grant form defaults to the JOB scope. T-UI-10/15 compare the resolved href with `<root URL>batch-control/grants/?scopeFullName=<encoded full name>` and, because the defect was visible as a form that was not about the job, follow the link and assert the form's scope type is JOB, the scope field holds the full name, the page says "Prefilled for" the job and CONFIGURE is checked. Green at commit time. Since D-71 the form has no scope type: the rows assert that it carries no scope type control, and the link may also carry `actions=CONFIGURE` but never `scopeType` (note 260).

195. **D-38b rows (T-05-26..30; T-05-25 follows the redirect).** Written from the SPEC item 2 D-38b line, D-38b and spec-review-S5 B-1. The actor `fr` now holds Item/Read and Request only through the folder property of `ops` (Overall/Read globally), so jobs outside the folder are invisible to fr and "requests of jobs they cannot see" is measurable. Submissions in these rows follow redirects with their own client, because `ApproverFormFixtures.post` turns redirects off (`client`, line 60) and that is how T-05-25 missed the 404 on the landing page. The root and sections are asserted reachable for fr after fr has a request of their own, which satisfies both the SPEC line and D-38b's "holds Request globally or has requests of their own"; reachability before any own request is not asserted. T-05-30 is the 404 guard for a user without Batch Control permission and without own requests. Red against 96e2a24 (before D-38b): T-05-25/26 land on a 404, T-05-27 404 on `changeApprover`, T-05-28 404 at the root, T-05-29 403 on the ACTIVATE request; T-05-30 green (guard).

196. **APPROVERS_CHANGED notice (T-05-31/32, spec-review-S5 m-3).** The re-designated approver decides with the APPROVERS_CHANGED mail, so it carries the D-38a notice under the same condition as REQUEST_CREATED (T-05-23/24); observed through the shipped e-mail notifier as in note 184. Green against 96e2a24.

197. **Redirect query cap (T-06-97, security-33 S-33-03).** The D-60 redirect query is capped at 4000 URL-encoded characters (counting `?`, `&`, `p.<name>=` and the value), filled in parameter-definition order; a value that would pass the cap is skipped and a later shorter one may still fit; the 2000-character per-value bound (T-06-93) is unchanged. Values of plain ASCII letters are used so that encoding does not change lengths: `?p.A=` + 1500 = 1505, `&p.B=` + 1500 brings 3010, C would bring 4515 and is skipped, `&p.D=short-d` brings 3022. Green at commit time (ui-dev 3a5baf7).

198. **Active-grant URLs in a real Jenkins (T-UI-48).** The GET-only redirect handlers of the active-grants section were replaced by views (reviewer comment 2026-09-27, ui-dev aadb8da). The row runs under `RealJenkinsExtension`, as T-UI-46 does, because a plain JenkinsRule's flat class path has hidden view-resolution failures before; it asserts the 302 and its resolved Location under the non-root context path for an administrator and a RequestGrant holder, 405 (not 404) for a GET of `revoke`, and a refusal for a user without a grants permission. Green at commit time.

199. **D-38b service rows (T-05-33..35).** Written from the SPEC item 2 D-38b line and D-38b; the service entry names were given by the coordinator (core-dev 68d9c01) and the signatures read from the compiled public API only (`javap -public`), not from src/main: `cancel(String)`, `changeApprovers(String, List)`, `canCancel(request)`, `canChangeApprovers(request)` (answering for the current authentication) and `hasOwnRequests(Authentication)` on RunRequestService and ActivationService. Losing Request is modelled by replacing the folder property with one that keeps Item/Read, so the refusal measures Request alone. Green at commit time (the methods did not exist before 68d9c01).

200. **D-59a moved-job lock and the refusal page link (T-SEC-64..69).** In every row u1's move is allowed by D-59 (native Delete on the source, native Create on the destination), so the rows test only the D-59a lock. The HELD record must name the job and contain "mov". T-SEC-64 has no negative twin: a user who cannot read the item gets 404 from its move endpoint before any refusal page exists. With the test files copied onto the committed HEAD 84c7c9a (core-dev's D-59a work still uncommitted), T-SEC-65/66 failed and the rest passed; with core-dev's work in progress, all six pass.

201. **Global matrix per-item warning and the matrix variant's name (T-02-108..110).** SPEC 8 says the warning comes "before its install action". Core's administrative-monitor markup puts the controls container first in the DOM and shows it beside the message, so DOM order cannot express that. The rows therefore assert that the warning is in the message text shown with the button, and that the confirmation question repeats it. A first version asserted DOM order and failed on correct markup; it was the assertion that was wrong, not the product.

202. **UI polish markup evidence (T-UI-50..52).** These rows give automated evidence for checklist items that only had e2e coverage. A control is found by its endpoint (`href`, `data-url`, `formaction`, or the submit button of a form whose action ends in `/cancel`, `/revoke` or `/revert`), never by its caption. The Revert control is looked for on `manage/batch-control-configuration/` and then on `manage/configure`. All three rows failed on fc720fb, the commit before the polish.

203. **Request Run in the new job page's app bar (T-UI-55).** Automated evidence for a checklist item that only had e2e coverage. It uses core's public menu API (`Action#getGroup`, `Action#getSemantic`), so it checks the declared placement and style rather than the rendered page.

204. **Rebuild Last in the job context menu (T-06-98/99, e2e-07 DEF-06).** The flag is set as a system property and cleared after each test. T-06-98 failed on 49472ed, before the fix, with "'Rebuild Last' has a null URL" in the `event` of the new menu model, so the row reproduces the defect. The job-without-a-completed-build case is rebuild's own defect (LIMITATIONS 45) and is not asserted.

210. **Discover-only move destination (T-SEC-70/71, backlog #74).** Written from SPEC 8 (D-59), issue #74 and security-33 S-33-05. The "folders plugin's normal answer" is measured, not assumed: it is the answer to a destination that does not exist (`/no-such-folder`), and the Discover-only destination must get the same status. The 403 S-33-05 describes could not be reproduced from outside: with native Delete, with granted Delete, with Create on `secret` without Read, with global Create and with a CREATE window on `team`, the folders plugin answered 302 for `/secret` on 39f4bad (before the fix) as well as after 02ca78a. Both rows are green on both commits; T-SEC-70 is a regression bound, not a reproduction.

211. **Requester Build notice across views (T-05-36..39, backlog #75).** Written from SPEC 5 (D-38a), issue #75 and the behaviour core-dev reported (per-request cache, 5 minutes on the plugin clock, dropped when the request is saved). A test `AbstractPasswordBasedSecurityRealm` counts `loadUserByUsername2` per name; only lookups of the requester are counted, after REQUEST_CREATED reached the notifiers. On 39f4bad (no plugin cache) 5 views already cost one lookup of nb, so T-05-36 does not discriminate the fix; it stays as an upper bound. T-05-37..39 assert correctness only (the cache must never hide a change of Build after a new request, a save or the cache life); they pass on both commits. The stale answer inside the cache life is deliberately not asserted.

212. **Activations section for per-folder Request holders (T-05-40, backlog #87).** Written from SPEC 2 (D-38b line, now naming D-38c) and DECISIONS D-38c. fr is admitted to the root by an own run request only, so the row measures that the activations section no longer needs an own activation request. Red on 39f4bad (403), green on the backlog/ux head.

213. **Grant request landing (T-08-65, backlog #89).** Same landing contract as T-05-26 for run requests; the submission follows redirects with its own client. The table width part of #89 (1280 px) is a visual property and is left to e2e. Red on 39f4bad (landed on the Grants list).

214. **Revocation reason of the kill switch (T-08-66, backlog #85, D-63).** On 39f4bad the record detail already said "change control was switched off", so the record half failed there only on D-63's wording; the grants screen half is the real gap (it read like an individual revoke). The screen is opened after change control is turned back on (with the setter, which revokes nothing), because the reason must survive on the listed closed window.

215. **Windows behind a move (T-09-24, backlog #84).** Asserted structurally: each window id must appear in the record's grantId or detail, and grantId must be the CREATE window (core-dev's reported contract); the exact sentence is not asserted. The refusal page's "Grant" column (UX-4) is not covered. Red on 39f4bad (only the CREATE id).

216. **Pre-filled grant form on the move refusal (T-SEC-72, backlog #83).** Links are found in `#main-panel` by target (`batch-control/grants` with `scopeFullName=`), never by caption. Only Delete is missing in the fixture, so a link for `team` would offer a window that cannot help; the row refuses it. The Move page hint of #83 (UX-3) is not covered. Red on 39f4bad (no such link).

217. **Overview counts (T-UI-56, backlog #88).** The count is read as the first stand-alone number in the body link to the section or its three nearest ancestors, so the row does not depend on captions. The shipped overview counts requests, activations and grants; incidents are not counted and the row does not demand it. Red on 39f4bad (no section links in the body).

218. **Naming strategy on moves (T-SEC-73/74, D-59b).** Written from SPEC 8 (D-59 line as amended) and D-59b. The Create item role uses `team(/team-.*)?` so that Create on the container `team` is a measured premise, and the naming strategy refuses `team/x` while it accepts `team/team-ok`. "Naming the naming rule" is asserted as the word "naming" in the record's target or detail. T-SEC-73 fails on 6ba5aec (302, the item moved) and passes with core-dev's uncommitted MoveGuard change.

219. **Change control off (T-SEC-75).** The twin refusal comes first so that the row cannot pass because moves are never refused. It fails on 6ba5aec at the twin, for the same reason as T-SEC-73.

220. **Job-level URLs after StaplerProxy removal (T-UI-70..72, #71, D-64).** Real-class-loader smoke (`RealJenkinsExtension`, as T-UI-46/48). D-64 moves the activation form to its own action at `<item>/batch-control-activation/` (submit `.../submit`, POST) for jobs and computed folders and drops `<item>/batch-control/activation` without a redirect; the run-request and computed-folder activation actions lose `StaplerProxy`. The rows assert: `<job>/batch-control/` with the D-60 pre-fill unchanged; the new form and submission answer an allowed user (GET followed through redirects, POST not followed); every activation link on the job page answers 200; the old URL answers 404 to the allowed user on GET and POST (redirects not followed, so a 3xx also fails) and stores nothing; 404 for a user without Request and for one who cannot read the item. The crumb is fetched over HTTP as the logged-in user, because `createCrumbedUrl` computes it on the test thread and a real Jenkins rejects it (403 "No valid crumb"). The first version (old URLs, before D-64) was green against 39f4bad. The existing rows that used the old URL now use the new one, with no assertion changed otherwise: ActivationFixtures (`submitActivation`), ActivationRequestTest T-06a-16/21/22, ActivationBreadcrumbTest T-UI-22/24, ActivationScreenTest T-06a-38 and its helper (the job page's link must contain `batch-control-activation`), plus Javadoc in ActivationComputedFolderTest.

221. **One source for pending counts (T-UI-73..77, #76, D-61).** API from the coordinator and `javap -public` on core-dev 5f40f4d: `countPendingFor(Authentication)` on RunRequestService, GrantRequestService and ActivationService returning `model.PendingCount` (`getAwaitingDecision`, `getOwn`, `getCount`, `isEmpty`, `NONE`), plus `ActivationService#listAwaitingDecision(Authentication)`. Rows use users who are only requester or only approver, so how `getCount()` combines both numbers is not pinned; `isDecisions()` is not asserted. "The badge shows the same number" is asserted per tab (requests, grants, activations) with the T-UI-44 badge reader: badge text = `getCount()`, no badge for 0. Losing Approve is modelled by replacing the strategy after designation (designation itself may require Approve). Green against 5f40f4d with ui-dev's uncommitted SectionTabs/ActivationsSection change in the working tree.

222. **Ids.** T-UI-70..77 and T-02-120 are taken out of sequence so that parallel backlog worktrees, which add rows from T-UI-56 and T-02-111 upward, do not collide.

223. **role-strategy minimum in the manifest (T-02-120/121, #78).** What is proven: the manifest Jenkins reads for the plugin under test declares role-strategy as an optional dependency with a minimum of 918 or newer, and the running Jenkins parsed it that way. The test manifest `the.hpl` is used because surefire runs before `package`, so `target/*.hpi` does not exist yet; maven-hpi-plugin builds both manifests from the same POM data, but the `.hpi` manifest itself is not read. The minimum is compared rather than pinned to one string because the scheduled role-strategy-latest build (#77) raises `role-strategy.version`. D-61 is now cited by the tab bar, badge and context-menu rows T-UI-40..46 (doc only); T-UI-47 (pager caption) is not a D-61 row and is left as it was.

224. **Jenkins refuses Batch Control next to role-strategy 898 (T-02-122, #78).** Proven locally with the 898 hpi copied by hand to `target/test-classes/old-plugins/role-strategy.hpi`: Jenkins boots, role-strategy 898 is active, and batch-control is listed under the plugin manager's failed plugins (not under `getPlugins()`) with "Update required: Role-based Authorization Strategy (role-strategy 898.vc050ed2424ca_) to be updated to 918.v91e5468d8db_2 or higher". Without that file the row is skipped by an assumption, never passed; it becomes a CI check only once the build copies `org.jenkins-ci.plugins:role-strategy:898.vc050ed2424ca_:hpi` to that path (request to release-manager). The class references no Batch Control or role-strategy type, because its step runs in a Jenkins where Batch Control is not loaded.

230. **D-69 (no load-time migration).** T-03-21 (MultiApproverLegacyLoadTest, the single-`approver` to set conversion) is withdrawn and its test removed; T-03-07 no longer asserts the compatibility `getApprover()` value, which SPEC 3 no longer names. Other tests still call `RunRequest#getApprover()` on requests created by the current plugin (RunRequestServiceTest, StoreDurabilityTest, OwnerScenario*); they do not test a conversion and are unchanged.

231. **UUID identifiers (T-08-90..95, D-68).** "Canonical" is asserted as `UUID.fromString(id).toString().equals(id)` (36 characters, lower case); the UUID version is not pinned. Earlier-format records are made from records the current plugin wrote: every UUID is replaced by an id of the form `yyyyMMdd-HHmmss-<6 chars>` (ARCHITECTURE 5) in the content and names of all files under `batch-control/` between two sessions, so references between files stay consistent and the startup index sees only the earlier ids. Each restart row asserts the replaced UUID no longer resolves, so a 200 comes from the earlier-format record. The window URL `grants/active/<id>/` is followed through redirects; an unknown window id must answer >= 400.

232. **R4-4 (notice cache keyed by request id).** T-05-36..39 are unchanged; T-05-90 adds the reverse direction (losing Item/Build), which a cache shared between requests or not dropped on save would hide.

233. *Withdrawn by D-71 (2026-10-05); rows T-08-100..111 rewritten, see note 260.* **FOLDER_ONLY scope (T-08-100..108, D-65).** Written from SPEC 8 and D-65 with the owner's rulings: CREATE only directly in the folder, DELETE only on direct non-folder items (not on a nested folder, a multibranch project in the folder or the folder itself; a move of a nested folder out is therefore refused, T-08-109..111), CONFIGURE of a nested folder itself allowed (it is an item whose parent is the folder). Configure/Delete are asserted both as the item's ACL answer and, for jobs, as the HTTP result (config.xml, `doDelete`). Each FOLDER_ONLY row has a FOLDER guard so it cannot pass because windows never confer. The grants form's FOLDER_ONLY option (rendering) is not asserted; T-08-105 asserts the POST binding.

234. **T-04-08/T-04-10 under D-68.** The rows required request ids in the timestamp form carrying the plugin clock's time. D-68 replaced that for requests and windows, so they now assert a canonical UUID (T-04-08: under each non-ASCII-digit locale; T-04-10: plus `createdAt` equal to the plugin clock's instant, the time a request is ordered by). Change record ids keep the timestamp form and their assertions are unchanged. No other row or test asserted the conversions D-69 removed (single `from`/`to` of an approver change, inline diff of a change record, grants without `grantRequestId`).

235. **caffeine-api is required (R4-2).** The requester-build cache uses caffeine-api as a required plugin dependency, so T-02-86's kept set (`OptionalDependencyFixtures.REQUIRED`) names it; without it batch-control itself cannot load. The row still omits every optional plugin, the six compile-time optional ones (file-parameters included since D-74, note 271) among them.

236. **role-strategy 927 minimum (D-35g).** Decision-driven rewrites, not loosenings: 927's Assign Roles page calls `checkSidName` and the strategy endpoints (`assignRole`/`assignUserRole`/`assignGroupRole`, `unassign*`, `deleteSid`/`deleteUser`/`deleteGroup`) instead of 918's `checkName`, `checkForWhitespace` and `manage/role-strategy/assignSubmit`. T-02-46 and T-SEC-52 now probe `checkSidName` and `checkPattern` (the variant still answers 403 to Overall/Read and refuses GET); T-02-94 drives the 927 endpoints and keeps the "class stays Batch Control" assertion and its plain-strategy guard; T-02-98's known members are `clazz`, `checkPattern`, `checkSidName`; T-02-106 (`checkName`) is withdrawn. T-02-120..122 now require 927 (918 is a guard below it; the 898 fixture is still too old).

240. **Overview counts and dashboard bound (T-UI-90..92, D-67).** D-67 removed the #88 count table and the pending banner, so T-UI-56 (which demanded the table) is withdrawn rather than loosened and its test method replaced by T-UI-90. T-UI-90 uses distinctive counts (7, 5, 4, total 16) so the banner check cannot match unrelated text, and it keeps the badges as the positive guard. The dashboard rows count a run as shown when its job name is in the visible body text (tab bar, select, datalist, script excluded), so a job filter listing every job does not count. "Links to History for the rest" is read as: the left-out runs are reachable from the dashboard's History link, History's own paging included. Red on bec34ba (banner text "7 run requests are awaiting your decision", no History link from the dashboard).

241. **model-link (T-UI-93/94, R4-11).** A job/run link is a body anchor whose path is exactly the job or the build. On bec34ba the dashboard's run link had no class (red), and the request list offered no job link at all, so the list is checked only for the links it does offer (SPEC does not pin the list's columns, note 27).

245. **List layout (T-UI-95/96, D-66).** Rows are found by the id in their link and ordered by document order of `#main-panel` links outside the tab bar, so neither section captions nor markup are pinned. The active window may link by its request id or its window id. "Not the first thing" is read as: a grant request form, if still on the page, comes after the pending row. Red on bec34ba (the form preceded the lists).

246. **Revoke from the detail page (T-UI-97, D-66, R4-12).** The control is found by its endpoint (a path ending in `/revoke`, in href, action, formaction or a data attribute) and posted with a crumb. The permission rule is the list's (Manage; GrantWebTest). The confirmation before revoking is browser behaviour (a dialog) and is left to e2e. Red on bec34ba (the detail page offered no revoke).

247. **Request dialogs (T-UI-98..100, D-66, R4-9, R4-14).** HtmlUnit runs without JavaScript, so the rows test the server side of the dialogs: an entry is any element outside the tab bar whose href or data attribute names a same-instance URL, and the page offers an entry when that URL renders the request form posting to the existing endpoint. A submission must redirect to the new request's detail page. That the dialog opens on the current page and follows the redirect is left to e2e. On bec34ba T-UI-98 was red (no entry on the grants page and no folder entry); T-UI-99 and T-UI-100 were already green (the Request Run link and the redirects existed), and stay as guards for D-66 and D-60.

248. **Existing rows adapted to D-66.** D-66 moved the grant request form off the grants list page to `grants/new` (the content of a dialog); ui-dev named the public surface, so the rows now pin it. T-UI-10/15: the entry resolves to `grants/new?scopeFullName=<encoded name>`; context path, encoding and the prefilled form after following it are unchanged. T-UI-13/14: the prefill and the no-reflection checks run on `grants/new`; the blank-form guard opens `grants/new` without a query. T-UI-26: the grants page carries no request form and offers `[data-batch-control-request=grant]`; on `grants/new` a list table is no longer a premise, and if one is there the form and the "240" refusal still precede it. T-08-49: the re-request entry may be a dialog button (target from a data-* URL); the expired row is matched on normalized text, because the new cells have no whitespace between them and the raw text glued "Expired" to its neighbours. None of these drops a behaviour D-66 kept.

249. **D-66 public surface (T-UI-101..105, ui-dev dac5094).** Lists `table[data-batch-control-list=pending|active|ended]` with the paging parameters `pendingPage/activePage/endedPage`, the activations marker `small[data-batch-control-awaiting]`, the fragments `job/<j>/batch-control/dialog` and `grants/dialog`, `dialog=true` submissions (400 re-render, redirect on success), the redirect of the former `grants/?scopeFullName=` link, and `POST grants/<id>/revoke` (T-UI-97). An approved activation may be listed as active rather than ended, so T-UI-96 accepts either for it. SPEC does not say whether an approver who is not designated sees a pending activation, so T-UI-103 only requires that a2 has no marked row. Red on bec34ba: T-UI-95..98, 101..104 and the adapted T-UI-10/13/14/15/26; T-UI-99, 100 and 105 were already green there and are guards.

250. **Filter forms keep the crumb out of the URL (T-UI-106, e2e-12 DEF-07).** No SPEC acceptance line covers the URL of a GET filter form, hence a T-UI row; the crumb in a URL leaks into history, bookmarks, logs and the Referer. The defect comes from core's `hudson-behavior.js`, so the web client runs with JavaScript on (a client without JavaScript could not reproduce it). Forms are found by their submit caption ("Filter", "Show"); the Changes/Incidents month field is found by `type=month` or a name containing "month", and its name is read from the page, not pinned. Each page also has to navigate and keep the value, so a form that drops the filter cannot pass.

251. **Unlinked ids are shown as text (T-UI-107..109, UX review 2026-10-04 UX-1, regression of the e2e-11 DEF-05 fix).** SPEC 2 allows a link only to a user who may open its target; the id itself must still be visible, so an id cell is never empty. Rows are found by content (job or scope name), never by caption or column. "Shown as text" accepts the full id in the row text, or a short form (at least the first 8 characters) on an element whose `title` or `data-batch-control-id` holds the full id, so a DEF-05 style short display passes. SPEC offers no user path to a window whose request the viewer cannot open: window and request share one id and one visibility (requester, designated approvers, Manage), and retention keeps a closed grant request as long as its grant file is kept (measured: deleting the request by retention while the grant with `changedItems` stays was attempted and the request file stayed). T-UI-109 therefore removes the `requests/grant/<id>.xml` files (ARCHITECTURE 5) to obtain windows with no linkable request; both detail URLs then answer >= 400. Red on 559c0df (all three cells empty: dashboard and History Requests empty cells, Active list empty ID cell), green on 729e7a7.
252. **The activation page follows the job page layout of its sibling (T-UI-110/111, e2e-14 DEF-08).** No SPEC acceptance line pins the chrome of the activation form, hence T-UI rows; SPEC 6a gives the page and 6 the Request Run sibling. e2e-14 found that a user with core's new job page on got the job's classic side panel on `batch-control-activation/`, with core's URL-less new-job-page actions rendered as dead `a.task-link` entries (`href=""`: a second "Delete Project", "Permalinks"), while `batch-control/` renders no side panel for that user. The job UI is chosen per user through core's `UserExperimentalFlagsProperty` (`new-job-page.flag` `true`/`false`), not the global default, so both UIs run in one Jenkins. Each row asserts the same layout on Request Run first, so the activation page is held to its sibling and a change to the sibling shows up as a reference failure, not a silent pass. The page is read without JavaScript (the side panel and the app bar are server-rendered). T-UI-111 is a guard (classic was already correct). Red on a12e7ee (T-UI-110: `#side-panel` present on the activation page; T-UI-111 passes), green on dde0aa4.

260. **One-item permission windows (D-71, replaces D-65): T-08-100..127 and the rewrites listed here.** Decision-driven rewrite, not a loosening: D-71 replaces the scope types JOB, FOLDER and FOLDER_ONLY with ITEM; a window names exactly one item and confers nothing on any other. (a) *D-65 rows:* T-08-100..111 keep their ids with D-71 content (note 233 withdrawn): CONFIGURE on a folder covers the folder only (T-08-100), on a job that job only (T-08-101), CREATE directly in the folder only (T-08-102/103), the delete veto for a folder window's holder (T-08-107), DELETE on a job only (T-08-109), refusals at submission (T-08-104/108/110), the form binding without scope type (T-08-105), the restart (T-08-106) and the move of a folder (T-08-111). T-08-108 asserted the opposite of what it now asserts (a FOLDER DELETE window deleted a nested folder); D-71 withdraws that intent, so the row asserts the refusal and moves from P1 to P0, since it is what stops a window from deleting a folder's children as SYSTEM. (b) *New rows* T-08-112..127: D-35c as amended (T-08-112), CREATE on computed folders (T-08-113), DELETE on a multi-configuration project (T-08-114), the item kind (T-08-115..117), the screens (T-08-118..122, 124), the mail (T-08-123), the enum (T-08-125), an earlier scope type not converted (T-08-126) and a sub-item of a job (T-08-127). T-08-128 (a move into the Jenkins root) and T-08-129 (approval message parity) follow in note 261. (c) *Rewritten existing rows.* Where only the fixture named JOB or FOLDER, the window now names the same item (about 45 test files; `ApproverFormFixtures.submitGrant(Ok)` and `StrategyFixtures.grant` lost their scope type argument, the form posts no `scopeType`). Where the intent rested on a FOLDER window reaching items inside the folder, the row now asserts the opposite (refused) instead of being deleted: T-08-11 (a pre-existing child 403), T-02-12 (a folder window does not reach `f/job`), T-02-24 (window on `team/sub`, not on its job), T-02-38 (the save of `S/F/j` 403; the guard measured on `S` itself), T-02-39 (no Create in `S/F`; the positive twin moved to `S/mine`), T-SEC-03 (children out of scope), T-UI-98 (no scope type control), T-SEC-72 (prefill for the item, never the source folder). Where a fixture requested DELETE on a folder (now refused at submission), DELETE moved to the job and, where the old fixture was the point, the refusal is asserted first: T-SEC-54 (the [CREATE, DELETE] request on `team` refused, then a Delete window on another job does not cover the source), T-SEC-58 and T-09-24 (DELETE window on `prod/x`), T-08-42 (the request refused, then a window on `team/legacy-job`), T-SEC-36/39 (CREATE on `team` plus DELETE on `team/legacy`, core's Create+Delete rename branch for a user without Configure on the item; no row claims that every rename needs two windows, since Configure on the item suffices in core's other branch), T-08-50 and T-13-20 ([CREATE, CONFIGURE]). Where a copy relied on the folder window's CONFIGURE to read the source (Extended Read), a CONFIGURE window on the source was added: T-08-44, T-SEC-40. T-RT-06 measures the per-write expiry under four job windows granted at the same instant. T-UI-10/15 accept, besides `scopeFullName`, only `actions=CONFIGURE` (the frozen prefill URL format) and never `scopeType`. The self-grant guard rows (T-02-62/67/72, D-58a/b) are unchanged in intent: D-71 leaves the guard of what is below a guarded folder as it was. (d) *How it is measured.* A refusal at submission is IllegalArgumentException from `GrantRequestService#create` and, from the browser form, 4xx with the grant request form shown again and the typed reason kept (the wording is not pinned); approval of a request whose item is gone or of another kind is IllegalStateException and leaves it PENDING with no window, while an empty scope stays IllegalArgumentException (T-SEC-12/17, unchanged). The check endpoint is POSTed with the name as both `value` and `scopeFullName`; its FormValidation answer is read through `class=ok|error` and its decoded text, and a missing and an invisible item must give the same answer once the name is masked. The kind element is found by `data-batch-control-item-kind`; its display name may be text, `title`, `tooltip`, `data-html-tooltip` or `aria-label`, and it must sit in the row naming the full name. T-08-124 reads the prefill URL from an anchor or from the refusal's text. T-08-126 makes the earlier-type file from one the plugin wrote by replacing its single ITEM value (element or attribute), and asserts only that it confers nothing, not how the loader skips it. (e) *Test dependencies.* workflow-job, workflow-multibranch, cloudbees-folder and, transitively, matrix-project and branch-api (organization folders) are on the test classpath; the Maven plugin is not, so Maven modules (T-08-127) and Maven projects (T-08-114) are not tested. (f) *Ids.* Note 260 leaves 253..259 to parallel lanes. (g) *Red for the right reason.* In a scratch copy run against the pre-D-71 build, with ITEM mapped to JOB or FOLDER, the job-scoped rows pass (T-08-101, T-08-109, T-08-114, T-RT-06), the folder rows fail exactly at their D-71 assertions (T-08-100/102/103/112: children or the nested folder still covered under FOLDER), T-08-127 fails at the service refusal and T-08-117 at the exception type (IllegalArgumentException before D-71).

261. **Root move refusal and approval message parity (T-08-128/129, D-59, D-71).** Follow-ups to note 260, written from SPEC 8 (the D-59 move line: "a refused move changes nothing, answers with a plain message naming what is missing and is recorded as GRANT_VIOLATION"; the D-71 line: CREATE applies only to a regular folder) and SPEC 2 (a hidden item is not disclosed, the T-08-120 rule). (a) *T-08-128.* The Jenkins root is not an item a window can name, so no window can give Create there: the refusal of a move into the root must not offer one. It is measured on both answers (browser page and scripted body): `administrator` must appear (the move needs one), `create` must appear (what is missing), and no suggestion to request a Create window may appear; the suggestion is a "request / ask for / apply for (a) (new) Create" or "... (permission) window ... Create" phrase not preceded by "not", "cannot", "can't" or "never", so a sentence that explains why no window applies passes. Every `a[href]` and `form[action]` of the page and the text of both answers must not contain `grants/new` (T-08-124's prefill URL, by href or text). The row keeps T-SEC-64's item link allowed. The folders plugin names the root destination `/` (`"/" + fullName`); the administrator guard proves that value is accepted, so the 403 cannot come from a malformed destination, and u1's move into `team` proves the DELETE window does cover the source. *Observation, not pinned:* the scripted refusal repeated within seconds of the browser refusal (same user, item and destination) added no second GRANT_VIOLATION (also with a 2 s gap and in the reverse order); SPEC names a one-minute merge only for a person's refused re-runs (D-51), so the row pins one record for the first refusal and leaves the repeat's count to the human (reported). (b) *T-08-129.* D-71 refuses approval when the item is gone (IllegalStateException, T-08-117) and P-10 when the approver cannot see it (IllegalArgumentException, T-SEC-18); the service keeps the types apart, and the row asserts both again in the same fixture as a guard. On the web page the approver must not learn which of the two applies. The two requests are symmetric (same kind, reason, duration, approver; only the item name and id differ), so the answers are compared after masking the item name, the request id and every digit (times). The message is isolated as the answer's text lines that are not on the request's detail page a1 opened just before, so it is found whether the refusal is shown on the detail page or on a page of its own; the whole main panel must be equal too, so no other part of the page leaks existence. The wording is not pinned. (c) *Red for the right reason.* In a scratch copy of the commit before the fix (`d2bba0a`), T-08-128 fails at the suggestion assertion (the refusal said "Request a permission window for Create in the Jenkins root, or ask an administrator", so `administrator` alone would not have caught it; that page had no `grants/new` link, so the link assertions are guards), and T-08-129 fails at the service type guard (IllegalStateException for the invisible item). Its web comparison passed there too: the parity assertion is a regression pin against the new type distinction reaching the page, not a reproduction of an earlier leak.

262. **D-71a identity binding, window-only folder renames and the spec-review-S6 gaps (T-08-130..147, T-UI-112; T-UI-10/15 tightened).** Written from SPEC 8 lines 167-171 (D-71, D-71a, the D-73 clause), the Given/When/Then of security-34 S-34-01..04 and spec-review-S6 M-1, M-2, m-1, m-2, m-4 and m-5. (a) *Rows by source.* S-34-01: T-08-130 (matrix strategy; Probe A's first step, the window-only rename of the folder `sandbox`, is refused with one GRANT_VIOLATION), T-08-131 (identity binding: the administrator performs the probe's renames and no window reaches the job or folder that now carries a window's name, nor follows its own item), T-08-132 (role-strategy: item role `sandbox.*` plus one window on `ops`, the rename of `ops` to `sandbox2` refused), T-08-133 (guards: the administrator and a standing Configure holder rename folders). S-34-03: T-08-135 (a Folder replaces the window's Freestyle job), T-08-136 (a new job of the same kind). S-34-04: T-08-137 (`ops/` and `OPS` stored as `ops`, and the window then confers; SPEC pins storing, so a refusal next to the field would fail the row). S-34-02: T-08-138. M-1: T-08-139 (the form's item check) and T-08-140 (lists and detail page; T-08-122 is unchanged). M-2: T-08-141 (a DELETE window after its job is replaced by a created or a moved-in folder), T-08-142 (a CREATE window after its folder is replaced by a job or a multibranch project). m-1: T-08-134 (a pre-existing job renamed through its CONFIGURE window) with T-08-130 (the folder half, refused since D-71a). m-2: T-08-143 (delete veto for a folder and a multibranch project), T-08-144 (folder move into a regular folder; the root is T-08-128). m-4: T-08-145. m-5: T-UI-10/15 (job entry) and T-UI-112 (folder entry). The coverage inventory item "a window does not follow a rename or move of its item" is T-08-146; SPEC 169's "D-73 coalescing applies" is T-08-147. (b) *T-UI-10/15 reversal.* Note 260 let the job entry carry `actions=CONFIGURE` besides `scopeFullName`. spec-review-S6 m-5 found no decision behind that allowance (note 194's e2e-06 DEF-01 guard needs one parameter), so note 262 withdraws it: the entry's href must equal `<root>batch-control/grants/new?scopeFullName=<rawEncoded>` exactly, and a URL in a data-* attribute of the entry must equal that or `<root>batch-control/grants/dialog?scopeFullName=<rawEncoded>` exactly. T-UI-112 applies the same exactness to the folder entry (which had no exact row; its URL may be either form). This restores the note 194 guarantee; no row was loosened. (c) *How it is measured.* What a window confers is read from the item's own ACL (`hasPermission2` for the holder) and from HTTP (config.xml 200/403, `doDelete`, `confirmRename`), never from `GrantService#hasActiveGrant(user, fullName, ...)`, which takes a name only, the thing D-71a stops trusting. Renames use core's `POST <item>/confirmRename` with `newName`, redirects not followed (success is 302); a refused rename is any 4xx; a GRANT_VIOLATION is counted in the current month and must name the user and the item in its target or detail (wording not pinned). D-73 for renames is read as for moves: the same user, item and new name within a minute merge, another item writes its own record. Deletions, re-creations and the T-08-141 move are SYSTEM fixtures (the administrator's act); the administrator's renames and move in T-08-131/133/146 go through HTTP. T-08-138 finds the notice by the ui-dev marker `data-batch-control-notice="group-configure"`; its text must contain one of inside/within/contain/below/beneath/under and, for the multibranch project and the organization folder, "creat" and "delet"; the wording is otherwise free, and SPEC does not say whether the requester sees it, so only the designated approver is asserted. T-08-139 takes the first `<svg` of the FormValidation answer, requires no visible text before it, strips every svg (a `<title>` inside is not text) and compares the rest exactly; an `img` does not count, because a spacer `img` in validation answers would satisfy it; the three kinds' icons are symbols (`symbol-folder-outline`, `symbol-freestyle-project`, `symbol-pipeline`), which render as svg. The hostile name is the MoveRefusalPageTest one; the answer is parsed as HTML and no element may carry an attribute from it, since a markup answer (`okWithMarkup`) must escape the name itself. T-08-143/144 read the refusal in the main panel when there is one (the side panel and breadcrumbs belong to the item, as in T-SEC-64/72) and each has a job twin that must reference `grants/new?scopeFullName=<job>`, which shows that the scan finds a link when one is offered. T-08-145 makes each earlier-type request file from one the plugin wrote, replacing its single ITEM value (as T-08-126), and approves through HTTP, so no exception type is pinned. T-08-142 asserts the ACL only: neither a job nor a multibranch project offers a creation endpoint, and branch-api's `createItem` answers 500 (UnsupportedOperationException from `BaseEmptyView`) to everyone, the administrator included, so an HTTP attempt measures branch-api, not the window; the administrator's Create on the same ACL is the guard. (d) *Red at commit time* (this worktree, D-71a core and ui work not merged): T-08-130, T-08-132, T-08-147 (the window-only folder rename answers 302), T-08-131, T-08-135, T-08-136 (windows still match by name), T-08-137 (the request stores `ops/`), T-08-138 (no notice element), T-08-139 (the check answers `<div class="ok">Folder &#039;team&#039;</div>`), T-08-145 (an earlier-type request loads with a null scope type and is approved: the log shows `Grant ... created for user 'u2' on null:ops`; SPEC's "not converted" is read, as the coordinator specified, as "cannot be approved and confers nothing"). Green already, and kept as regression pins: T-08-133, T-08-134, T-08-140, T-08-141, T-08-142, T-08-143, T-08-144, T-08-146, T-UI-10, T-UI-15, T-UI-112 (the check-time kind rules, the list icons and the no-window refusal pages came with D-71 untested; a renamed or moved item already loses its window because its name changes). (e) *For core-dev, not pinned.* T-08-136 re-creates a job under the same name and kind at once; if the identity were a file-system key that a file system reuses after a deletion, the row could pass or fail by chance on another platform. The row asserts SPEC's result only.

263. **D-72a rerun fallback link, refused-build disposal and the D-72 form surface (T-05-65..69, T-11-13..20, T-UI-113..118).** Written from SPEC item 11 (the D-72a sentence), item 5 (the D-72 disposal and body-cap lines), item 6 (D-60: nothing is queued or stored until the requester submits the form), section 6 (usability, CSRF, secrets), DECISIONS D-60, D-72 and D-72a, LIMITATIONS items 16, 32 and 48 (32 as amended in 10cf566: the channels whose refused files are disposed of, and the refused re-runs left alone; citations corrected from 31 and 49 in note 265, spec-review-S7 m-9), the coordinator's frozen D-72 contract and the surface ui-dev documented (68f52c3 and b7ce183 commit messages and report, relayed by the coordinator); no src/main knowledge. *Rerun link:* the reference travels as `fromRerun` in the form URL, in the form's hidden field and in the form's action query. The positive paths (T-11-13, T-11-19 and every guard) use the form exactly as rendered, so they depend on ui-dev's wiring. Every crafted reference is forced into the submitted form (or into its action query, T-11-20, keeping the rest of that query, the crumb included), so the server's re-validation at submission is what is measured, whatever the page rendered; the rendered page is checked separately (no `fromRerun` field and no "will be linked" text for a reference that is not linkable). "No error" is pinned as the submission being accepted (< 400) and creating exactly one unlinked request. T-11-17's `viewer` case (ViewHistory without Request) follows D-72a "the same rights as the rerun button" and SPEC 5 (the rerun needs Request, Item/Read and ViewHistory). T-11-18's vanished incident is made by deleting `incidents/<id>.xml` (ARCHITECTURE 5), with the premise that it no longer loads. The traversal check only looks for `x`/`x.xml` in the store root. The coordinator's first relay said the field is absent after a 413; the latest says ui-dev now carries the validated reference in the action query so that it survives a 413; T-11-19 follows the latest. *Refused-build disposal:* SPEC's disposal line speaks of requests; for a refused build the rows rest on D-60 (nothing stored before the requester submits) and D-72 (Batch Control leaves no file content behind), with LIMITATIONS 32 naming the channels. Every refusal row first proves its detector on an uncontrolled twin tied to a label no node has: the same submission there is queued and leaves new files under the documented directories (both directories for the form, `buildWithParameters` and the two token channels; the core directory for the CLI, whose stdin file is a core `file` value), then the twin's item is cancelled by task (cancelling the looked-up item object raced with the queue moving it from waiting to buildable; seen once). "Nothing new" is the before/after difference under both directories. T-05-69 guards the re-run exclusion: the source build's copy under its build directory stays byte-identical, and at least one MARKER_REUSE_BLOCKED or TRIGGER_BLOCKED record shows the gate saw the attempts. The re-runs and unattended submissions LIMITATIONS 32 says are left alone (a rebuild parameters page uploading a new file, parameterized-trigger) are not asserted either way. *Form surface:* wording is not pinned except the substrings ui-dev declared stable (`will be linked to incident`; the earlier "is not linked to the incident" must be gone) and "select the file(s) again" (LIMITATIONS 48). The 413 size message is a line the 413 answer adds to the plain form (or to the dialog fragment) that matches a size word. Page and dialog re-renders are told apart by `dialog=true` in the re-rendered form's action (68f52c3: the dialog is recognised by `?dialog=true` in its action, never by a body field). The 400 re-render must not carry the typed password even encrypted (no `{...}` value that decrypts to it); BATCH_DAY kept follows the usability line. T-UI-118 is the positive twin of T-05-64; JenkinsRule's `addCrumb` adds a body field, so the header crumb is built from the crumb issuer. *Baseline:* on 763f994 (this branch) the disposal rows, T-11-17, T-11-18 and T-UI-113/114/116/117/118 pass; T-11-13..16, T-11-19, T-11-20 and T-UI-115 fail on the link or its notice (the form wiring is ui-dev's b7ce183, not on this branch). On b7ce183 (scratch worktree, the tests copied, nothing committed there) every new row passes except T-11-19 (the action-query carry is still in progress). On e0c7dbf, before the disposal fix, T-05-65..68 fail with the submission's uploads left under `fileParameterValueFiles` and T-05-69 passes (guard). *Gaps:* "the approved run could not be queued" had no row here (note 267; rows added by note 265); the D-70 dialog opening on the new job page and its JavaScript are left to e2e; whether a crafted reference still shows a generic rerun notice is not asserted (only that nothing promises a link); a valid reference sent together with a different one in the action query is not asserted (SPEC is silent on precedence). *Ids:* T-UI-112 is taken by the D-71 lane, and that lane also used notes 267-262, so this batch is note 263.

264. **D-71b event unbinding and the unbound window display (T-08-148..155; T-08-138 tightened).** Written from SPEC 8 line 169 (D-71a), D-71b, ARCHITECTURE 4 (the binding paragraph) and 5 (`itemIdentity`: absent, the grant is bound to nothing; cleared when an item event ends the binding), SPEC 8 lines 157 and 172 (revocation by a Manage holder, from the list and from the detail page) and the ui-dev screen contract (the Active list's Remaining cell and the detail page's State cell carry `data-batch-control-window-state="bound"` or `"unbound"`, the latter reading exactly "No longer applies (the item was renamed, moved or deleted)"; an ended window has no marker; Revoke stays offered for unbound windows; the folder rename refusal's field check and page wording). Note 263 is left to a parallel lane. (a) *Rows by D-71b clause.* Deleting an item unbinds the windows naming it or anything below it: T-08-148 (a folder, a job in it and a job in a nested folder; `fold-sibling` is the prefix guard, so an implementation that unbinds by string prefix instead of by path segment fails). A rename or move ends the windows on the old name and renaming back does not restore them: T-08-149 (rename and rename back), T-08-152 (move and move back). Creating or copying an item unbinds windows bound under its name: T-08-150; and drops stale D-35c records under that name: T-08-155. At startup, windows whose item no longer exists are unbound: T-08-151. Revoking an unbound window: T-08-153. The folder rename refusal's screens: T-08-154. The clause "unbinds any window still bound under the new name" has no row: a rename or move needs the new name to be free and deletion already unbinds, so no state reachable through Jenkins leaves a window bound under a free name; D-71b's stated remaining gap (a directory replaced on disk followed by a reload) needs file-system access and is not tested. (b) *How it is measured.* Each event row measures three results: what the window confers (the item's own ACL, an HTTP config.xml save, never a name-based service query, as note 262), the screens (`WindowStateFixtures`: the Active list row is the one linking to `batch-control/grants/<id>/`, and the detail page is that URL; each must carry exactly one state marker; unbound must read exactly the documented text; bound must show minutes left in the list and "Open, ... left" on the page; an ended window has no Active list row and no marker; a page without an Active table, "No active grants.", has no row), and the stored grant (`batch-control/grants/<id>.xml` holds an `itemIdentity` element with content at approval, a premise, and none after the event). Every event row keeps an untouched window (`keep`, or `ops/c` at startup) as its guard: shown bound, stored bound, still conferring. T-08-149 and T-08-152 assert as a premise that the item is the same object and that its directory keeps its file key (where the platform reports one): an implementation matching name and identity alone would confer again there, so only the event ends the window. Events are the administrator's acts through HTTP (`doDelete`, `confirmRename`, `move/move`, `createItem`), except the re-creations in T-08-148 and T-08-151 (SYSTEM fixtures) and the deletion while Jenkins is down (the item directories removed between two JenkinsSessionExtension steps). T-08-153 revokes as the administrator (Manage); the approver a1 is the 403 guard, as in T-UI-97, because SPEC 157 gives revocation to Manage holders only. T-08-154 reads the field check by GET (as core's rename page does) and the browser page; the GRANT_VIOLATION of the same refused POST is T-08-130's and is not repeated, and whether the field check itself records anything is not pinned. T-08-138's added sentence is matched as a negated "renam" phrase (does not allow / cannot / never ... renam) plus "administrator"; the wording is otherwise free. (c) *Red and green.* All green on 813aa90. In a scratch copy of 8fad604 (the D-71a core work, before the ui commit) T-08-148..153 and T-08-151 fail at their first display assertion (no marker); with the display helpers stubbed (scratch only) every permission and stored-binding assertion passes there, so the event unbinding came with the D-71a core work and those halves are regression pins whose red was not reproduced (no commit binds by identity without events; the file key premise is the falsifiability argument). T-08-154 is green on 8fad604 too (a pin). T-08-138 fails on debcef1 exactly at the new sentence (the notice then had two sentences). No assertion was loosened.

265. **D-72b hardening of typed parameter values (T-05-70..89, T-05-91..97, T-11-21..24; T-05-44 adjusted; six "approved, never queued" fixtures replaced; notes 267 and 263 corrected).** Written from SPEC item 5 (the D-72b line and the D-72 lines), items 1, 4, 7 and 11, section 6, DECISIONS D-72, D-72a and D-72b, ARCHITECTURE sections 2 and 5, and the Given/When/Then of security-35 (S-35-01..07) and spec-review-S7 (M-1, M-2, m-1, m-2, m-3/O-1, m-4, m-9, m-10, m-11); the file:line references in those reports were not used, and no src/main knowledge. *Field error:* HTTP 400, an HTML page not titled "Error", no crash text, the form again (T-05-18, T-UI-117), and an explanation that the plain form does not have (re-entry notices excluded) which names the field or sits in the field's own parameter block, or an `X-Error` header naming it (T-UI-07 precedent); wording is not pinned. *Channels:* the repeated name is refused on core's `json` field (as the rendered form posts), on multipart `json` whose file entries name their parts (core's form convention), on raw url-encoded fields, and in the service. A submission carrying a name once in `json` and once as a raw field is not asserted (the request then holds one value). *Service exceptions:* a repeated name throws `IllegalArgumentException` (security-35's fix direction, relayed as the contract); over-long and XML-illegal values throw `IllegalArgumentException` or `Failure` (as T-05-49). Temporary files made by a service caller's own value objects are the caller's and are not asserted. *Nothing stored* is the run request ids plus the whole `requests/run/` listing (any name, so a leftover `.tmp` is caught), plus the two temporary directories for form rows. *XML:* U+0000 on the form and in the service, U+FFFF in the service; both are illegal in XML 1.0 and 1.1. U+0001..U+001F are not asserted (storable as character references in XML 1.1, which Jenkins writes; ambiguous). *Length:* D-72b (2) "every stored value, secrets included": a Password value and the test's Secret-carrying type (`CustomParameterFixtures.TokenParameterValue`, masked) are refused at 10,001 characters and accepted at 10,000; `base64File` content is not limited (D-72b alternatives: not chosen). *Stored values that do not match:* `requests/run/<id>.xml` is edited on disk (ARCHITECTURE 5) and each row first proves that the plugin reads the edit (a marker appended to the stored reason is read back). Refusal is pinned as: after the service call and after the HTTP approve (< 500, no crash text) the request is neither APPROVED nor EXECUTED and nothing is queued; whether the service throws, the request's later state and the message are not pinned. Each row has an unedited twin on the same job that is approved and runs with its own value. Fail closed at submission is pinned through startup recovery (T-05-82), the only path that submits an approved, unqueued request later; build steps of the test do not survive a restart, so that row reads the recovered run's parameters. *Queue refusal (corrects note 267's gap):* `QueueRefusalFixtures` refuses an approved submission either with a test `QueueDecisionHandler` (a nested `@TestExtension` of the test class; core orders equal ordinals by class name, so it is consulted before Batch Control's gate in a sub-package) or with core's `ItemDeletion` veto (consulted after the gate). Each use asserts that the handler was consulted. The ordering is confirmed by the baseline below (before the gate the current code already disposes, after it it does not, as spec-review-S7's probe found); every row holds under either ordering because SPEC asks the same result. While APPROVED and not queued, the request keeps its files and typed values (guards in T-05-85 and T-05-88..92), since SPEC item 4 submits it after a restart and item 5 needs the original values. *Fixture replacement (decision-driven, not a loosening):* T-04-02, T-07-03, T-07-04, T-07-10, T-UI-05 and the approved variant of T-RT-03 reached "approved, not yet submitted" by approving under quiet-down and clearing the queue. Clearing cancels the approved queue item, and D-72b (7) now says such a run is not resubmitted (T-05-87), so the old fixture would make T-04-02 and T-07-04 fail for a reason unrelated to what they pin, and the others depend on how the cancellation is recorded. They now approve while the queue refuses the submission before the gate, which leaves exactly "approved, never queued"; every assertion is unchanged, and all six pass on b138136. *T-05-44:* it asserted after the run that the request file still holds the whole Base64; D-72b (5) removes typed values when the approved run starts, so the "only in the request's own file" check moved before the approval and after the run the Base64 must be nowhere in the store (stricter). *Typed values removed:* no Base64 (first 32 characters) and no `{...}` token that decrypts to the password; the display map is unchanged and the detail page renders it. "When the approved run starts" is read from inside the build by a step that copies the request file (`TypedParameterFixtures.RequestFileSnapshot`). *Listings never load them:* the probe value counts its own XStream `readResolve` (premise: a direct `Jenkins.XSTREAM2` read increments it); the Run Requests list for requester and approver, the overview with its badge (2) and the expiry work with nothing due must leave it at 0. The detail page is not a listing and is not asserted; approval is not used as a guard because a cached object may legitimately be reused. No timing is asserted. *Cancelled queue item (T-05-87):* only "no build, not EXECUTED, its file gone" is pinned, not the request's state; the file also goes through the file-parameters cancellation listener. *Default cap (T-05-94):* a plain socket with an API token (exempt from the crumb), `application/octet-stream`, the body never sent: 104857601 declared answers 413; exactly 104857600 must not be 413 and must be answered without waiting for the body (60-second limit). *Chunked (T-05-95):* premise: the same small body with a declared length is accepted. *Rerun:* T-11-21 accepts a refusal or the form fallback; T-11-22 accepts the fallback (SPEC 11: an unrecoverable value opens the form) or a refusal, and a carried `p.TARGET` must be the incident's own; T-11-24 makes the rerun fail by designating a user not on the approver list. *m-1:* the credentials plugin's parameter value holds a credentials id, not a `Secret`, so the test type stands for "any other `Secret` field". *Citations (m-9, m-11):* note 263 now cites LIMITATIONS 32 (channels) and 48 (files are not carried); T-06-89..96 and RefusedBuildPrefillTest cite D-60/D-72 instead of P-03 (wording only). *Baseline (b138136, before core-dev's and ui-dev's D-72b work):* red on the D-72b behaviour they pin: T-05-70, 71, 73..87, 89, 92, 95 and T-11-21, 22, and the adjusted T-05-44 (the duplicate is stored, the over-long password accepted, U+0000 gives a 500 / RuntimeException, edited files are approved, recovery submits the edited and the cancelled requests, typed values stay in ended files, listings load them 22 times, chunked bodies are refused, a refusal after the gate keeps the files, reruns carry repeated names and the re-created job's build). Green already: T-05-72 (core's simple definitions refuse two raw values and the plugin answers 400 naming TARGET), T-05-88 and T-05-91 (refusal before the gate already disposes), T-05-93, T-05-94, T-05-96, T-05-97, T-11-23 and T-11-24, plus the six replaced fixtures; the guards of the red rows were run separately on b138136 and pass. *Gaps:* a parameterless request in the pre-D-72 shape is not asserted (a parameterless D-72 request may carry no typed values at all, so "cannot be approved" can be read either way); the request's state after a refused approval and after a cancelled queue item, and the messages, are not pinned; the heap and time bound of S-35-02 is covered only by "never loaded"; Stapler's leftover upload directories (S-35-05) are documentation only. *Ids:* T-05-90 was taken, so the T-05 rows run 70..89 and 91..97; the note is 265 by the coordinator's assignment. *T-05-85 premise corrected (after the D-72b implementation; not a loosening):* both requests were approved at T0 and the rename came after the expiry work at T0+61, on the reading that only the rename could end the second request; SPEC item 7 expires every approved, unqueued request past the timeout, so the expiry work had already made it EXPIRED and the rename had nothing to invalidate. The second request is now approved after the clock move (approved-run timeout measured from approval), stays APPROVED through the expiry work with its typed values kept (an added guard), and is then INVALIDATED by the rename; every assertion is kept. *Addendum, security-37 S-37-01 (T-05-98..100):* D-72b (4) judges a body without a declared length by what it parsed; security-37 showed two chunked encodings that the prediction of which parts would be read missed (a file reference given as a JSON number, and `json` sent as a file part after a form-field decoy), so the request kept about 800 KiB against a 64 KiB cap. The rows pin the documented surface relayed by the coordinator: what a request keeps (file contents, decoded Base64 size, stored texts) is held to `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.maxRequestBodyBytes` before anything is stored; the form answers 413 and the service throws `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.policy.RequestTooLargeException` (an `IllegalArgumentException`). The message wording ("The run request was not submitted: its files and parameter values take ...") is not pinned. *Nothing kept* is the run request ids, the whole `requests/run/` listing and the files under `fileParameterValueFiles/` and `stashedFileParameterValueFiles/`; Stapler's own upload directories are not asserted (D-72b (8)). The string-reference control (an over-cap chunked body naming its part, refused 413) is T-05-95 and is not repeated. T-05-98's guard only says that the numeric encoding under the cap is not refused by the cap (accepting or refusing a numeric reference otherwise is not specified); T-05-99 has no under-cap guard, since what a decoy submission does under the cap is not specified. T-05-100 also pins that the cap bounds the sum of the values, not each one (two 36 KiB files). The caller's own value files are not asserted (as above). Run on 3de519a: T-05-98..100 pass with the rest of RequestBodyCapTest (11/11). Not run on the pre-fix commit (T-05-100 needs the new exception type to compile).
