267. **D-72: run requests keep the submitted, typed parameter values (T-05-41..64, T-11-08..12; T-SEC-07 and T-SEC-19 rewritten; note 44 superseded).** Written from SPEC item 5 (the three D-72 lines), item 11 (rerun), section 6 (secrets), ARCHITECTURE sections 2 and 5, DECISIONS D-72 and the coordinator's frozen contract. *Decision-driven rewrite, not a loosening:* T-SEC-07 asserted P-03 option ① (the approved build receives `********`); D-72 supersedes that ruling, so the row now asserts the opposite delivery (exactly the typed secret, as a sensitive `PasswordParameterValue`) while every "no plaintext as text" assertion and its non-sensitive twin stay unchanged. T-SEC-19's logic is unchanged (the run-record path still masks); only its wording cites D-72's textual-form rule instead of P-03. No test referred to LIMITATIONS 16. *Surfaces:* requests are submitted through the job's Request Run form as a browser does (JavaScript on, the file chosen in the parameter's own file control inside core's `<div name="parameter">` block, multipart) where the row is about the form, and through `RunRequestService.create(Job, List<ParameterValue>, String, String)` where it is about the stored value. Approvals go through `RunRequestService.approve`. *File bytes:* contents are an ASCII marker followed by every byte value and are compared byte for byte; core's file is read from the workspace at the parameter's location and from core's copy under the build directory (`fileParameters/<location>`); stashed and Base64 files are read back by the Pipeline with `unstash`, `withFileParameter` and `readFile`/`writeFile` in Base64 encoding (no `sh`, so Windows CI works), and the test reads the workspace. Core's file parameter is tested on Freestyle only (it does not work in Pipeline). *Secrets inside a build:* a static build step (`TypedParameterFixtures.CaptureEnv`) records environment values in test memory without printing them and holds no captured state, so no log, logTail, configuration snapshot or diff holds them. *Encrypted storage:* `requests/run/<id>.xml` must hold a `{...}` token that `Secret.decrypt` turns into the secret, and every store file is scanned for the plaintext and the definition default. *Server paths:* the forbidden list adds the JVM temporary directory, `jenkins-stapler-uploads` and `StoreLocation=`: on the pre-D-72 code a file value was stored and shown as the upload's `toString()`, which names the servlet upload area outside `$JENKINS_HOME`. *Disposal:* "the request's temporary files" are the regular files that appeared with the submission under the two documented directories; empty directories are not pinned; T-05-57 is the guard that disposal is per request. "The approved run could not be queued" had no row here; the reason first given, that no public input makes the queue refuse an approved request deterministically, was wrong (spec-review-S7 M-2): a test `QueueDecisionHandler` consulted before Batch Control's gate, or core's `jenkins.model.queue.ItemDeletion` veto consulted after it, refuses deterministically. Note 265 adds those rows (T-05-88, T-05-89, T-05-91, T-05-92). Dropping a queued item still hands the files to core's own cancellation listener, which is not Batch Control's disposal; D-72b (7) adds that such a run is not resubmitted (T-05-87). *Body cap:* the property is set per test and cleared afterwards, so the plugin must read it when it checks (Request to core-dev, as for TriggerBlockedAuditTest); a test servlet filter records each submit's Content-Length, so "just under the cap" is a measured premise; T-05-61 proves "before the form is read" with a body that is not valid multipart; T-05-62 proves the permission check comes first; T-05-64 adds the crumb check for multipart, because core's crumb filter does not read a multipart body. *Rerun:* the answer is pinned as 302 (frozen contract); `p.DATA` is not expected because a file is not a simple value; T-11-12 expects `p.DATE` because the incident recorded it and SPEC 11 prefills recoverable non-sensitive values. The notice on the form that file and secret values must be given again is not asserted (its wording is not part of the contract; gap). *Baseline:* at commit time the tests do not compile (the typed `create` overload and `RerunNeedsFormException` do not exist yet). Compiled against throwaway stubs on the pre-D-72 code (not committed), T-05-47, T-05-50, T-05-62, T-05-63, T-05-64 and T-SEC-19 pass and every other new or rewritten row fails on the D-72 behaviour it pins (the build received `********`, a file shown as the upload's `toString()`, no 413, no disposal, rerun created a request after a deleted build). *Ids:* the note is numbered 260, out of sequence, so that the parallel D-71 worktree can use 253 onward (as note 222).

268. **D-74 (1): typed values live in `requests/run/<id>.values.xml` (T-05-101 added; T-05-44, 45, 74, 77..86 and 93 retargeted).** Decision-driven retarget, not a loosening. Written from DECISIONS D-74 (1) and the storage relayed by the coordinator as documented: `requests/run/<id>.xml` holds the request with its masked `parameters` and no typed value; the typed values are in `requests/run/<id>.values.xml`, root `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.model.RunRequestValues` with `requestId` and `values` (the `ParameterValue` objects as XStream writes them, Secrets encrypted); a parameterless request has no values file; the values file is deleted when the approved run starts or the request ends, and retention deletes it with the request; a request with parameters whose values file is missing or unreadable cannot be approved or run (fail closed); listings read only `<id>.xml`. No src/main knowledge. *Why the rows failed on 309ade7:* each looked for the typed values inside `<id>.xml` (baseline run: T-05-74/45/93 found no encrypted token there, T-05-77 saw the extra `<id>.values.xml`, T-05-78..80 and 82 found no `parameterValues` to edit, T-05-81 removed nothing because `<id>.xml` had nothing to remove and the request was approved, T-05-44 found the Base64 in `<id>.values.xml`, T-05-83..86 found neither the Base64 nor the probe in `<id>.xml`); every other assertion of those rows held. *What moved (every assertion's intent kept):* T-05-74, 45 and 93 read the encrypted token from the values file. T-05-77's guard expects exactly `<id>.xml` and `<id>.values.xml`; the "listing unchanged" checks after each refusal are unchanged and now also cover the values file. T-05-78, 79, 80 and 82 edit the values file (`TypedParameterFixtures.typedElement` finds the value inside its `values` element; duplicate, rename and retype are unchanged string edits) and their premises read the edit there; T-05-78..81 still append the marker to the reason in `<id>.xml` and read it back, which proves the request is re-read from disk (whether the values file is re-read is observable only through the approval, where a stale copy would make the row fail, not pass). T-05-81 deletes the values file instead of stripping `parameterValues`: under D-74 a request stored before D-72, a request whose values file was lost and one whose values were removed all look the same on disk (`<id>.xml` without `<id>.values.xml`), and the row still asserts the refusal with the twin guard. T-05-44 expects the Base64 while pending only in `<id>.values.xml` (which holds all of it), after the run nowhere (unchanged). T-05-83..85: "kept" means the values file holds the Base64 and the encrypted secret; "removed" means the values file is gone and no remaining `<id>.*` file of `requests/run/` holds the Base64 or a token that decrypts to the secret (stricter than the former single-file check: a renamed leftover such as `<id>.values.xml.bak` is caught); `RequestFileSnapshot` also records the values file from inside the build (`<job>#<n>:values`, `<missing>` when absent) and T-05-83 requires it to be `<missing>` while the approved run runs. T-05-86's premise reads the values file with `Jenkins.XSTREAM2` (only it holds the probe), so the counter staying 0 means no listing, badge or periodic work read a values file. `TypedParameterFixtures.withoutTypedValues` (the pre-D-72 shape of a single file) was removed with its only caller. *T-05-101 (new):* the parameterised request adds exactly the two files; the values file's root element, its `requestId`, the encrypted secret and the typed string value as XStream writes it (`hudson.model.StringParameterValue`); `<id>.xml` holds neither value's class name nor the encrypted secret and carries the display map; a parameterless request submitted on the form adds `<id>.xml` only, and the guard approves it and sees it run, so the fail-closed rule for a missing values file is not applied to a request without parameters. P1 (storage layout; the run-blocking rule it guards is P0 elsewhere, T-05-81). *Not pinned:* the refusal message ("the stored values are missing"), as note 265 leaves messages unpinned. *Gaps:* an unreadable values file (truncated or not XML) is covered only through a value whose class cannot be loaded (T-05-80); retention deleting the values file together with the request is not asserted (RetentionClosedRequestsTest seeds requests without parameters); ARCHITECTURE section 5 still describes the D-72b single-file layout. *Results (309ade7, test changes only):* before the retarget the four classes ran 33 tests with exactly these 14 failures, each at the old location; after it TypedParameterDisposalTest 10, TypedParameterFormSurfaceTest 6, TypedParameterIntegrityTest 12, TypedParameterRestartTest 4, TypedParameterValuesTest 14 (with T-05-101), TypedValueRemovalTest 4, RestartRecoveryTest 3 and RequestBodyCapTest 11 pass (64 tests, 0 failures).

269. **Coverage-inventory GAP rows, round 6 (T-02-124/125, T-03-27, T-05-102..111, T-06-100..106, T-06a-56, T-07-11, T-08-165..176, T-10-12/13, T-11-25..29, T-12-15, T-SEC-77/78, T-UI-119).** Written from the test-author's coverage inventory of 2026-10-06 (GAP ids G-H*, G-M*, G-L* below), SPEC items 2, 3, 5, 6, 6a, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 (including the incident-authorization line added in f0f67b0), DECISIONS D-35a/c, D-38b, D-40/40a, D-59/59b, D-60, D-66, D-70, D-71/71c, D-72 and D-73, and core's and the plugins' public APIs, without reading src/main. The D-74-dependent GAPs are not written here (G-H2 restart with typed values, G-H3 windows follow their item, G-H4 the separate values file, G-M8 the size check after D-74), and no row asserts where typed values are stored, window following, or the unbound-window display. *Dialog (G-H1, G-M1, G-M12):* core 2.568 opens both Request Run entries with its dialog "wizard" (`[data-type=dialog-opener]`, `dialog-url`): it fetches the fragment, inserts the fragment's form into the current page, recreates its scripts, and on submit runs `buildFormTree` and posts `FormData` (multipart when there is a file control) with the crumb, following a redirected answer. HtmlUnit cannot open core's dialog, so `DialogFixtures` performs the same steps on the job page: the fragment `job/<name>/batch-control/dialog` is fetched with the user's session, its markup is inserted into the job page, `evalInnerHtmlScripts` runs its scripts and `Behaviour.applySubtree` adds the crumb and the `buildFormTree` handler; the test fills the fragment's own controls and submits that form unchanged. The real dialog in both job UIs stays with e2e (G-H7, G-M13). T-05-111 reads the fragment itself (enctype, one file control per file parameter). *Credentials (G-M1):* `CredentialsParameterValue#isSensitive()` is true, so SPEC item 5 shows it as `********` and D-60 never carries it; the inventory's "display shows the id" is corrected by SPEC, not loosened. The credentials list is filled by the credentials plugin's own page script, which needs Credentials/UseItem, so the requester holds it. *Run parameter (G-M2):* SPEC does not pin the display text of a run value; the rows require it to name the job and the number (`src ?#1`) and the build to receive run id `src#1` (not the default, the newest build). T-06-103 asserts SPEC item 6's sentence ("the submitted parameter values filled in (sensitive values are never carried; file values are not carried either)"): a run value is neither, so it must be carried; note 185's frozen contract named only string, text, boolean and choice. **T-06-103 is red on fd69833+f0f67b0** (Location `?p.P=typed-p`, the form shows `src#2`): reported as a defect (owner ui-dev, or a SPEC narrowing by the human). *Role strategy (G-H5):* a restricted CREATE window answers Item/Create only inside the creating request (D-40a: the new name is read from the endpoint's parameter; outside a request it is unknown and a restricted grant confers nothing), so the rows drive `createItem` over HTTP and never assert `hasPermission(Create)` for it. T-08-168: role-strategy's `RoleBasedProjectNamingStrategy` refuses a name that no role of the creator allows; a window adds a permission but does not switch the installed naming strategy off (SPEC item 2: "the role naming strategy work[s]"; core asks the naming strategy on every creation; D-59b applies the same rule to moves), so `team/app-2` is refused for the window-only holder while the restriction violation `team/other` is still refused and recorded. The inventory's expectation that `app-1` is created under the naming strategy too is withdrawn on that ground; if the owner wants windows to bypass the naming strategy, SPEC must say so. Expiry is reached through `BatchClock.setForTest` (the existing Clock replacement), never by sleeping. *Incidents (G-H6):* users with no Batch Control permission (nobc, anonymous) get 404 by SPEC item 2 (#31), the more specific rule; users holding another Batch Control permission but not ViewHistory get 403 by SPEC item 11; the endpoints are the incident page's own forms (`acknowledge`, `resolve` on an ACKNOWLEDGED incident, `comment`). *Manager (G-L10):* `BatchControl/Request` is implied by `BatchControl/Manage` (`Permission.impliedBy`, observed through the public API), so a Manage holder is a requester and gets the Request Run page; the inventory's "manager: expect 404" was wrong and T-02-125 uses a ViewHistory-only user instead, with a premise that neither user holds Request on the job. T-03-27 (a manager cannot decide) is unaffected. *Log tail (G-M6):* the incident page and `incidents.csv` keep the console log tail (SPEC item 11), which names the build's workspace under JENKINS_HOME; there the file-value paths checked are the two temporary directories and the upload area (not JENKINS_HOME or `java.io.tmpdir` as such), with a guard that the log tail is shown; the run surfaces keep the full list. *Low GAPs:* added G-L1 (T-08-174), G-L2/G-L3 (T-08-176), G-L4 (T-08-175), G-L7 (T-12-15, an RFC 4180 reader checks the record width), G-L8 (T-05-110), G-L10/G-L11 (T-02-125/124), G-L12 (T-03-27, T-07-11), G-L13 (T-06-106), G-L14 (T-SEC-78, move guard only: under a plain strategy windows confer nothing, so there is no window rename to refuse). Recorded, not written: G-L5 (rerun with text, boolean and choice values, and their fallback prefill), G-L6 (rerun fallback for a deleted build holding a core file or a `base64File`), G-L9 (Maven projects; no maven-plugin test dependency, documented in LIMITATIONS by D-74); e2e only: G-H7, G-M13; after D-74: G-H2, G-H3, G-H4, G-M8. *Re-run after D-74 (4) #111 (`descriptor.valuePage`):* T-05-102..108, T-05-111 and T-06-100..104 render parameters through today's form; they must be re-run when #111 lands (the credentials parameter is the case whose descriptor has its own value page).

270. **D-74 windows follow their item, security-38 and D-74 gap rows (T-08-180..190, T-SEC-90, T-05-130..135 added; T-08-131, 146, 148..153, 155, 164 and T-SEC-56 converted).** Written from SPEC 8 line 170 (D-74, D-71c, security-38), SPEC 5 line 97 (values file), DECISIONS D-63, D-71c, D-73, D-74, ARCHITECTURE 4 ("Following the item") and 5 (`requests/run/<id>.values.xml`), docs/reports/security-38.md S-38-01/S-38-02 and the coverage inventory gaps G-H2, G-H3, G-H4, G-M8. No src/main knowledge. Notes 268 and 269 belong to parallel lanes. (a) *Decision-driven conversions, not loosening.* D-74 replaces the D-71a/D-71b identity binding and its unbound state: a window follows its item when an administrator or a user with their own permissions renames or moves it (items below a renamed or moved folder too), and ends when the item is deleted, when a new item is created at its name and when Jenkins starts after the item vanished. Each converted row keeps its intent (no window ever reaches an item nobody approved) and its guards; only the expected outcome follows the decision. T-08-131: the windows travel with the swapped folders and job; the job that took the name `sandbox/prod` still gets nothing. T-08-146: "a renamed or moved item loses its window" becomes "the window follows" (job rename, folder rename with the job below, move and move back), items created at the old names get nothing, and the holder's own rename is still the D-71c refusal (G-H3). T-08-148/150: deletion ends the windows (Ended list with the reason, one GRANT_REVOKE each) instead of unbinding them; re-creation and copying still reach nothing. T-08-149/152: the window follows the rename/move and the rename/move back instead of being lost; T-08-152 adds a folder move with a window on the job below; T-08-149 adds the prefix guard (deleting `ren` ends nothing on `ren-tmp`). T-08-151: windows whose item vanished while down end at startup instead of being unbound. T-08-153: "an unbound window can still be revoked" becomes "a followed window is revoked from its page, and a window ended by its item's deletion offers no revoke and is not revoked twice". T-08-155: the stale-D-35c intent is kept and the created-item record now follows an administrator's rename. T-08-164: "a failed unbinding write is retried" becomes "a failed write of a window's end never leaves it conferring" (in-JVM), and its restart half is the new T-08-190. T-SEC-56: the fixture grants u2's Delete before the SYSTEM move, because the carried window makes `parking` guarded (D-58a, D-58b (1)) and a later widening there is reverted; the row now also asserts that the window follows to `parking/a` and that u2's swap gives u1 nothing on the new `team/a`. (b) *How it is measured.* `WindowStateFixtures` no longer reads the window state marker or the stored `itemIdentity` (ui-dev removed the unbound display, core-dev the identity field); the "No longer applies" text is asserted neither way. Active on an item = the service lists the window with exactly that scope full name and the grants page's Active list has the row linking to `batch-control/grants/<id>/` that names the item; ended = not active, no Active list row, the detail page still opens; ended by deletion = additionally an Ended list row naming the item shows "its item was deleted" (D-63: the grants screen shows the reason), and exactly one new GRANT_REVOKE record per ended window identifies it (grant id, or the id or item in target/detail) and says the item was deleted. The record's wording observed on 0271918 is "Grant <id> for user '<u>' (ITEM:<name>) ended: '<name>' was deleted"; D-63 asks that the record names the reason, not that it repeats the screen's text, so the exact phrase is pinned on the screen and the record must say "was deleted". What a window confers is still read from the item's own ACL and an HTTP config.xml save. T-08-187 reaches "a window on a name no item carries" through the documented gap path (directories removed on disk and `Jenkins.reload()`, which fires no deletion event) and pins only the end state after a creation and a copy at the name. T-08-188 covers the "window follows" column of the inventory's section 2 for Pipeline, Folder, Multibranch Pipeline, Organization Folder and multi-configuration project (Maven untestable, D-74). T-08-189 pins that a followed window is persisted (restart). (c) *security-38.* S-38-01: every URL form of the report's regression test is a row, with distinct new names so each refusal is a separate record: folder window (T-08-180), job window (T-08-181), DELETE+CREATE pair (T-08-182), role-strategy folder and job (T-08-185/186), restricted CREATE (T-SEC-90), and `checkNewName/x` (T-08-183, a field error and no record). Each refusal row pairs the user's refusal with guards: the window still confers afterwards, and in T-08-180/181 the administrator renames through the same URL forms (3xx), proving each form is a live core rename endpoint rather than a 404 that would make the refusal meaningless; "no standing permission" is checked after the administrator revokes the window. The `confirmRename;jsessionid=...` and `confirmRename/%2E%2E` forms have no row: core itself refuses them (400/500) and nothing is renamed either way; whether the plugin should record them is core-dev's request in security-38. S-38-02: T-08-184 pins a bounded detail (the name's first 200 characters present, its first 300 absent, under 1000 characters) and a capped merge key (a name differing only after the cap adds no record). (d) *D-74 gaps.* G-H2 is T-05-130 (core file, password, stashedFile, base64File through a restart between approval and run). G-H4: most of its clauses are already note 268 rows (layout T-05-101, deletion at run start and every end T-05-83..85, listings never load T-05-86, missing values file at approval T-05-81, repeated name T-05-78 and at recovery T-05-82); this note adds only what those do not: listings, badge and periodic work with an unreadable or deleted values file (T-05-132), an unreadable values file at approval (T-05-133) and a missing or unreadable one at recovery (T-05-131). No row: retention deleting a values file left behind by a failed deletion (ARCHITECTURE 5 "retention deletes it with the request"; no public input leaves one behind). G-M8 is T-05-134/135 (stashedFile through the declared-length filter and the kept-size check, form, raw, chunked and json-referenced); RequestBodyCapTest (T-05-59..64, 94..100) is re-run unchanged. (e) *Ids.* New ids start at T-08-180, T-SEC-90 and T-05-130 to leave room for the parallel lane of note 269; the numbers skipped (T-08-165..179, T-SEC-77..89, T-05-102..129) are not rows of this note. (f) *Results on f39770e* (r6/integration merged): 75 of the 77 tests of the ten touched classes pass; T-08-164 and T-08-190 fail. When the end of a deleted item's window cannot be written (grants directory read-only during the deletion), the service stops listing the window and it confers nothing in the running JVM, but the grants page still lists it among the active windows after write access returns and the periodic work ran (T-08-164), and after a restart the window is active again and confers Configure on the job re-created at its name (T-08-190), so the end is neither retried nor re-derived (suspected owner core-dev; the D-71c (3) retry was removed with the binding).

271. **file-parameters is an optional dependency (D-74 (2); T-02-123 added; T-02-86 premise, notes 182 and 235 updated).** Written from DECISIONS D-74 (2), SPEC item 5 (D-72), ARCHITECTURE 4, dependency-01 M-3 and the change relayed by release-manager and core-dev (file-parameters is now an optional dependency; no src/main knowledge). *T-02-86:* `OptionalDependencyFixtures.COMPILE_TIME_OPTIONAL` names file-parameters, so the premise now requires it in the computed omit list, and the boot's absent list names it; the omit list itself was already computed from the hpi manifests and needed no change. *T-02-123:* follows T-02-84/85 (the shared absence-boot steps run first) and adds core's own `file` parameter through the form, since that is the file path that must keep working without the plugin: the stored display, the request detail, the approved build's workspace file compared byte for byte, and the disposal of a rejected request's core temporary file (measured as in T-05-53: the regular files that appeared under `fileParameterValueFiles` with the submission). It also asserts that no plugin at all failed to load (stricter than T-02-84..86, which only check batch-control): nothing on the test class path requires file-parameters today; if a future test dependency does, the message names it and the omit list of this row must grow. The class and every fixture it calls (`OptionalDependencyFixtures`, `TypedParameterFixtures`, `UsabilityFixtures`, `ApproverFormFixtures`, `BatchControlFixtures`) reference no file-parameters type. The form submission runs with the crumb issuer off, which the shared steps leave behind (note 182). Run on the integration branch (f52eb07 plus this change): the six OptionalDependency* classes pass (6/6).

272. **DELETE records of items deleted with their folder name the deleting user (T-09-25..29).** Written from SPEC 6 (usability: "recorded history names who did what"), SPEC 9 (deletions are recorded "whatever the path" with who changed what; recording is active while either switch is on), SPEC 3 (ChangeRecord `target, user, at`) and DECISIONS D-71 ("core's `AbstractItem.delete()` deletes all children as SYSTEM without checking them"); no src/main knowledge. *Why the children:* the folder's own deletion runs as the requesting user, but every item below it is deleted by core under SYSTEM, so a record that takes its user from the authentication current when the item's deletion fires names SYSTEM for each child. A throwaway probe in src/test (a `@TestExtension` `ItemListener` printing `Jenkins.getAuthentication2()` in `onDeleted`, not committed) observed exactly that on 177b13a for the admin's HTTP deletion of `fold`: `fold/child=SYSTEM, fold/sub/deep=SYSTEM, fold/sub=SYSTEM, fold=admin`. With attribution falling back to the current authentication, T-09-25, T-09-26 and T-09-27 therefore fail on their first child target (`fold/child`, `cfold/child`, `f2/c2`: "must name admin/d2, found [DELETE/<child>/SYSTEM]"), and the `changes.csv` check would fail the same way. T-09-28 and T-09-29 pass under that fallback; they guard against an over-correction: a deletion that SYSTEM really made must keep saying SYSTEM, including after a user's deletion on the same thread (a remembered deleting user that is not cleared would name admin there). *Fixtures:* T-09-27 runs with change control off because with change control on a standing Item/Delete without a window is vetoed (T-08-51, T-08-124, T-08-143) and no window confers Delete on a folder (D-71); d2 holds Delete on the folder only, since core does not check the children. The change-control-on case is T-09-26, by the administrator (D-71: deleting a folder requires an administrator). *Assertions:* exactly one DELETE record per item (one deletion is one change; a duplicate pair, one naming the user and one SYSTEM, would misname it too), read through `FileStore#listChangeRecords` as in ChangeRecordTest; in `changes.csv` (current month) the row is found by the cells `DELETE` and the item's full name, and the user must be a cell of it. *Run on 177b13a:* the new class 5/5, together with the other ChangeRecord classes 28/28.

273. **spec-review-r6 M-1 and m-11 rows (T-08-191..193, T-05-136..138).** Written from SPEC 8 (the D-59 move line with its D-73 clause; the D-40 line), SPEC 5 (the D-72 and D-72b lines), SPEC 6 (usability), DECISIONS D-40, D-59, D-72b, D-73 and D-74 (4), LIMITATIONS 31, issues #107 and #111, and docs/reports/spec-review-r6.md (M-1, m-11). (a) *T-08-191 (M-1).* Mirrors T-08-147/156/184 on the move path: the same user, item and destination merge within a minute, any other user, item or destination writes its own record. Every move lacks only Delete (u1 and u2 each hold a CREATE window on the destination), so the key is the only difference between attempts. Time is the plugin clock (`BatchClock.setForTest`), never a sleep. T0 is not on a minute boundary, and the attempt to `/team2` at T0+61 s, 31 s after its own record, must write nothing: D-73 names "a one-minute cooldown per attempt key", so a calendar-minute bucket fails the row. "Repeats inside that minute go to the Jenkins log only" is measured as a log record of a logger under `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol`, any level, whose formatted message names `prod/x`, emitted during the immediate repeat; the level and wording are not pinned. Green at commit time. (b) *T-08-192/193 (#107).* SPEC says only that "a CREATE request may carry" the restriction; it does not say what a request without Create does with a submitted one. The rows follow D-74 (4) and #107 (the field belongs to Create and is shown only while Create is ticked) and the coordinator's reading: without Create the text is ignored, neither stored nor a refusal. T-08-193 extends that to an invalid regular expression, because the usability line asks for a refusal next to the field and the field is hidden without Create; it is P2 because it rests on that reading (reported as ambiguous). The service-level refusal of a restriction without Create that spec-review-r6 mentions is not pinned (no SPEC line). Both green. (c) *T-05-136/137 (LIMITATIONS 31).* SPEC and D-72b name the refusal of XML-illegal characters for stored values and the reason only; the comment and the parameter name come from LIMITATIONS 31. The rows therefore pin the refusal, the unchanged store and the usability line (an HTML page with the form again and an explanation, no crash page), not the HTTP code (4xx for the name post, below 500 for the decision post, which may redirect) and not the wording. U+0001 is used because XML 1.1 can hold it and XML 1.0 cannot; U+FFFE is a non-character XML cannot hold at all. *Harness finding:* HtmlUnit's `setRequestParameters` sends U+FFFE as `?`, so the first version of T-05-136 saw an approval with the comment `looks?fine` and failed; Jenkins never received the character. The decision post now percent-encodes its body as UTF-8 itself (what a browser sends), and a scratch probe confirmed that the service and the endpoint both refuse U+FFFE, U+FFFF, U+0001, U+001F and U+D800. Both rows green. No earlier row posts U+FFFE, U+FFFF or a surrogate over HTTP (T-05-77's U+FFFF is a service call; the U+0000 rows encode correctly), so no other row is affected. (d) *T-05-138 (#111).* A form that includes the definition with a hard-coded `index.jelly` falls back to the string parameter's page, so the marker, the starting value and the `origin` field are all missing and the stored value ends in `@index`. Core's own build form, which includes `descriptor.valuePage`, is the premise that the test type is wired correctly. The value page is a test resource (`src/test/resources/.../ParameterValuePageTest/OriginParameterDefinition/valuePage.jelly`). Green.

274. **security-39 regression rows (T-SEC-91..95, T-09-30).** Written from the Given/When/Then of docs/reports/security-39.md S-39-01, S-39-02, S-39-03 and S-39-05, SPEC 4 (restart durability), SPEC 5 (D-74: the values file; listings never load it), SPEC 8 line 170 ("renaming, moving, swapping or re-creating items never makes a window reach an item nobody approved"), SPEC 6 and 9 (recorded history names who did what), DECISIONS D-71c (3) and D-74 (3), CLAUDE.md (user input reaching a file path is validated) and ARCHITECTURE sections 4 and 5. S-39-04 waits for an owner decision and has no row yet. (a) *T-SEC-91.* Asserted on any file system, without a premise that `<id>.VALUES.xml` resolves: on a case-sensitive one the row is green already, on a case-insensitive one (this macOS run: yes) it reproduces the finding. The heap measurement of the report is not pinned (not a stable assertion in a shared JVM); the 404 and the absence of a ClassCastException show that the values file is not read as a request. (b) *T-SEC-92/94, how the approval race is played.* No public extension point runs between the approval's item check and the window's registration, so the rows play the registration themselves through the public `GrantService#register(Grant, Item)` with the item object the approval checked, as the report's probe F2 did. The `Grant` constructor is private, so the never-registered window is read with core's `Jenkins.XSTREAM2` from a copy of a window file the plugin wrote (`grants/<id>.xml`, ARCHITECTURE 5), with its id, request id and item name replaced; the copy's id, holder and item are asserted as premises. Each row first registers such a copy for an item still in place and requires it to confer, so neither a broken hook nor a broken copy can make the row pass. The signature of `register` was learned from the compiler's error on a probe call, not from src/main. Request (core-dev): if the fix moves the re-check out of `register`, keep a public or test-visible way to play the approval's registration step, or give approval a test hook between the check and the registration, so these rows keep measuring the race. (c) *T-SEC-93.* Read-only bits as in T-08-190 (skipped where the process can write anyway); the "either names `b` or ended with a GRANT_REVOKE record" Then of the report is asserted as written. (d) *T-SEC-95.* The records are appended while Jenkins is down, directly to the newest month file, as copies of the newest stored line with a fresh UUID id each (StoreDataFixtures' approach), so all of them are newer than the window's GRANT_REVOKE record and inside its lifetime. Checked for the right reason: with 0 appended records the same row is green (this run), with 60,000 it fails at the Configure assertion. (e) *T-09-30.* A test `ItemListener#onCheckDelete` vetoes `gf/c2`; core deletes the children as SYSTEM inside the administrator's deletion, so the veto aborts it after `gf/c1`. (f) *Red at commit time* on r6/integration 76a2826 (fixes on r6/int-core4): T-SEC-91 (`<id>.VALUES/` answers 500 for u1, ClassCastException `RunRequestValues` to `RunRequest` logged), T-SEC-92 (Configure on the new `r` = true), T-SEC-93 (Configure on the job renamed into `a` = true; the follow logged `StoreWriteException ... could not be saved`), T-SEC-94 (Configure on the job renamed into `s` = true; the move half is not reached), T-SEC-95 (Configure on the new `a` = true after the restart), T-09-30 (the DELETE record of `gf/c2` names admin). Guards and premises passed in each.

275. **security-39 remainder and D-75 rows (T-SEC-96..104); e2e-16 round-6 rows (T-E2E-12..34).** Written from SPEC 8 lines 170 and 171 (the new line "a window's followed name is shown only to a viewer who may read the item"), SPEC 13 (D-36), SPEC 4 (restart durability), SPEC 6 (usability), SPEC 3 (`Grant` fields `revokedBy`, `revokedReason`), DECISIONS D-63, D-68, D-71c (3), D-74 and D-75, ARCHITECTURE 4 ("Following the item": registration re-check, a window that cannot follow ends, D-35c records updated in memory first and retried, time-bounded startup re-end that fails closed, followed names only for readers) and 5, LIMITATIONS 11 and 24, CLAUDE.md (user input reaching a file path is validated), docs/reports/security-39.md (S-39-01..04) and docs/reports/e2e-16.md (R6-01..R6-23). No src/main knowledge. (a) *T-SEC-96/97 (S-39-04, D-75 (1)).* "Not shown" is the destination folder's name `vault-q9` absent from the raw HTML of each answer (text, links, attributes) and from every field of the notifier payload and the mail's subject and body, which also covers the new full name. The fixed note is pinned only as the word "moved" next to the approved name `team/x`: D-75 gives its sense ("moved; its new location is not visible to you") and SPEC 171 its content, neither fixes the wording; on u1's grants list the word must be in the window's own Active row, so a help text elsewhere on the page cannot satisfy it. The request reasons name no item, so an item name on a page or in a mail comes from the window's scope. a1's view of the window's page and a1's grants list are asserted only negatively (LIMITATIONS 24: an active window is visible to its holder and to Manage). The controls (a rename inside `team`, which u1 and a1 may read) require the current name `team/y2` where a reader looks, and the administrator must see `vault-q9/x`, so a fix that hides the name from everyone fails the rows. T-SEC-97 runs the expiry work on the plugin clock (`BatchClock.setForTest`, no sleep); the two GRANT_EXPIRING mails are told apart by the request id each carries (SPEC 13), after the APPROVED mails were delivered and cleared. (b) *T-SEC-98/99 (S-39-01).* The administrator is the viewer, so no visibility rule can produce the 404. On a case-insensitive file system `<ID>.xml` resolves to the record's own file; the row demands 404 because that URL is not the record's identifier (D-68 names the identifiers; a second URL for a record would be an undocumented alias). `<id>~1` is the report's Windows 8.3 route, `x.y` a dotted id. T-SEC-99 plants files under fresh UUID names so the identifier's shape cannot be what refuses them; each foreign copy has its own id replaced by the planted one, so only its type is wrong; the values-file copy is the S-39-01 shape (`RunRequestValues` read as a request). The list pages answering 200 afterwards is a guard (a planted file must not break a section). (c) *T-SEC-100 (S-39-02 (b) for the item lists a window keeps).* ARCHITECTURE 4: "D-35c records are updated in memory first and their write is retried", so u1 already configures `fo/k` while the write fails; "after the next write" is read after the periodic work, a documented retry point. The stored window's two documented lists (ARCHITECTURE 5: `createdItems`, and `changedItems`, which "follows renames and moves") are read separately: `createdItems` must list `fo/k` and not `fo/j`; `changedItems` must not keep `fo/j`, which now names the administrator's job, and must list `fo/k` when it listed `fo/j` before the rename. A guard first shows both lists following a rename when writes succeed (`fo/g1` to `fo/g2`), so a failure is about the failed write, not about following in general. (d) *T-SEC-101 (fix direction (4)).* Core compares item names case-insensitively: the row reads `getItemByFullName("gone") == GONE` as a premise and asserts the end only when it holds, as the brief asked; u1 gets no Configure on `GONE` either way. The item vanishes by the documented gap path of T-08-187 (directory removed, `Jenkins.reload()`, no deletion event); whether the reload already ended the window is reported in the assertion messages and on standard output, not pinned (as T-08-187); on 2843465 the window was still active after the reload and Jenkins found `GONE` at `gone`, so the creation path ended it. (e) *T-SEC-102 (D-71c (3), upheld by D-75 (2)).* "After the deletion event, before the name is freed" is produced deterministically by a test folder (`WindowStaleNameTest.HookFolder`, its descriptor installed for this row only) whose `onDeleted` does what the folders plugin's own does (fire the item listeners, remove the child, update the views) with a hook between the listeners and the removal; the registration therefore runs after every item listener, whatever their ordinals, while the name still carries the deleted job (premise asserted). A test item listener cannot do this: `@TestExtension` gives ordinal 0, so it would run before a listener with a lower ordinal and only re-test T-08-148. The window copy is made as for T-SEC-92 (note 274 (b)). The row reads no grant page: the stored windows show that a window's id is its request's id, while the copy carries an id of its own and its request stays PENDING (only the registration is played), so no detail page or list row can show it as an approved window; first runs that read the pages failed on that artefact (404 for the copy's page), not on the plugin. The end is read instead from the service (not active), the stored window (`revokedAt` set, `revokedReason` containing "its item was deleted", read with core's XStream2) and the GRANT_REVOKE records. (f) *T-SEC-103/104 (D-75 (2), ARCHITECTURE 4).* T-SEC-103 clears the read bits of every change month file between two sessions, after a plain restart showed the window intact (guard), and is skipped where the process can still read them; "revoked by SYSTEM with a reason" is read from the stored window with core's XStream2 (`Grant#getRevokedBy`, `#getRevokedReason`) and from u1's Ended list. T-SEC-104 tightens T-SEC-93's either/or Then (which stays as the report wrote it) to the D-75 ruling: the window that could not follow ends at once, with exactly one GRANT_REVOKE record whose detail names the failed follow and the Ended list reason "it could not follow its item" (the screen wording as relayed by the coordinator). In the record only the word "follow" is pinned (as note 270 pins "was deleted" for deletions): D-63 asks that the record names the reason, not that it repeats the screen's text; the wording observed on 2843465 is "Grant <id> for user 'u1' (ITEM:fol-a) not followed: its file could not be updated to its item's new name 'fol-b'". (g) *Results on 2843465* (r6/integration, macOS APFS case-insensitive, JDK 21.0.12, Maven 3.9.16): 14 tests of RecordLookupPathTest, WindowStaleNameTest, WindowEndRestartTest, WindowFollowedNameVisibilityTest and RequestIdPathTest, 11 pass. Green: T-SEC-98, 99, 101, 102, 103 (not skipped), 104, and the unchanged T-SEC-91..95. Red: T-SEC-96 (u1's grant request page shows `vault-q9/x`; its premises and the `team/y2` control passed) and T-SEC-97 (the GRANT_EXPIRING payload to u1 has `subject=vault-q9/x`), both expected until the D-75 (1) fix (ui-dev, core-dev); T-SEC-100, a possible defect (suspected owner core-dev): after the failed write the stored window's `createdItems` is right (`fo/k`), but its `changedItems` still lists `fo/j`, which now names the administrator's job, and not `fo/k` (log: "GrantService#rewriteChanged: Could not update the changed-under-grant state of 'fo/j'"); with writes succeeding both lists follow (guard green), so the changed-under-grant list is neither updated in memory first nor retried, unlike the created-item list, and the job changed under the window loses its D-58a state while another job takes it over. (h) *T-E2E-12..34* are e2e-16 R6-01..R6-23 in order (e2e-tester's request): type e2e, no Java test; the test file column names the driver and section(s) of docs/reports/e2e-16.md, all PASS there on aeaac42 (R6-23 after the driver fix 0a68f5c, re-run `supp2`). Priorities follow this matrix's rule: permission scope and refusals, granting, the run gate, secrets on text surfaces and durability P0 (16); screens, form errors, disposal and rerun links P1 (7). R6-24 (fixture preconditions) is not a scenario and has no row. 276. **Coverage lane 1 gap rows: run control, requests, activation, incidents, records (T-GAP-101..180).** Written from the lane-1 scenario list (L1-01..L1-21; there is no L1-10), SPEC 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6a, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and the usability line, DECISIONS D-20, D-21, D-23, D-30, D-36, D-37, D-46, D-51, D-51a, D-54, D-55, D-57, D-59a, D-60, D-66, D-72, D-72a, D-72b and D-74, LIMITATIONS 16, 19, 28, 31, 39, 48, 49 and 51, and ARCHITECTURE 1, 2 and 5; no src/main knowledge. New classes only (19, all named `*GapTest`), no existing test or fixture changed; one test resource, the form view of the L1-14 fixture parameter types. (a) *Fault injection.* Only through the store on disk (a non-empty directory where a month or values file is expected, `requests/run` replaced by a plain file, hand-edited request, values, incident and activation files, deleted state files and job directories, chmod with an assumption that skips the row where the path stays readable or writable, as under root), the documented `BlockedAttemptAudit` seam (`swapStoreForTesting`, `flushAtShutdown`, `flushPersonSummaries`), a queue handler of the test (`QueueRefusalFixtures`) and test extensions that subclass core's and file-parameters' cancelled-queue-item listeners and throw. Time moves only through `BatchClock`. (b) *Ambiguities (assertions follow the documents, not the scenario where they differ).* T-GAP-113 (inverted by D-80, owner decision 2026-10-09, note 303): a job directory replaced on disk by a copy of itself is what a backup restore or a move of JENKINS_HOME leaves; the activation identity is the marker kept in the job's directory, so the copy keeps its activation and the row asserts the job stays activated and its timer runs (it first read the replaced directory as a job deleted and re-created outside Jenkins and asserted the opposite); the copy without the marker is T-06a-65. T-GAP-130..132: no document names a maximum of 50 approvers or a 256-character approver id, so the rows assert the documented refusal of approvers that are not on the list (SPEC 3) with a message naming the approvers and the input kept; the incident rerun form has no reason field (observed), so T-GAP-132 checks the kept reason only when the form has one. T-GAP-136: the 413 message format ("1,500 bytes", "1 MB") is not documented; any spelling of the limit is accepted. T-GAP-138/139: no document says how an unresolvable requester is shown; the rows read it fail closed (the requester cannot be shown to hold Build, so the notice appears) and move the plugin clock past the five-minute cache life of LIMITATIONS 49 before each re-evaluation. T-GAP-146: the display of a null parameter value is not documented; only the numeric value is asserted. T-GAP-171: anonymous's refused cancel is answered with the sign-in page (HTTP 200), not 4xx; no document fixes the status for anonymous, so the row accepts either and asserts the documented outcome (PENDING). T-GAP-173: the status of a POST to a read-only history endpoint (the scenario says 405) is not documented; the row asks for 4xx; the 400 for a bad month must name the month and the form YYYY-MM. T-GAP-121: the scenario's MARKER_REUSE_BLOCKED record for a marker presented on another job before it was consumed is read as SPEC 6 D-30 (passes). (c) *Possible defect.* T-GAP-147 is red on bd449cd: a run line whose `parameters` member is an array (`["P1"]`) is listed on the history screen but missing from `runs.csv` ("shown on the history screen: true, in runs.csv: false"), so screen and export disagree about the same line (SPEC 4 #13 "screens and exports never silently disagree", "the CSV export, which is complete"). The other malformed lines and every valid variant agree. (d) *Fixture notes.* The dashboard shows the last seven days up to the plugin clock's now, so a clock fixed before the builds start hides them: T-GAP-145..152 keep the real clock and only compute the month. In Jenkins, what anonymous holds applies to every user, so T-GAP-171 grants anonymous Request and Item/Read in its own row only (a first draft with the grant in the common setup let every account open the run requests section). The Request Run form re-renders on a 413, so the L1-14 fixture definitions need a form view (`src/test/resources/io/jenkins/plugins/batchcontrol/RequestCustomParameterGapTest/TextDefinition/index.jelly`); without it the page failed with 500. A url-encoded POST from HtmlUnit must be sent as UTF-8 for non-ASCII prefill values (T-GAP-157). *IDs.* `T-GAP-<serial>` rows come from the coverage-gap scenario lists (behaviour left uncovered by the suite, written in behaviour terms): 101..199 lane 1, 2xx lane 2 (note 277).

277. **Coverage lane 2 GAP rows: change control, guard, windows, configuration, monitors (T-GAP-201..269).** Written from the lane-2 scenario list (L2-01..L2-18, uncovered behaviour stated in behaviour terms), SPEC items 1, 2, 5, 6, 6a, 7, 8, 9, 15 and the usability line, DECISIONS D-31, D-34, D-35b..d, D-40, D-40a, D-42, D-48, D-50a, D-52, D-53, D-58..D-58c, D-59, D-59b, D-71, D-71c, D-73, D-74, P-09, P-10, P-15, ARCHITECTURE sections 1, 4 and 5, LIMITATIONS 11, 12, 13, 29, 33, 35 and 44, and docs/reports/security-05 S-06. No src/main knowledge: two public signatures were taken from the compiled classes' public method lists (the six-argument `GrantRequestService#create` that carries a name restriction, and the `check<Field>` names of the global configuration), and the HTTP answers of `markReviewed` and `batch-control/reviewed` were observed black-box only to choose URLs, never to set an expected text. (a) *Fault injection* uses only the scenario file's methods. GuardRestoreGapTest declares a save listener and an item listener with `@Extension(ordinal = 100000)` (`@TestExtension` has no ordinal), so they exist in every test JVM of the module but are inert unless armed for one item's full name; armed, they fire once and replace that item's `config.xml` with a non-empty directory, so the next write of the item fails (root-safe), and every test restores it. Store faults are a corrupt or chmod-000 snapshot (`snapshots/<name>.xml`, chmod case skipped where it does not take effect), a non-empty directory in place of `changes/2026-09.jsonl` (clock fixed at T0), and `BlockedAttemptAudit.swapStoreForTesting` with a dynamic proxy whose `appendChangeRecord` throws. Stored-file edits (T-GAP-223, 229) and the vanished directory (T-GAP-245) are made between two sessions of `JenkinsSessionExtension`, because the request and grant index is built once per session (ARCHITECTURE 5), each edit from the file the plugin wrote with its premise asserted. (b) *T-GAP-205 is red (possible defect).* A folder copied through a CREATE window keeps no authorization entry when it has no children (part 1 green, one GRANT_VIOLATION). The scenario's folder with a job inside cannot be copied by a CREATE-window holder: core copies the child as the user and refuses it ("bob is missing the Job/Create permission", 403), because a window's CREATE never reaches inside the new folder (D-71). The half-made `dest/copy-f` stays; in memory it has no authorization property (also after `Jenkins.reload()`), but its `config.xml` on disk still carries the source's entries (alice's and bob's Item/Configure), and no GRANT_VIOLATION is written. SPEC 2 says a copied item's payload property "is removed and recorded as GRANT_VIOLATION". (c) *T-GAP-211 is red, as the scenario expects (possible defect, security-05 S-06):* when the save that removes a creation payload's authorization property fails, the creation answers without a crash page but no GRANT_VIOLATION is written at all, while the same failure on an existing item (T-GAP-208/209) and on a copy into a guarded folder (T-GAP-210) is recorded with a failure detail that tells an administrator to check the item. (d) *T-GAP-221:* of the three URL variants only `…/./confirmRename` reaches core's rename endpoint (refused and recorded); `;x=1` is answered 400 by core's "Semicolons are not allowed in the request URI" request filter and the malformed escape by Jetty's bad-message answer, both before any rename endpoint, so they are skipped after asserting that nothing was renamed (scenario rule). (e) *T-GAP-222, ambiguity:* SPEC 8 says the restriction is "validated at submission (an invalid regex is refused)" and that names over 255 characters are refused; that a 1,001-character restriction, `//` and an exact name that is not a valid item name (`a/b`, `..`) are invalid is the scenario's reading of "validated", not a doc line. All are refused today. (f) *T-GAP-224, ambiguity:* the scenario expects a CONFIGURE-only request with a restriction to be refused; the form contract (T-08-192, D-74 (4), #107) accepts it and stores no restriction. The row accepts either at the service (refused, or stored without the restriction). (g) *T-GAP-230 is red (possible defect, LIMITATIONS 29, P-15):* with change control off, the Grants URL still answers with the explanation, requesting is refused with a message and a `GRANT_REQUEST_BLOCKED` record, but approving through the web (`grants/<id>/approve`) is refused with the message and writes no record. A probe outside the suite showed that `GrantRequestService#approve` itself writes the record, so the web path refuses before reaching the service. (h) *T-GAP-241 is red (possible defect, SPEC 6 usability):* `migrate` with no Batch Control variant and `revert` of a plain strategy are refused with 4xx and the right reason, but both answers are core's "Oops!" page with a stack trace (`HttpResponses.error`). (i) *T-GAP-247:* a confirmation is a sentence saying the item "was marked as reviewed"; the row's positive twin (`done-1`) shows that the page uses it, so the negative cases cannot pass on a page that never confirms anything. (j) *T-GAP-248, ambiguity:* the scenario expects "an empty OK" for a user without Manage; SPEC 2 says only that such a user cannot change the configuration, and T-CFG-09 has the approver check answer 403. The row asserts "no validation verdict and no server error" (an empty OK or a 4xx), with the manager's error as the guard. (k) *T-GAP-252, ambiguity:* the exact result `[15, 30]` for `grantDurationOptionsText: "15, abc, 30"` is the scenario's; D-42 ("a direct setter call ... applies the value") speaks of the switches. Green today. (l) *T-GAP-254:* the scenario names the blocking switch `replayedUnderGrant`; no doc line names it, so the row asserts the documented parts (TRIGGER_BLOCKED, the user, the job, the Replay cause kind). (m) *T-GAP-245:* the premise that a vanished item stays listed after the restart is the scenario's; it holds today. (n) The CLI rows (T-GAP-215, 216, 256, 266) run `hudson.cli.CLI` from Jenkins core's `cli` artifact in a child JVM with the test class path, `-s <url> -http -auth <user>:<fresh API token>`, stdin fed and stdout/stderr captured; `CLICommandInvoker` would skip the server-side CLI context. (o) Run on 2026-10-06 (Temurin 21, Maven 3.9.16): 69 tests, 65 green, 4 red (T-GAP-205, 211, 230, 241), 0 skipped. These classes alone cover 5,617 of 10,973 src/main lines (51.2 %, JaCoCo line counter, these 17 classes alone).

278. **security-39 / D-75 follow-ups (T-SEC-105..115; T-SEC-100 fixture changed).** Written from SPEC 2 (the D-58a line: guarding, "changed under a grant", a script's widening reverted whoever makes it), SPEC 4 (append-only records, restart durability), SPEC 8 lines 153, 157, 158, 170 and 171, SPEC 13 (D-36), DECISIONS D-58a, D-63, D-71c, D-74 and D-75, ARCHITECTURE 4 ("Following the item": D-35c records updated in memory first, the time-bounded startup re-end that fails closed, registration re-check, followed names only for readers) and 5 (`changedItems`, JSONL change month files), LIMITATIONS 11 and 24, notes 273..275, and the coordinator's brief relaying two owner decisions of 2026-10-06. No src/main knowledge; the page shape used by T-SEC-113 (where the "Request again" control sits) was observed from rendered HTML in a throwaway probe, not from the code. Notes 276 and 277 belong to parallel lanes. (a) *T-SEC-100, decision-driven, not loosening.* The earlier fixture created `fo/m` as SYSTEM while the CREATE window on `fo` was active; under D-58a (2)/(5) that item enters the window's changed-under-grant state itself, and `changedItems` follows renames (ARCHITECTURE 5), so after `fo/m` → `fo/j` the list legitimately names `fo/j`. The owner changed the fixture: `fo/m` is created by the administrator over HTTP `createItem`, the creation D-58a (2) exempts (premise: not listed). The Then is now unconditional: `changedItems` lists `fo/k` (premise: `fo/j` was listed before the rename) and not `fo/j`. Note 275 (g)'s "possible defect" on T-SEC-100 is thereby withdrawn for its "still lists `fo/j`" half (the fixture's own state); its "and not `fo/k`" half was a defect, fixed on r6/integration by c2ea95b. T-SEC-105 keeps the SYSTEM creation and pins the other side: `changedItems` lists `fo/j` (fo/m's own state, followed) and `fo/k`. Both rows share one scenario helper (`failedFollowOfACreatedJob`). (b) *"Changed under a grant" is read two ways* in T-SEC-100, 105 and 112: the stored window's `changedItems` (ARCHITECTURE 5, D-58a (5)), and its consequence once every window has ended (the plugin clock moves past the 30-minute windows, `BatchClock.setForTest`, no sleep; premise: u1 no longer configures the created job): a script (SYSTEM, not an HTTP request) adds an authorization property giving `carol` Item/Configure; D-58a (2) reverts it and writes a GRANT_VIOLATION on an item in the state and leaves it alone on any other (T-02-58, T-02-65). While the CREATE window is active every item below `fo` is guarded by scope (D-58b (1)), so the widening is only meaningful after the window; a probe confirmed `fo` itself is not listed. The result is read in memory and in `config.xml`, which must agree. Each row has a guard item still in the state whose widening is reverted, so a broken widening cannot make a row pass. (c) *T-SEC-106..109, the torn line.* Written while Jenkins is down, to the newest `changes/YYYY-MM.jsonl` (premise: it ends with a line end), as the brief gave it: `{"id":"<uuid>","type":"GRANT_REVOKE","target":"a","user":"adm`, no closing brace and no line end (a write torn by a crash). T-SEC-107's line is complete, has a line end, `"type":"FUTURE_TYPE"`, target `a` and `at` = the current time in the stored lines' epoch-millisecond form (premise read from the newest stored line). T-SEC-106 and 107 measure exactly the brief's Then. T-SEC-108 and 109 pin what must still hold after the torn line was handled; both are red on 989cf24 and reported as a possible defect (suspected owner core-dev): the first record written at that start (the GRANT_REVOKE of the window on `a`) is appended onto the torn line, which has no line end, so the month file then holds `..."user":"adm{"id":"...","type":"GRANT_REVOKE","target":"a","user":"SYSTEM",...}`: the end of that window is not readable in the change log (only `c`'s record is), and the merged line stays unreadable, so the next plain restart fails closed again and ends the window a1 approved after the torn line was handled (its GRANT_REVOKE by SYSTEM is the last line after the third start). SPEC 8 line 157 says a restart keeps an unexpired window; ARCHITECTURE 4 bounds the re-end read by the time the oldest open window was granted, and that window was granted after the damage. LIMITATIONS 11 still says "a record line that is damaged on disk is skipped with a warning ... so it counts as a record that was never written", which d078bff ("end open windows at startup when a change record line cannot be read") no longer matches (Request to release-manager in the report). (d) *T-SEC-110/111, unknown recipient.* T-SEC-110 deletes u1's user record (`User#delete` as SYSTEM, an administrator's "Delete user") after every web request as u1, and nothing in the row recreates it before the expiry work (`can("u1", …)` is called only before the deletion). T-SEC-111 keeps the record and its address and installs a realm (`RealmWithoutU1`, a test class) whose `loadUserByUsername2("u1")` throws `UsernameNotFoundException`, so `User#impersonate2` throws (premise asserted). "Fail closed" is the brief's either/or: no GRANT_EXPIRING notice for the moved window, or one that names `vault-q9` in no field and `team/x` in the subject, reason or link. u2's window on `team/z`, due in the same run, is the guard that the work ran. Observed on 989cf24: in both rows the notice was sent with `subject=team/x`. (e) *T-SEC-113/114.* The "Request again" control is discovered from u1's Ended list (any `href` or `data-*` value in the table carrying `from=<id>`; on 989cf24 a `data-dialog-url` to `grants/dialog?from=<id>`), and both `grants/new?from=<id>` and `grants/dialog?from=<id>` are opened directly. "Prefilled from the window" (Configure ticked) is a premise, so an unprefilled form cannot pass; the control (the window on `team/y2`, which u1 may read) must start with `team/y2`. The note's marker `[data-batch-control-scope-note="moved"]` and wording "moved; its new location is not visible to you" come from the brief and D-75 (1)'s quoted text; T-SEC-96 pins only the word "moved". In this build a window's id is its request's id, so the window page and the request page are one URL; both paths are opened anyway. adm2 holds no entry of its own on `vault-q9`, but matrix-auth lets Overall/Administer read it, so "administrators see the current name" cannot be told apart from "readers see it"; the row pins the administrator's view without the note. (f) *T-SEC-115, how the race is played.* Calling `GrantService#register` alone (T-SEC-92/102) sends no APPROVED notice: the request stays PENDING there. The row therefore runs a1's real approval (`GrantRequestService#approve`, the service call on the deleting thread, so no HTTP request waits on the deletion's locks) inside the T-SEC-102 hook folder's deletion handling, after every item listener and before the name is freed; the approval's own registration then ends the window (premises: the request is APPROVED, the stored window, found by its `grantRequestId`, is revoked with "its item was deleted", it is not active). The notice is read in the mail, which carries the request id (SPEC 13) and renders every field. "A line saying the window ended at once and why" is pinned as one line containing "ended" and "deleted", case-insensitive; the control (an ordinary approval's mail) must have no such line. If the approval itself refused (a stricter reading), the row fails on its premise with that message, not on the notice. (g) *Results on 989cf24* (r6/integration, macOS APFS, JDK 21.0.12, Maven 3.9.16, `-DforkCount=2`): WindowStaleNameTest 10 tests, WindowEndRestartTest 6, WindowFollowedNameVisibilityTest 6. Green: T-SEC-100 (new fixture), 105, 106, 107, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114 and every earlier row of the three classes (T-SEC-92..97, 101..104; none skipped). Red: T-SEC-108 and T-SEC-109 (possible defect, (c)); T-SEC-115 (expected until r6/int-core6: the APPROVED mail is "Request approved / Request / Scope: hf/rr / … / Reason", with no line about the ended window; every premise passed).

279. **Coverage lane 3 GAP rows: store faults and restarts, windows whose file is unreadable or gone, the review surfaces, retention, store reads, grant and activation pages, incidents, notifications (T-GAP-301..387).** Written from the lane-3 scenario list (L3-01..L3-26, uncovered behaviour stated in behaviour terms), SPEC items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6a, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 and the usability line, DECISIONS D-19, D-35c, D-36, D-40, D-43, D-54, D-58..D-58c, D-63, D-66, D-67, D-68, D-72a, D-72b, D-74 and D-75, LIMITATIONS 11, 23, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35 and 44, ARCHITECTURE 1, 4 and 5, and docs/reports/security-29 S-29-02, security-30 S-30-04 and security-39 S-39-01. No src/main knowledge: the HTML shape of a few pages (where the monitor lists items and runs, the grants list's rows) was observed from rendered pages in a throwaway probe that is not committed, and the test logs were read for the printed observations only; no expected value was taken from either. New classes only (14 integration classes and one unit class, all named `*GapTest`), no existing test or fixture changed. Notes 276..278 belong to parallel lanes. (a) *Fault injection*, only through the store on disk and test extensions: chmod with an assumption that skips the row where the path stays readable or writable (as under root); a non-empty directory in place of the current change month file (T-GAP-377) or a snapshot (T-GAP-385); hand-edited or overwritten files (the activation state, an incident file, a grant request file, incident index lines, change month lines); grant, request and job files deleted while Jenkins runs or between two sessions; a grant file copied while its window was open and copied back after the window ended ("open again on disk", LIMITATIONS 11: Jenkins stopped between the GRANT_REVOKE record and the grant-file write); test extensions: an item listener that puts another item at a renamed job's old name (T-GAP-376), two notifiers of which one blocks (T-GAP-370), a parameter type whose plain-text value is flagged sensitive (T-GAP-367) and one whose value XStream cannot write (T-GAP-386). Time moves only through `BatchClock`; the only waits are polls for asynchronous delivery and the ten-second look at the queue in T-GAP-384 (a resubmitted run of a job bound to a label no agent has would never leave the queue, so `waitUntilNoActivity()` cannot be used). (b) *The torn change-log line (L3-04, finding F-1).* T-GAP-316 follows the owner's ruling relayed by the main session: D-75 (2) and ARCHITECTURE 4 govern, so a damaged line inside the startup read ends every open window, and LIMITATIONS 11's "a record line that is damaged on disk is skipped ... so it counts as a record that was never written" is superseded (the Request to release-manager of note 278 (c) stands). The row's damaged line carries a line end, the state of a torn line once it has been closed by one; the torn line without a line end is T-SEC-106..109. Window F, whose GRANT_REVOKE record lies before the damaged line, must end from that record (LIMITATIONS 11 "is ended again from that record"), and window H, granted after the damaged line, must survive a plain restart (the line is read back by one start only, ARCHITECTURE 4's time bound). (c) *Possible defects, red on ff28137.* **T-GAP-314 and T-GAP-387:** at a start whose change month file cannot be read but can be written, every open window ends as documented, but no GRANT_REVOKE record is appended (the log says "Could not record the end of grant ... it has ended all the same"); the end lives only in the grant file, so in T-GAP-314 window D, whose grant file is back at its open version, is active again in the next session, and in T-GAP-387 the change log holds no record of U's end. LIMITATIONS 11 says such a window "is revoked by SYSTEM with the reason 'its state could not be confirmed at startup' and a GRANT_REVOKE record", and ARCHITECTURE 4 says ending appends that record; the file was writable. T-GAP-314 passed on 3a7f550, so this is new with the r6/int-core7 merge (the torn-line change, judged by its commit subject only; suspected owner core-dev). **T-GAP-320:** after the administrator renames folder `F` to `G`, the strategy monitor lists `G` with the marked run `G/P#2` but no longer lists `G/P`, which it listed as `F/P` with that run before the rename; D-58a (1) "Coverage and the 'changed under a grant' state follow renames and moves" and D-58c "Both review surfaces list the marked runs of the item". **T-GAP-384:** an approved run whose queue item was cancelled while `requests/run/` refused writes is not resubmitted in the same session, also after writes were allowed again and the periodic work ran, but it is submitted again when Jenkins restarts (log: "Recovering approved run request ... for job qj"); LIMITATIONS 32 "never submits that run again, not when Jenkins restarts either" names no exception for a failed write. **T-GAP-385:** with `snapshots/l3-snap.xml` replaced by a non-empty directory, the administrator's `config.xml` save succeeds and is stored, but no CONFIGURE record is written (the log shows an `UncheckedIOException` "Failed to write config snapshot of l3-snap" escaping an item listener); SPEC 9 records every modification whatever the path, and ARCHITECTURE 1 says the records are always written by the event listeners. (d) *Expected red by the scenarios, green on ff28137:* T-GAP-301 and 302 (finding F-3: on 3a7f550 the RENAME record of `b` was missing and u1's `job/a/` answered 500; T-GAP-303 and 304 were green there already), T-GAP-318 (finding F-2: the review clears the entry in memory first and its GUARD_REVIEWED record agrees with the monitor before and after the restart), and T-GAP-316's guard (on 3a7f550 the plain restart ended H). The web approval's GRANT_REQUEST_BLOCKED record of L3-13 (finding F-4, LIMITATIONS 29) is T-GAP-230 and is not repeated in T-GAP-346. (e) *Ambiguities (assertions follow the documents; both documented outcomes accepted where they leave it open, the observed one printed).* T-GAP-325: no folder has a Batch Control page (`job/F/batch-control/markReviewed` answers 404) and the monitor refuses carol (403), so a native Item/Configure holder cannot review a changed folder at all; LIMITATIONS 35 offers the review to such users "on the item's Batch Control page", and the scenario expected carol's review to clear `F`. T-GAP-348: anonymous holding BatchControl/Manage is answered with core's sign-in page (HTTP 200) and the request stays PENDING (as T-GAP-171); SPEC 7 lets a Manage holder cancel, the scenario expected 403. 280. **Expiry-notice isolation, DEF-E17-01 and e2e-17 rows (T-GAP-401..403, T-SEC-116/117, T-E2E-35..46).** Written from SPEC 4 (the per-minute expiry work), 6a (activation requests are notified like run requests, D-36), 8 line 170 (a window applies to its item, not to a name) and 13 (D-36: `EXPIRING`/`GRANT_EXPIRING` fire once, `notifyBeforeExpiryMinutes` before the expiry), DECISIONS D-36, D-74 and D-75, LIMITATIONS 11 (the DEF-E17-01 paragraph, "A window whose own item is still there under exactly the window's name is therefore about that item and stays, whatever arrives next to it under another spelling", and "When the change request's file is there but cannot be read, no expiry notice is sent for that window"), ARCHITECTURE 5 (store layout) and docs/reports/e2e-17.md (R17-01..R17-12, F-2 DEF-E17-01), with the scenarios relayed by the coordinator. No src/main knowledge. New classes only (`ExpiryNoticeIsolationTest`, `WindowCaseVariantRestartTest`); no existing test or fixture changed. (a) *Timeline of T-GAP-402.* The brief's "created 35 min earlier, pendingTimeoutHours=1" is read relative to the window's approval at T0. The expiry work runs at T0+21 min, when the window is 9 minutes from its end and each pending request is 56 minutes old, so inside the 10-minute `EXPIRING` lead of its 60-minute pending timeout. Read relative to the work itself, a request 35 minutes old would be 25 minutes from its expiry, outside the 10-minute lead that the brief sets in its first scenario. (b) *Visiting order.* SPEC does not fix the order in which the expiry work visits windows and requests, so a row shows isolation only when the work visits the faulty entry before a healthy one. The windows of T-GAP-401 and T-GAP-403 are therefore approved one second apart in the order A, B, C: the faulty one is the oldest and ends first. Every expected notice is asserted after the first run, not only after the second, so a work that the faulty entry aborts, and that reaches the others only on a later run, is red. (c) *Faults* are injected only through the store on disk. T-GAP-401 overwrites a change request file with the first half of its own XML. T-GAP-402 sets mode 000 on a pending change request file, and T-GAP-403 on a grant file. An assumption skips the row where the file stays readable (as under root), and `tearDown` restores the mode. (d) *DEF-E17-01 rows.* The folders are created in session 1, so in session 2 they are loaded from disk. Whether core then admits the case variant is core's and the folders plugin's behaviour, so it is checked as a premise: otherwise the row is skipped, with the observation printed. On 07d4529 both premises held: `createItem` of `f/CTL` and `confirmRename` of `f/other` to `CTL` each answered 302 and left a new item next to `f/ctl`. T-SEC-116's guard uses a second folder `g` because `f/CTL` already exists after the main step. Not covered: the D-35c created-item records and the changed-under-grant state next to a case variant (LIMITATIONS 11, "The same exception keeps ..."), and the deletion of a case variant next to a windowed item. The row as committed asserts the directory stays gone, so a timer run that lands inside the deletion still turns it red; it is not forced deterministically (that would need src/main knowledge). Time moves only with `BatchClock`; `ExpiryPeriodicWork.doRun` is called directly. Both green on r6/integration 94a2ec9 (Temurin 21, Maven 3.9.16, `-DforkCount=2`).
