288. **Role naming strategy with a CREATE window (T-E2E-62, e2e-19 G-27).** role-strategy 927 grants Item/Create on every folder to a user who holds any project role with Create while `RoleBasedProjectNamingStrategy` is installed (`RoleMap.AclImpl`), and that naming strategy admits a name only through such a role (or a global Create). So a name both the strategy and a window admit is never created through the window alone: the user already holds Create natively, and a D-40 restriction, which limits only the grant, does not limit that native Create (observed: with a `/teamA-r.*/` window requester created `teamA-x`; not asserted, this is role-strategy's model). The row therefore asserts the two halves separately: for the role holder the window does not loosen the strategy, and for the window-only user the strategy refuses every name while the D-40 restriction still refuses and records first.
289. **Several approvers from the multipart Request Run form (T-03-28..31).** SPEC 3 (D-37): "the requester designates one or more approvers (form field `approvers`, one user id per entry)". T-03-07 pinned this with a url-encoded POST to `submit` only, but the real Request Run form posts `multipart/form-data` (D-72 lets it upload file parameters; the page form of a job without parameters is multipart as well, as T-03-30's failure message shows), so the encoding a browser actually sends was not covered: with two approvers ticked in a browser, only the last one was stored. The rows repeat T-03-07 as a raw multipart POST shaped as the form posts it (T-03-28 without parameters, T-03-29 with a core file parameter) and through the job's `batch-control/` page in HtmlUnit with JavaScript on, the form submitted by core's own form script (T-03-30 without parameters, T-03-31 with a file chosen). "As the form posts it" was observed, not assumed: a scratch capture of the HtmlUnit submission showed the raw parts `reason`, one `approvers` part per ticked box, core's parameter parts (`name`/`value` pairs, the file renamed `file0`) and last core's structured `json` field (`buildFormTree`) holding reason, approvers and `parameter` (on 8891d0e its `approvers` was `[true,true,false]`, one boolean per checkbox). **Maintainer decision (2026-10-09), documented limitation:** a multipart client that sends repeated `approvers` parts without a `json` field keeps only the last value, because Stapler keeps one value per multipart field name before any plugin code runs; the url-encoded body (T-03-07) and the `json` field (`"approvers": [ids in page order]`, which the fixed form sends) both keep every value. So T-03-28/29 send the raw parts plus the `json` field with `"approvers"` in the same order (T-03-29 also with `"parameter":[{"name":"UPLOAD","file":"file0"},{"name":"DATE","value":"2026-10-01"}]`), every assertion and guard unchanged; no row asserts the lossy no-`json` behaviour. Written from SPEC 3 and 5 (D-37, D-72), the existing T-03-07 setup and fixtures (`ApproverFormFixtures` gains `postMultipart`/`submitRunMultipart(Ok)`, `UsabilityFixtures` gains `approverChoices`/`tickApprovers`; the page form comes from `TypedParameterFixtures.requestRunForm`); no src/main knowledge. "Page order" is read from the form (the order of the `approvers` checkboxes, or multiple-select options, in the document), not assumed; the browser rows untick every other choice so a preselected approver cannot leak in, and T-03-30 ticks a2 before a1 to show that only the page order counts. Every positive assertion is paired with a guard that fails if the set is not really stored: a member who was not sent (a3) cannot decide, and a member of the stored set decides (the first member in T-03-28/30, which the defect drops; the second in T-03-29/31, after which the build must also have received `data.csv`, so a "fix" that stops posting multipart is caught). T-03-30's one-tick guard runs before the two-tick submission, so the red run also shows the browser path works. Red on 8891d0e and again on its merge with 68c1a4c (Temurin 25, Maven 3.9): all four rows fail at the set assertion with `expected: <[a1, a2]> but was: <[a2]>`, T-03-28/29 also with the `json` field (the code before the fix does not read `approvers` from it); T-03-07 and the other 18 rows of the class pass in the same run. Green with the fix (these tests merged with fix/multi-approver-multipart 03fb122): all 23 rows of the class pass, the guard tails included. Not covered: the request dialog (D-66) and the grant request form (`grants/create`) in multipart, and the `changeApprover` form if it is multipart. Non-ASCII user ids on the same form: T-03-32, note 290.
290. **Non-ASCII approver ids on the multipart Request Run form (T-03-32).** Written for a suspected defect from PoC-6 (docs/POC-RESULTS.md on `poc/multipart-filter`, Q2): Stapler decodes a plain multipart part that carries no charset as ISO-8859-1, so `山田` arrives as `å±±ç\u0094°`, while the `json` field is decoded as UTF-8; after #21 the server reads the approvers from the `json` field and also adds the raw `approvers` part. Contract: SPEC 3 (D-37), the stored set is exactly the designated ids, in submission order, each once. This matters only where user ids may be non-ASCII (LDAP, SAML, OIDC); the dummy realm accepts any id, so `山田` is created with `User.getById` and granted BatchControl/Approve, and the approver list names it. One row, four methods: `t_03_32_multipartNonAsciiApproverFirstIsStoredOnce` and `..LastIsStoredOnce` (the T-03-28 shape, `submitRunMultipart`, with [山田, a2] and [a2, 山田]; Stapler keeps one raw value per multipart field name, the last, note 289, so only the second order puts `山田` in the raw channel), `t_03_32_requestRunFormNonAsciiApproverIsStoredOnce` (the real form in HtmlUnit; `山田` configured first, then last, page order read from the form and both sets checked with `assertAll` before the guards) and `t_03_32_urlencodedNonAsciiApproverIsStoredOnce` (the T-03-07 control, both orders). Guards per request: a3 is refused (4xx) and the request stays PENDING; `山田` approves, EXECUTED, `decidedBy` `山田`, one build each. **Fixture correction:** HtmlUnit's `WebRequest` defaults to ISO-8859-1 and turns `山田` into `??` before it leaves the client (the first run refused every case, the url-encoded control included, with `User '??' is not on the configured approver list.`); a browser encodes a Jenkins page's form in UTF-8, so `ApproverFormFixtures.post`/`postMultipart` now set UTF-8 (ASCII values are the same bytes; the multipart text parts still carry no charset header, which the server's ISO-8859-1 reading below confirms). `assertSuccess` now also quotes the page's `role="alert"` texts. **Red on origin/main 2abd14f (Temurin 25, Maven 3.9):** the multipart [a2, 山田] submission and the real form are refused with HTTP 400, `User 'å±±ç\u0094°' is not on the configured approver list.` (the form adds `Nothing was submitted. Correct the fields marked below and submit again; ...`); the page lists the approvers as a1, a2, a3, admin, 山田 whichever position `山田` has in the configured list, so in a browser `山田` is always the last ticked box and cannot be designated at all. Not a garbled duplicate: the garbled id is refused as not eligible before anything is stored. The multipart [山田, a2] submission and the url-encoded control pass, guards included. Expected (owner ui-dev): a multipart submission that carries the `json` field stores exactly the ids of its `"approvers"`, so the raw part must not add an ISO-8859-1 copy (either ignore it when the `json` field is present, or decode it as UTF-8). Not covered: the request dialog (D-66), `grants/create` and `changeApprover` with a non-ASCII id, a non-ASCII requester, and a real LDAP/SAML/OIDC realm.
291. **Storage-fault fixtures and the hostile item name on Windows (maintainer decision 2026-10-09).** The Windows workflow (run 37891753646, windows-latest, JDK 21) failed 35 rows at their fixture, none at an assertion about the plugin. (1) Storage faults: these rows simulate an unreadable or unwritable store by taking a permission away from a file or directory with `File.setReadable`/`setWritable(false, false)` or `Files.setPosixFilePermissions`. On Windows the fault cannot be built: `setReadable(false)` is refused, a directory cannot be made read-only, and NTFS has no POSIX permissions (`UnsupportedOperationException`). `PlatformFixtures.assumeCanMakeUnreadable()` / `assumeCanMakeUnwritable()` decide with a probe, not by the OS name: a scratch directory and file get the same treatment as the fixtures (both mechanisms) and the probe checks that reads, or writes, are then actually refused (computed once per JVM). Each row calls it just before its fixture takes the permission away and is skipped (JUnit assumption) where the probe fails. Unreadable: T-GAP-112, 212, 301, 302, 303, 304, 305, 306, 307, 308, 314, 322, 341, 342, 378, 387, 402, 403, 437 and T-SEC-103. Unwritable: T-GAP-152, 179, 180, 314, 317, 318, 365, 384, 431, T-08-164, T-08-190, T-SEC-93, 95, 100, 104 and 105. On Linux and macOS, run as an ordinary user, every row runs exactly as before; the existing "(assumed)" premise checks stay after the probe. A process running as root is refused nothing, so there the probe skips the rows, as those premises already did. T-GAP-112, 152, 179, 180 and 437 already skipped without POSIX permissions and now use the same probe. (2) Hostile item name: T-08-139 and T-SEC-63 (and T-SEC-64, T-SEC-72, T-08-128, which share MoveRefusalPageTest's setUp) create an item named `x"onmouseover='alert(1)' data-injected="1`; the item's directory carries that name and NTFS forbids `"` (`InvalidPathException`), so the item could not be created. Jenkins' name check forbids `<`, `>`, `&` and the other HTML-special characters, so on NTFS the only quote left is `'`. `PlatformFixtures.HOSTILE_ITEM_NAME` keeps the original name wherever a probe can create a directory whose name contains `"`, and is `x'onmouseover='alert(1)' data-injected='1` otherwise. Every assertion is unchanged and checks the name actually used (the text names it verbatim, no element gains `onmouseover` or `data-injected`, no script holds `alert(1)`), so on NTFS these rows cover a break-out of a single-quoted attribute only; the double-quote break-out stays covered on Linux and macOS. Not covered on Windows: every storage-fault row above.
292. **An approval survives a concurrent read of the request file (T-04-21, Windows CI defect).** On ci.jenkins.io windows-21, T-05-14 and T-05-15 (ApproverJobAccessTest) failed intermittently with "the request must move to EXECUTED, not stay APPROVED (#26)": the store's replace of `requests/run/<id>.xml` by its temporary file was refused (`java.nio.file.AccessDeniedException ...<id>NNNN.tmp -> ...<id>.xml`, `StoreWriteException: The run request <id> could not be saved; nothing was stored.`). Windows refuses to replace or delete a file while another handle has it open without delete-sharing, and `java.io.FileInputStream` opens files exactly that way, so any concurrent reader of the request file could make a status write fail. The contract was frozen between the main session and core-dev (no SPEC acceptance sentence names it; it rests on SPEC 4's store and the SPEC 4절 state machine): while something holds the request's stored file open for reading with a plain `FileInputStream` for about 300-500 ms, an approval still completes (EXECUTED, decidedBy the approver, exactly one build); the store tolerates a transient open of at least about 1 s. P0: a request that stays APPROVED after its run started is the state that startup recovery (SPEC 4, approved but not queued) would queue again. *Synchronisation, so that the hold really overlaps each write.* (A) The approval's write: the executors are set to 0 first, so the build cannot start and the approval's write is the only one in the window. The reader thread opens the file, reads a byte and counts down an `open` latch; the main thread, already logged in and warmed by a GET of the request page, waits for `open`, counts down a `postSent` latch immediately before sending the POST, and the reader starts its 400 ms only after `postSent`. So the file is open before the request leaves and stays open for 400 ms after it left; on macOS the response came back 3-9 ms after sending, far inside the window. A hold ending only when the response arrives is not possible: a fixed store waits for the release, which would then never come. (B) The run-start write: the reader opens the file again and signals, the main thread gives the executors back and schedules queue maintenance, and the reader keeps the file open until `job.getLastBuild()` is non-null and then 400 ms more; the write therefore waits at most about 400 ms plus the build creation time, inside the 1 s tolerance. Three rounds on three jobs. For the Windows run the test logs, per round, the request status the reader saw just before closing and how long after the close the approval answered: on macOS (A) logs APPROVED with the answer about 390 ms before the close and (B) logs EXECUTED (both writes were made while the file was held); on a fixed Windows store (A) is expected to log PENDING with the answer after the close, and (B) APPROVED (the store waited). On an unfixed Windows store the approval's write fails and the row is red at the (A) success or status assertion. Not covered: the values file (`<id>.values.xml`) held open while a run starts (its deletion fails the same way on Windows; the jobs here have no parameters, so there is no values file), and readers other than `FileInputStream`. Green on macOS at commit time (one method, 18.7 s for the class); it cannot be made red outside Windows. The fix (core-dev 5569ae2) is pinned on every system by T-04-22..29, note 293: the store's bounded retry as a unit, and the recovery of an EXECUTED state the store could not write, built with the note 291 fault fixtures.
293. **Bounded Windows retry and recovery of an unsaved EXECUTED state (T-04-22..29, the fix for note 292).** Contract frozen from core-dev's report on 5569ae2 (no SPEC sentence names it; it rests on SPEC 4's store and restart recovery, SPEC 7's approved-run timeout and the SPEC 4절 state machine). (1) `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.store.SharingRetry` (package-private, so the unit test lives in that package): `static <T> T run(Path file, SharingRetry.FileOperation<T> operation, boolean windows) throws IOException`; with `windows` true it retries `AccessDeniedException` or a `FileSystemException` of exactly that class, pausing 10, 20, 40, 80, 160 ms and then 250 ms seven times (12 pauses, about 2,060 ms, 13 attempts) before rethrowing the last refusal; no other `FileSystemException` subclass and no plain `IOException` is retried; with `windows` false one attempt; an interrupt during a pause stops it at once, keeps the flag and rethrows the last refusal. (2) When the approved build starts and the store refuses the EXECUTED write, `RunRequestService.markExecuted` no longer throws, the state stays EXECUTED in memory, the expiry does not end the request as "approved run did not start", and `RunRequestService.retryUnsavedExecutions()` (called by `ExpiryPeriodicWork` every minute) writes it once the store accepts writes. (3) At startup an APPROVED request whose build exists on its job is recorded as EXECUTED instead of only skipped. *Rows.* T-04-25..29 (unit, every OS, the `windows` flag passed in): a fake operation counts attempts and fails N times with a new, numbered exception, so that "the last refusal" is told from the first by identity; the pauses are real time (the contract names no clock for them), asserted with generous bounds (at least 1,800 ms and below 10 s for the full bound; at least 50 ms for the first three pauses; the interrupted worker ends within 1 s, against about 2 s of remaining pauses). T-04-22/23 (integration): the approved run is held in the queue by a label no agent has, `requests/run/` is made read-only (`PlatformFixtures.assumeCanMakeUnwritable()` plus a create-file probe, so the rows are skipped on Windows and as root, note 291), and the label is removed so the build starts against a store that refuses the write; the stored file still saying APPROVED afterwards is the premise that the fault was real. T-04-22 moves the plugin clock past the 60-minute timeout and runs the periodic work twice, once while writes are refused and once after; T-04-23 calls `retryUnsavedExecutions()` directly (under `ACL.SYSTEM2`, as the periodic work runs it). T-04-24 (JenkinsSessionExtension) rewrites the stored file of an executed request to APPROVED without `executedRunId` between the sessions, as T-GAP-124 does, and then also checks the expiry judged from the recovery time. "What the store holds" is read from the stored file (`<status>...</status>`), never from memory; "no expiry" is checked three ways: no `<status>EXPIRED</status>`, no "not start" text (it covers "did not start" and the unfixed store's "Expired: approved but not started within 60 minutes."), and no EXPIRED notice for the request after the 1.5 s quiet period (a capturing notifier). Every positive assertion has a guard: one build, next build number 2 and an empty queue after every step; a second approval refused (T-04-22); a further retry changes nothing (T-04-23). *Red on origin/main e3bde4e* (a scratch worktree with a temporary copy of the class; `retryUnsavedExecutions()` replaced by a periodic-work run, since the API does not exist there): all three integration rows fail at their first distinguishing assertion, T-04-22/23 with "the EXECUTED state stays in effect in memory ... expected: <EXECUTED> but was: <APPROVED>" and T-04-24 with "startup recovery records EXECUTED ... but was: <APPROVED>". With those assertions turned into log lines: in T-04-22 the periodic work at T0+61 while writes were refused threw nothing and changed nothing (memory and disk APPROVED), and at T0+62 the stored file said `EXPIRED` with "Expired: approved but not started within 60 minutes."; in T-04-24 the request was APPROVED in memory and on disk after the restart and past the timeout it ended EXPIRED with an EXPIRED notice to u1. The unit rows cannot compile there (`SharingRetry` does not exist). *Green* with the fix (5569ae2 merged with ae2543d): the 5 unit and 3 integration methods pass on macOS (Temurin 25, Maven 3.10), none skipped, together with T-04-21. Not covered: the retry on a real Windows sharing violation (the unit rows fake the exceptions; T-04-21 is the Windows-only end-to-end row), the values file (`<id>.values.xml`) whose deletion goes through the same retry, a store write refused for a request other than at run start (approve, reject, cancel), `markExecuted` called directly, the one-minute schedule of `ExpiryPeriodicWork` itself (the rows call `doRun()`), and every integration row on Windows or as root (skipped by the note 291 probe).
294. **A refused scripted build answers 4xx, not a redirect to the form (T-06-107, bug hunt B R4-02).** Summary: an API-token `buildWithParameters` or `build` of an approval-required job whose `Accept` lacks `text/html` gets a plain 4xx approval-required refusal; a browser keeps D-60's 303. Reproduced on a real Jenkins (e2e PoC on `poc/bughunt-b`, `e2e/bughunt/b/r4_02_scripted_build.py`): curl and python requests got a 303 to `job/X/batch-control/?p.…`, so `curl -fL` exited 0 with nothing queued, a silent failure (SPEC 6). Contract frozen by the main session: a refused submission whose `Accept` header does not include `text/html` gets an HTTP 4xx carrying the plain approval-required message, no redirect, nothing queued; one whose `Accept` includes `text/html` keeps the 303 to the prefilled Request Run form (D-60). The scripted calls use `java.net.http.HttpClient` (sends no `Accept` unless set; redirects never followed) with u1's API token, so no crumb is involved; the three `Accept` variants and both endpoints are checked with `assertAll`. "Names the approval requirement" is the existing case-insensitive `approv` check (T-06-60); the row does not fix the wording or demand the request URL in the body. Failure on c679b6b: all six scripted answers are HTTP 303 to `scripted-x/batch-control/?p.P=…`; both guards pass. No src/main knowledge.
295. **Non-ASCII text on the multipart Request Run form is read as UTF-8 (T-05-139..141, bug hunt B R4-03).** Summary: a refused multipart Request Run submission re-renders the typed reason exactly and the stored reason (and, without `json`, the raw string parameter) equals the submitted text, in the browser flow and in multipart with and without the `json` field. The refusal used is a submission with no approver ticked (SPEC 3). The bytes are UTF-8 and the text parts carry no part charset, as a browser sends them (`ApproverFormFixtures` conventions, note 290); the browser flow resubmits the re-rendered form without retyping, as the user would. Failure messages quote the ISO-8859-1 reading of the reason so a garbled copy is recognisable. Failure on c679b6b: T-05-139 and T-05-140 re-render `ìë§ ì ì° ì¬ì¤í â Ã¼nÃ¯cÃ¶dÃ©` (the stored reason of T-05-140 is already correct, through `json`); T-05-141 re-renders, stores the reason and stores NOTE garbled; every guard passes. Not covered: a non-ASCII approver id in a multipart body without `json` (the `json` path is T-03-32). No src/main knowledge.
296. **User ids compared with the realm's id strategy in the forms, the grants pages and the window (T-03-33, T-03-34, T-08-194, T-08-195, bug hunt B R4-01).** Summary: a job approver spelled `Approver-1` against the global `approver-1` is offered by the Request Run and change-approver forms, and a user signed in as `LREQUESTER` is `lrequester` for the grants page, the detail page, cancel and the approved window. Reproduced on a real Jenkins (`e2e/bughunt/b/r4_01a_approver_case.py`, `r4_01b_ldap_case.py` on `poc/bughunt-b`): (a) the forms said "No approvers are configured" with no Submit although the service accepted the designation; (b) with LDAP the other-case login saw badge 1 but no row, got 404 on the detail and 403 from its approved window. Contract frozen by the main session: everywhere the plugin compares user ids (UI predicates and GrantService's user comparisons) it uses the realm's id strategy (SPEC 3: "User ids are compared with Jenkins' configured user id strategy, not by plain string equality"). The dummy realm's strategy is case-insensitive (each class asserts it as a premise). `MockAuthorizationStrategy` matches sids literally and matrix-auth's own comparison is not under test, so both spellings get identical entries; only the administrator holds Item/Configure natively. The other-case login is a real sign-in (`WebClient.login("LREQUESTER")`) for the pages and `BatchControlFixtures.token("LREQUESTER")` for the ACL check (an authentication carrying that name; `User.impersonate2` would return the stored spelling). Offered approvers are compared ignoring case, so either spelling passes. Failure on c679b6b: T-03-33 offers `[]` ("No approvers are configured"), T-03-34 offers `[]`, T-08-194 finds no row for LREQUESTER, T-08-195 confers no Configure to LREQUESTER; every guard passes. Not covered: the activation form's approver list, `FilterParser.matchesUser` (history filters) and the pending badge. No src/main knowledge.
297. **An invalidating rename cancels the queued approved run whoever renamed (T-07-12, bug hunt B R2-04).** Summary: when a user who can no longer read the job after renaming it invalidates an approved request whose run waits in the queue, the queued item is still cancelled and never runs. Reproduced on a real Jenkins with the Batch Control role strategy (`e2e/bughunt/b/r2_04_rename.py`, `r2_04_role.yaml`; control `r2_04_control_admin_rename.py` on `poc/bughunt-b`): the request became INVALIDATED but its queue item stayed and later ran, because the queue was read as the renaming user, whose Item/Read filters it. Contract frozen by the main session: when a rename or move invalidates an approved request, its queued item is cancelled regardless of who renamed (queue read and cancel as SYSTEM after core's own permission check, the reason in a comment per CLAUDE.md): INVALIDATED, queue empty, no build even after an executor becomes available. Change control is off as in the reproduction (a window would confer Item/Read and hide the effect). The run waits because the job is restricted to a label no node carries; the test polls (100 ms steps, bounded) for the queue state and never calls `waitUntilNoActivity` while an item may be stuck. Failure on c679b6b: `nightly-old`'s `BuildableItem` is left in the queue after u2's rename; the administrator's rename (guard) cancels its item and the INVALIDATED premise holds. Not covered: a move into a folder by such a user (folders' Item/Move), and the activation-request counterpart. No src/main knowledge.
306. **A run request does not outlive its job (T-07-13..16, #38).** Contract frozen by the main session on 2026-10-10 (Wave A): deleting a job, directly or with a folder above it, ends its PENDING run requests INVALIDATED with a reason that names the deletion (as SPEC 6a already does for activation requests); approving a run request whose job no longer exists, or was re-created under the same name after the request was made, is refused with a 4xx and schedules no build; a job re-created under the old name never receives a build from a request made for the deleted job. SPEC 7 (D-21) and the state machine in SPEC 4 name only rename and move as invalidating events; the contract adds deletion. This is an addition, not a contradiction (SPEC says nothing about a run request whose job is deleted), so no conflict was reported; a SPEC 7 sentence for deletion is advisable (DECISIONS). The reason is checked for "delet" (any case) plus the deleted job's name, or the deleted folder's name, which the job's full name contains. T-07-16 is the missed-event row: the request files are unreadable while the jobs are deleted and re-created (the fixture of note 281), so the refusal at approval cannot rest on the deletion event alone; it pins only the refusal and the absence of a run, not the end state. "A clear message" is pinned only as a 4xx that is not an "Oops!" page; the wording is not. Red on fe83a6d: T-07-13 and T-07-14 `expected: <INVALIDATED> but was: <PENDING>`; T-07-15 and T-07-16 the approval answers HTTP 302 (accepted). Not covered: an APPROVED request whose run waits in the queue when its job is deleted (core removes the queue item with the job), and the activation-request counterpart (covered by T-GAP-111/433). No src/main knowledge.
300. **No store file is written that cannot be read back (T-04-30, T-05-144, T-06a-57, T-08-197..199, T-11-30, T-11-31, bug hunt A R1-01).** Summary: an incident whose log tail held ANSI colour codes no longer vanishes (escape sequences and XML-illegal characters are removed from system text, printable text kept), user text holding an XML-illegal character is refused with a 4xx before anything is stored, and the store itself refuses (`StoreWriteException`) to save such an entity. Written from the frozen R1-01 contract, SPEC 4, 5 ("every stored value ... contains only characters XML can store; a failed save leaves nothing behind"), 6a, 8, 11 and 12 and ARCHITECTURE 5; no src/main knowledge. (1) *Characters.* The forms use U+000B (the reproduction's); the store row also uses U+001B, U+FFFE and an unpaired surrogate. "Allowed" is XML 1.0's set: tab, LF, CR, U+0020..U+D7FF, U+E000..U+FFFD and paired surrogates; the store row's guard round-trips tab, LF and an emoji, so a fix that strips or refuses too much fails. The log-tail row prints the console lines with a `TestBuilder` (no shell, so it runs on every platform) and finds the incident file on disk by its `jobFullName`, so a listing that misses it is the defect and not a missing incident. Which text replaces a removed sequence is not pinned beyond "ERROR failed" (from `ESC[31mERROR ESC[0m failed`) and the printable words around a bell and a vertical tab; whether the incident page and CSV show the stripped text is pinned only for the page ("ERROR failed"). (2) *"Nothing is stored".* Pinned as the entity file byte for byte unchanged (decisions, incident actions) or no new id and no file naming the request (submissions); "a clear message" as `UsabilityFixtures.assertPlainRefusal` (no crash page or stack trace) naming the cause in plain words (`character|control|not allowed|invalid|unsupported`). (3) *Surfaces that pass on main.* T-05-144: the run-request decision comment is already refused (the contract says run-request input already uses `store/XmlChars`); it stays as a regression guard. T-08-199: the contract lists "revoke reasons", but on main neither revoke endpoint (`grants/active/<id>/revoke`, `grants/<id>/revoke`) stores any user text (probed: a `reason`, `comment`, `revokeReason` or `revokedReason` parameter is not stored; the window's reason is the plugin's own, D-63), so there is no user text to refuse; the row pins that a junk parameter is never stored and the ended window stays readable, and it changes if a revoke reason field is ever added (that field then falls under T-08-197's rule). (4) *Not covered.* Other system text than the log tail (for example parameter values in run records, which are JSONL and not XML) and the entities without a public save path in tests (incidents, grants, activation states) at the store level; the last-line-of-defence row covers the two entities the tests can save directly.
304. **Run records carry the time they were appended (T-10-14, T-12-16, bug hunt A R1-02, D-81).** Summary: each new line of `runs/YYYY-MM.jsonl` has `appendedAt` (epoch millis of the append on the plugin clock), and a date-filtered listing stops on it, so a run whose record was appended late no longer hides the runs appended before it: the History listing for the day matches `runs.csv`. Written from D-81, SPEC 4, 10 and 12 and ARCHITECTURE 2 and 5; no src/main knowledge. (1) *Why two rows.* A run's start time and duration are Jenkins' own and cannot be moved by `BatchClock`, so a day boundary between two real runs more than 60 s apart would need a minute of real waiting. T-12-16 therefore builds the defect's file through the store's public append (`FileStore.appendRunRecord`, the store's own line format) with the plugin clock set to each append instant, and T-10-14 shows with two real runs, a test `RunListener` holding one in `onCompleted` and the plugin clock moved forward, that the listener path writes `appendedAt` as the instant of the append and not start + duration. Together they cover the contract end to end without a real wait. (2) *Frozen expectations.* `appendedAt` is the plugin clock's `millis()` at the append (both rows compare it exactly), written by the store for every new run line, whichever caller appends it. The D-1 listing guard proves the period still filters by start time (an implementation filtering by `appendedAt` would list `r102-slow` on D); the CSV guard proves the export was always complete. Lines without `appendedAt` keep the old estimate (D-81); no row pins that the old estimate still drops runs, because that is the defect, not a contract. (3) *Fixture change.* `StoreDataFixtures.RunLine.render` now replaces the `appendedAt` of the template line (the plugin clock when the template was made, 2001 in BoundedReadTest) with the generated record's start + 777 ms; without it every generated line would claim one append instant, and the bounded-read and paging rows (BoundedReadTest, DashboardLimitTest, OversizedLineTest, RetentionGapTest, StoreReadGapTest, StoreReadRegressionTest) would stop at the first line or read a whole month. A template without the field (main before the fix) renders exactly as before. (4) *Not covered.* That the scan with `appendedAt` still stops early (bounded reads, #13, the reason D-81 rejected reading the whole month) is left to the existing bounded-read rows, which now generate lines with `appendedAt`.
298. **An approved request whose queued run was cancelled does not say "starts shortly" (T-05-142, T-05-143, bug hunt B R2-05).** Summary: once the approved run's queue item is cancelled, through the queue or by disabling the job (D-55), the request page says the queued run was cancelled and will not start instead of "starts shortly". Reproduced on a real Jenkins (`e2e/bughunt/b/r2_05_cancelled_queue_notice.py` on `poc/bughunt-b`). Contract frozen by the main session: after the cancel the request page does not contain "starts shortly" and contains "cancelled" (SPEC 5, D-74: the request stays APPROVED and is never submitted again). The run waits because the job is restricted to a label no node carries; the queue state is polled (bounded). The guard (the page says "starts shortly" and not "cancelled" while the run waits) makes the negative check meaningful; both phrases are compared case-insensitively on the normalised page text. Failure on c679b6b: T-05-142's page still says "the run starts shortly" and never "cancelled"; T-05-143's page says "approved (waiting: the job is disabled)" without "cancelled" (its "starts shortly" check already passes); guards and premises pass. For the human: D-55 says a request approved before the job was disabled "shows that it waits because the job is disabled", while core's disable removes the queued run and D-74 never submits it again, so after re-enabling it will not start; the contract's "cancelled" wording resolves that, but D-55's sentence may deserve a look (proposal only, no change made). No src/main knowledge.
302. **A job's sub-items follow the parent job's run control (T-06a-58..62, bug hunt A R2-02 and R2-01, D-82).** Summary: a matrix configuration has no activation or approval state of its own; the queue gate applies the parent's approval property and activation, so an activated matrix project's runs run their configurations, a direct configuration build is refused like the parent's, and a configuration offers no activation notice, activation form or run request of its own (its request form and submit point to the parent). Written from D-82, SPEC 1, 2, 5, 6 and 6a; no src/main knowledge. (1) *Dependency.* matrix-project is on the test class path transitively (existing rows already use it, ItemScopeSubmissionTest); it is not declared in `pom.xml` (see the report's Request line). Maven modules, the other sub-item kind D-82 names, are not covered: the Maven plugin is not a test dependency (as in note 260). (2) *Frozen expectations.* T-06a-58 runs all three entry points the contract names (Build Now, timer, approved run) on one activated project and reads every configuration run's result; the never-activated `mx-off` guard shows the gate still applies the parent's activation rather than passing every matrix run. T-06a-59 does not pin the status code of the refusal, because the parent's own answer to a refused API build is the subject of bug hunt B R4-02 (T-06-107); it pins "not 2xx", "equal to the parent's answer" and the blocking triple on the configuration, and its run-control-off guard shows the refusal is Batch Control's (SPEC 1). T-06a-60 uses the activation screen contract of note 96 (the wording "not activated"/"on hold" and the link target `batch-control-activation`), with the parent's page as the premise in the same row. T-06a-61 and T-06a-62 were added at the coordinator's request. Of the two instructions about a run request on a configuration, the later one is the implemented screen contract of ui-dev: the per-job request and activation actions are absent on a configuration (their forms, the dialog and both submits answer 404, as SPEC 2 #31 makes an action absent rather than refused), and the configuration page points to the parent through a sub-item notice (containing "part of" and linking to the parent). The pointer "request it on '<parent>'" of the earlier instruction is therefore pinned on core-dev's service refusal (`RunRequestService.create` for a configuration throws a `RuntimeException` whose message holds "request it on" and the parent's name), and nothing is stored on either path. T-06a-62 reads the entries by caption (the T-UI-09 and T-UI-16 contracts), the approval notice as the T-06-56 notice (an element of the main panel naming "manual" and "approv", note 116) and the sub-item notice as the innermost main-panel element saying "part of" with a link to `job/mx/` within it or up to three levels above; the parent's forms, entries and notice are its premise and guard, so an implementation that hid them everywhere fails. (3) *Not covered.* A configuration of a parent that is approved but not activated (whether its configurations pass is not stated by D-82 beyond "the parent's run starts its configurations"), and upstream causes on a configuration.
308. **The deprecated `Cause.UserCause` is a human submission, exactly like `UserIdCause` (T-06-108, T-06-109, #37).** Contract frozen by the main session on 2026-10-10 (Wave A): a queue submission of an approval-required, activated job whose only cause is `Cause.UserCause` is refused with the same refusal and record as a `UserIdCause` submission. Consistent with SPEC 6 (every manual run without an approved request is refused at queue entry) and SPEC 6a (only causes that are not a human submission are judged by activation); no conflict. Both causes are made while authenticated as u1, as a script or plugin running for that user would make them (`new Cause.UserCause()` records the current authentication's name); a SYSTEM-authored cause is the separate T-06a-54 rule and is not pinned here for `UserCause`. "The same refusal" is pinned as the same form: both `scheduleBuild2` calls return null, or both throw the same exception class with the same message once the job name is replaced; "the same record" as the same number of new change records per `ChangeType` on the job (none on fe83a6d). T-06-109 is a parity guard and green on fe83a6d: a `UserCause` on a job that needs no approval is not sent to the activation check, so the fix must not over-block. Red on fe83a6d: T-06-108 `expected: <hudson.model.Failure: Approval required: job '<job>' only runs through an approved batch-control run request. Submit a run request at http://localhost:<port>/jenkins/job/<job>/batch-control/ and wait for approval.> but was: <accepted>`. Not covered: a `UserCause` combined with other causes, and the CLI or script-console path (the e2e unit). No src/main knowledge.
309. **Every submission form stores a value for every parameter (T-05-145..148, #40).** Contract frozen by the main session on 2026-10-10 (Wave A): whatever the submission form (urlencoded, multipart, or a `json` blob with all, some or none of the parameters), the stored request holds a value for every parameter the job defines, a missing one as the job's default at request time, stated explicitly; the approver sees all of them; the approved build runs with exactly the stored values even if the job's defaults change after the request. Consistent with SPEC 5 (the approved build's parameters match the stored ones exactly; no path changes them after approval) and the S-10 rows T-SEC-44/45; no conflict. "Stored" is read from `RunRequest.getParameters()` (the masked display map derived at submission, D-72) and compared as an exact map, so an extra or missing key fails; "the approver sees" is a1's `batch-control/requests/<id>/` page containing the names and values and not "No parameters." (the text named in the issue). The defaults are changed after the request by replacing the job's parameters property (DATE 1999-12-31; MODE choices reordered so the default becomes partial), so a build that took the default at build time would show it. Each row's guard runs first on the same job and passes on fe83a6d. T-05-148 (multipart, no `json`) is green on fe83a6d by design. Red on fe83a6d: T-05-145 `expected: <{DATE=2000-01-01, MODE=full}> but was: <{}>`; T-05-146 `expected: <{DATE=2026-09-01, MODE=full}> but was: <{DATE=2026-09-01}>`; T-05-147 `expected: <{DATE=2000-01-01, MODE=full}> but was: <{}>`. Not covered: typed parameters other than string and choice (file, password, credentials) in a partial json, and the dialog on the new job page (D-60 prefill). While writing these rows the author's search for the "No parameters." text also listed two `src/main/resources` jelly files by name; nothing else under `src/main` was read and the rows follow the issue text. No src/main knowledge.
299. **An Item/Read or Discover check never blocks on the GrantService monitor (T-08-196, bug hunt B R3-04).** Summary: with another thread holding `synchronized (GrantService.get())`, an item's Read and Discover checks answer within 1 s, and the D-35c creating grant still confers Read. Reproduced on a real Jenkins (`e2e/bughunt/b/r3_04_grant_scan_perf.py` on `poc/bughunt-b`): with 20,000 ended grants, 20 parallel job-list requests took a median 527 ms against 84 ms with change control off, the threads BLOCKED on GrantService, because each Read check took the monitor and scanned every retained grant. Contract frozen by the main session (corrected: GrantService is a static singleton, not an extension; `GrantService.get()`, whose synchronized methods lock that instance): an Item/Read (and Discover) check never blocks on the monitor and does not iterate ended grants; results unchanged. *Determinism.* The holder thread takes the monitor and counts down a latch, then waits on a second latch (a latch wait keeps the monitor) for at most 3 s; only after the first latch does a second thread run the four checks, and the test waits for them with `Future.get(1, SECONDS)`; it also asserts the holder is still alive when they answer, and releases and joins it in `finally`. No sleep decides anything. The role strategy is used because requesting a window needs to read its item: an item role whose pattern is exactly `team` lets maker read the folder and nothing inside it (premise checked on an administrator's `team/other`), so maker's Read on `team/made` can only come from the D-35c creating grant. Failure on c679b6b: the checks do not answer within 1 s while the monitor is held; all guards pass. Not covered: the "does not iterate ended grants" half as such (a time bound with many ended grants would depend on the machine) and the same check under the matrix variant. No src/main knowledge.
301. **A failed change-record append never stops or reverses the switch change (T-01-17..19, T-02-126, bug hunt A R3-01).** Summary: with `batch-control/changes/` unwritable, turning change control off through the form, the direct setter or JCasC at boot completes (off in memory and on disk, every open window revoked, no 500, no exception, Jenkins starts) and "Mark as reviewed" applies the review; the failure is logged at WARNING or SEVERE. Written from the frozen R3-01 contract, SPEC 1 (side effects run once the new state is durable; D-42 the direct setter never throws), SPEC 2 (D-58b review, JCasC round trip), P-15, D-63 and ARCHITECTURE 5; no src/main knowledge. (1) *The fault.* A new fixture, `RecordFaultFixtures.makeUnwritable`, makes `changes/` and everything below it unwritable (directories `r-xr-xr-x`, files `r--r--r--`) and proves it by a refused file creation and a refused append to an existing month file; it skips the row where the platform cannot refuse its owner a write (note 291), and its handle restores the permissions. The global configuration file stays writable, so these rows are the opposite case of T-01-07 (the save fails) and T-01-11/12 (the configuration file fails): here the save succeeds and only the record fails. (2) *What is asserted.* "Saved" is read back with `BatchControlGlobalConfiguration.load()`; "revoked" is `hasActiveGrant` false, the window absent from `listActive()` and `<revokedAt` in `grants/<id>.xml`; the "they confer again when change control is turned back on" half of the defect is pinned by turning change control on again once the directory is writable and expecting u1's `config.xml` POST to answer 403. The log is captured with `LogRecorder` on `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol` at WARNING. Whether the form shows a warning that the record could not be written is allowed by the contract and not pinned. The CONFIG_TOGGLE and GRANT_REVOKE records cannot be written in these rows, so their absence is not asserted either way. (3) *Guards.* T-01-08 is the same form submission without the fault (toggle recorded, window revoked); each row also asserts its premise (the window active and conferring, the item listed in `changedItems`, the monitor active) before the fault. (4) *Not covered.* `GrantService.clearStaleEntry` (the contract names it with `markReviewed`) has no black-box trigger short of the vanished-item path of T-SEC-112 (an item removed on disk, a reload and the periodic work), whose record, if any, is not documented; it is left to code review. A JCasC apply at runtime with the record failing is T-01-18's setter path, which JCasC calls.
307. **An approval racing the change-control switch-off leaves no window (T-01-20, #39).** Contract frozen by the main session on 2026-10-10 (Wave A): after a switch-off has returned, no permission window is active and none becomes active; an approval that overlaps the switch-off is either refused with the "change control is off" refusal or registers a window that the switch-off revokes; either way turning change control back on confers nothing from it (LIMITATIONS 34, "the off period accumulates nothing"). Consistent with SPEC 1 (revoking the active grants is a side effect of turning change control off; the direct setter applies the value, D-42); no conflict. The race is timing-dependent, so the row is a black-box stress test through the service API and the direct setter, the documented script-console path (each setter call takes about 1 s here, so a round costs about 2 s and the row about 2.3 min). The switch-off thread is delayed by a sweep of 0 to 3.1 ms in 0.1 ms steps, two passes, because the losing interleaving (the approval's switch check before the flag flips, its window registered after the revocation) is narrow; on the author's machine it was hit at delays between 0.3 and 1.5 ms. A violation is any of: a window of u1 listed active or `hasActiveGrant` true after both calls returned, `hasActiveGrant` true or u1's ACL granting Item/Configure on `batch-x` after the setter turned change control back on. Violating windows are revoked so the rounds stay independent, and all violations are reported together. Refusals are checked to name "change control" (on fe83a6d every refusal did: 12 to 15 per run). Red on fe83a6d in 4 of 4 runs of the committed configuration (5, 6, 2 and 5 violating rounds of 64; every violation an accepted approval whose window stayed active and conferred after switching back on; an earlier 0.25 ms-step sweep gave 4 of 64). A fixed build must pass every run. Not covered: the global configuration form as the switch-off path, and the same race on a web approval (`grants/<id>/approve`). No src/main knowledge.
305. **A failed change-record append never breaks the operation it records: activation decisions, the D-59a hold, the closed Grants refusal and the D-48 report (T-02-127, T-02-128, T-06a-66..68, T-08-200, bug hunt A, follow-up of R3-01).** Summary: with `batch-control/changes/` unwritable, approving an ACTIVATE or HOLD still applies it, invalidates the job's other pending requests and notifies; a non-administrator's move still holds and locks the job; a grant request while change control is off is still refused with 4xx and its message; a creation payload's or copy's authorization property is still removed and reported with the D-48 403; each failure is logged at WARNING or SEVERE. Written from the R3-01 / D-42 contract as relayed by the main session (a failure to append the change record never stops, reverses or half-applies the operation it records; it is logged at WARNING or above; the request does not answer 500), SPEC 2 (D-35c, D-48), SPEC 6a (ACTIVATE/HOLD, D-59a, security-13), SPEC 8 (D-59), SPEC 9, LIMITATIONS 29 and ARCHITECTURE 5; no src/main knowledge. (1) *Fault and guards.* The fault is note 301's `RecordFaultFixtures.makeUnwritable` (skipped where the platform cannot refuse its owner a write, note 291). Every row first runs the same flow on another item with a writable store and asserts its full positive outcome, so a red row is red because of the fault. Records that cannot be written (ACTIVATED, HELD, MOVE, GRANT_REQUEST_BLOCKED, GRANT_VIOLATION, CREATE) are not asserted either way under the fault. (2) *Red on origin/bh/r3-01 (03c73bc), macOS, JDK 25.* T-06a-66 and T-06a-67: the approval answers HTTP 500. T-06a-68: the move answers below 400 and the job is no longer activated, but the D-34 lock is not applied (`approvalRequired` stays false): half applied. T-08-200: HTTP 500 "Oops!" instead of the refusal. T-02-127: `createItem` answers 200 with an empty body instead of the D-48 403 (the property is removed, the user is not told); T-02-128: the copy answers 200 with the copy's configuration page. All guards pass. (3) *Item 4 of the scenario ("a user whose Configure comes only from a grant changes an item's authorization property").* A throwaway probe (not committed) found the D-35b save paths already fine under the fault on the base: a job's `config.xml` POST, the job configuration form, a folder's `config.xml` POST and a direct API save as bob all revert the entry, keep the other changes and (over HTTP) answer the D-48 403, with the failed GRANT_VIOLATION logged at SEVERE. The defect is on the D-35c creation paths (`createItem` with a payload, a copy), so rows T-02-127/128 pin those; no row pins the passing D-35b paths, because every row here must be red on the base. (4) *Not covered.* Whether the approval notification is sent is observed through a capturing `BatchControlNotifier` test extension, not through mail. A HOLD and an ACTIVATE cannot be pending together on one job (the form refuses a HOLD for a job that is not activated and an ACTIVATE for one that is), so the S-13-07 invalidation is asserted for requests of the same action only. A move through the folders plugin's UI form (as opposed to `POST <item>/move/move`), a folder moved by a non-administrator, and a Pipeline build's reverted save are not repeated under the fault.
303. **Activation identity survives a copy of JENKINS_HOME (T-GAP-113 inverted, T-06a-63..65, bug hunt A R2-03, D-80).** Summary: the activation state stores the id of a marker file kept in the job's directory instead of the directory's file key, so a job directory replaced by a copy of itself (a restore, a volume move) stays activated, while a job re-created under a deleted job's name, a Jenkins copy and a restored directory without the marker start not activated. Written from D-80, SPEC 6a (security-13, fails closed) and ARCHITECTURE 5; no src/main knowledge. (1) *A changed contract, not a loosened assertion.* T-GAP-113 asserted that a directory replaced by a copy of itself starts not activated (note 276 read it as a job re-created outside Jenkins); D-80 (owner decision, 2026-10-09) rules the opposite for a copy that keeps the marker, so the row, its test (`t_gap_113_replacedJobDirectoryKeepsItsActivation`) and the note 276 sentence are inverted, and the row is raised to P0 (a restore silently stopping every timer is the defect). The fixture now copies to a temporary directory, deletes the original and copies back (as the coordinator specified), and the row adds a new-file-key premise where the platform has file keys, an upstream run and the job page. (2) *The guards keep security-13.* T-06a-63 deletes the directory on disk while the stored state stays behind and re-creates the job under the same name; T-06a-64 uses `Jenkins.copy`; both pass on main (the file key protected them) and must keep passing with the marker. T-06a-65 is the coordinator's guard: the marker name `.batch-control-activation-id` comes from core-dev's implementation of D-80 and ARCHITECTURE 5 on PR #46, and the row uses it only to delete the file from the restored copy (premise: the file exists, which is where it fails on main); the copy that keeps it is the in-row guard. (3) *Comment fixed.* `FailClosedGapTest` (T-GAP-437) said the identity is the directory's file key (D-71b); its comment now names the D-80 marker; the assertions are unchanged (an unsearchable parent makes the marker unreadable, which fails closed). (4) *Not covered.* An unreadable (rather than missing) marker is covered only through T-GAP-437's unsearchable parent, because the coordinator limited the use of the marker's name to deleting it; activation states written with a file key are not converted (D-69), and no row plants such a state.
340. **An activation decision that cannot be saved is refused before anything changes (T-06a-108..110, issue #36).** Summary: approving an ACTIVATE or HOLD request leaves memory, the activation-state file and the request status consistent, also across a restart; when `batch-control/activations/` refuses writes, the approval is refused with a 4xx/5xx answer saying the decision could not be saved (not the "Oops!" page), the request stays PENDING, memory and the state file keep the old state, the job's other pending requests are not invalidated, no ACTIVATED or HELD record is written, and once the directory is writable again the same approval works normally. Written from SPEC 6a (ACTIVATE/HOLD records, security-13 fails closed and S-13-07 invalidation), SPEC 4 (restart durability), the SPEC 6 Usability line, ARCHITECTURE 5 (`activations/<encoded job full name>.xml`, requests in `activation-requests/`), issue #36 and the wave-B contract (main session, 2026-10-10); no src/main knowledge. (1) *Fault.* `activations/` and every file in it become read-only (`r-xr-xr-x` / `r--r--r--`, proven by a refused create, restored in `finally`); the request directory stays writable, so only the state write fails. Skipped where the platform cannot refuse its owner a write (Windows, root; note 291), like the other storage-fault rows. (2) *Red on origin/main 16ecbc5 (macOS, JDK 25), first reproduction of #36.* The approval already answers HTTP 400 with a "could not be saved" message, but the request is APPROVED (T-06a-108, T-06a-110: "expected PENDING but was APPROVED"); T-06a-109: before the restart the page said "not activated / on hold" and memory said not activated, after the restart the job is activated again (the hold is undone). (3) *Not covered.* Notifications under the fault, a HOLD of a job inside a folder, and an unreadable (rather than unwritable) state file.
341. **Store writes are forced to disk (T-04-70..72, issue #34).** Summary: every store write that replaces a file forces its temporary file before the atomic rename and forces the directory after it where the platform allows, and every append that records a revocation or a decision is forced before the operation answers; behaviour is otherwise unchanged. Written from SPEC 4 (restart durability, append-only records), SPEC 8 (a revoked window confers nothing), ARCHITECTURE 5 (tmp → rename writes and the store layout), issue #34 and the wave-B contract (main session, 2026-10-10); no src/main knowledge. (1) *How a force is observed.* A power loss cannot be simulated in JenkinsRule. The rows instead record the JDK's Flight Recorder event `jdk.FileForce` (threshold 0, all threads) around one operation: the JDK emits it for every `FileChannel.force` call with the channel's path (checked on JDK 17 and 25; JDK 21 emits it through the same instrumentation as 17). Each window first forces a scratch file and requires that event (premise), so a red row is never a recorder failure; on main the same windows also show core's own `AtomicFileWriter` forces (`users/<id>/config.xml-atomic…tmp` and its directory), which confirms the method. A forced temporary file is recognised black-box as a forced file in the target's directory that no longer exists once the operation has answered (it was renamed onto the target), a forced directory as an event whose path is the directory, a forced append as an event on `changes/YYYY-MM.jsonl`. The directory assertions run only where a probe can force a scratch directory (not on Windows); the rows need no storage fault, so they run on Windows too. (2) *What this constrains.* `FileDescriptor.sync()` emits no `jdk.FileForce` event, so the fix must force through `FileChannel.force` (as core's `AtomicFileWriter` does), and the temporary file must live in the target's directory (as ARCHITECTURE 5's tmp → rename and note 292 already describe). (3) *Red on origin/main 16ecbc5 (macOS, JDK 25), first reproduction of #34.* T-04-70 and T-04-71 fail at their first assertion with no forced path under `batch-control/` at all ("forced store paths: []", while 5 and 11 core paths were forced in the same windows). T-04-72 is the guard and passes. (4) *Not covered.* Durability itself (a crash between the write and the force) is not observable in-process; incidents, run records and the other append types are not observed; whether the force precedes the success answer is asserted only as "inside the operation's window".
342. **A case-only rename keeps the job's activation (T-06a-112, T-06a-113, issue #32).** Summary: after a script or Job DSL changes only the case of a job's or a folder's name (`Job.renameTo` / `AbstractItem.renameTo`; the UI refuses it), the job is still activated, also across a restart, and its timer and upstream runs still pass when it was activated with both switches cleared. Written from SPEC 6a ("renaming or moving a job keeps its activation"; the D-46 gate; the job page shows the state), SPEC 4 (restart), ARCHITECTURE 5 ("Rename/move relocates the state file"), issue #32 and the wave-B contract (main session, 2026-10-10); no src/main knowledge. (1) *File system.* The defect needs a case-insensitive file system (default APFS, NTFS), where the old and the new state file are the same file. Each row probes `JENKINS_HOME` (a file created and looked up under its lower-case name, `Files.isSameFile`), prints the kind and names it in every assertion message, and asserts the same behaviour on both kinds: on Linux CI (case-sensitive) the rows are the guard. Each row also renames a second activated job (or folder) to a different name, which keeps its activation everywhere, so a red row is red because the rename was case-only. (2) *Red on origin/main 16ecbc5 on this macOS machine (default APFS, case-insensitive, JDK 25), first reproduction of #32.* Both rows: the job is activated and its timer runs right after the rename, but after the restart "nightly ... must still be activated after the restart ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>" (and the same for `team/etl`). The non-case guards pass. The same commit run from a case-sensitive APFS disk image passes both rows (2 tests, 0 failures), so on Linux CI they pass on main as guards. (3) *Not covered.* A case-only rename through Job DSL itself (the rows call `renameTo` as a script would), a move whose destination differs only in case, and Windows (expected red there as on macOS, not run here).
343. **A date-range query does not depend on the default time zone (T-04-74, T-04-75, issue #33).** Summary: the History listings and the CSV exports of run records and change records return every record whose timestamp lies in the requested days and no record outside them, whatever the JVM default time zone was when the record was written and is when it is read; files written before the zone changed keep working without migration. Written from SPEC 4 ("stored file names, month bucket names and record ids do not depend on the controller's default locale or time zone ... so retention and the history screens keep working"; "Dates on screens are rendered in the plugin clock's zone"; screens and exports never silently disagree), SPEC 12, SPEC 9, ARCHITECTURE 5 (month files), issue #33 and the wave-B contract (main session, 2026-10-10); no src/main knowledge. SPEC check: no conflict; SPEC 4 already says bucket names do not depend on the default time zone, and the plugin clock's zone is the system default zone (issue #33), so a zone change between restarts changes the buckets new records go to. (1) *Fixture.* The zone change is a restart with another `TimeZone.setDefault` between the `JenkinsSessionExtension` sessions (restored in `@AfterEach`, with `BatchClock.reset()`). In each session the plugin clock is fixed through `BatchClock.setForTest` at an instant in that session's default zone, as a fresh JVM's clock would be. The requested days are days in the plugin clock's zone, the zone the screens render dates in; a fix that read the filter in another fixed zone would show a record under a date its own filter does not return. (2) *Red on origin/main 16ecbc5 (macOS, JDK 25), first reproduction of #33.* Both rows fail on all four surfaces ("wrong on [runs listing, runs.csv, changes listing, changes.csv]"); the guards (mid-month record, out-of-range day) and the premise (a range spanning both months lists the record, so it is stored and readable) pass. (3) *Not covered.* Incidents (`incidents/index/YYYY-MM.jsonl`), the request history, the monthly summary counters, retention across a zone change, and the default 7-day window without explicit dates.
328. **CSV exports start with the UTF-8 byte order mark (T-12-37..41, #43, D-85).** Written from SPEC 12 (the four exports: runs, incidents, changes, requests; 403 without ViewHistory), SPEC 2 (#31: a user without any Batch Control permission gets 404, so the 403 guard uses a Request holder), SPEC 13 (D-37: `decidedBy` in `requests.csv`), issue #43 and the Wave C-UI contract of 2026-10-10 (owner decision "BOM by default", to be recorded as D-85: every CSV export starts with EF BB BF followed by the header row; the content type stays `text/csv; charset=UTF-8`; non-ASCII values are UTF-8); no src/main knowledge. *SPEC check:* SPEC does not describe the CSV byte format (no sentence on a BOM, the charset or the first line), so there is no conflict; "CSV exports keep their existing columns" (D-37) is not affected, since the columns and their order stay, and the BOM before the first header name is the trade-off the owner accepted (LIMITATIONS, release-manager). The raw bytes are read with `WebResponse.getContentAsStream()`, because a decoded string may already have lost the BOM. Each row checks "exactly one BOM, directly followed by the header row" (no doubled BOM, no blank first line). *Existing tests:* `ApproverCsvExportTest` already strips U+FEFF from header names; no other test was found comparing the first header cell, but a test that reads the first column name with `getContentAsString()` may see U+FEFF after the fix. Red on d003d10: every row fails with "the first bytes are 72 75 6e 49 64 2c ... (runs.csv: `runId,jobFullName`; requests.csv: `id,jobFullName,p`; changes.csv: `id,type,target,u`; incidents.csv: `id,runId,jobFullName`), not EF BB BF"; the guards pass.
362. **One decision box after Parameters; 7-column run tables (T-UI-270..291, Wave D D3, #18.5, #6, #18.1).** Written from the Wave D contract (D3, frozen 2026-10-10), issues #6 and #18, SPEC 5, 6, 10, 11 and D-55, and pages rendered on origin/main (d80e5fe); no src/main knowledge. (1) *Decision section.* On main the request page's headings were Reason, Parameters, Recent Runs of This Job, Approver Changes, Decision, and the section held two forms (`approve` with "Comment (optional)", `reject` with "Rejection comment (required)"), so two `comment` boxes. `DecisionAreaFixtures` reads the section as everything after the `h2` "Decision" up to the next `h2` (XPath `preceding::h2[1]`), finds Approve and Reject by caption and resolves a button's target from its `formaction` or its form's action, so a single form with `formaction` on Reject and two forms side by side both pass. Decisions are made by pressing the buttons in a JavaScript-enabled client (crumb as in a browser), so a `formaction` broken by core's form scripts fails T-UI-272/273. (2) *Refusal.* On main a blank reject comment answers 400 with the page re-rendered, the text kept in the reject box and `data-batch-control-field-error="comment"` next to it; T-UI-274 requires the same next to the one box ("next to" = inside the box's parent or grandparent). (3) *Incident tables.* The contract lists "History runs and incidents, Incidents list" among the tables that "shrink from 10 to 7 columns", but the incident tables had 6 columns (Incident, Run, Job, Result, Status, Created) and hold no cause, parameters or duration. T-UI-284 reads this as: the incident tables use the same Run cell (icon with tooltip, job link, `#n` link) and drop the separate Job and Result columns; nothing else about them is pinned. 326. **Run links of matrix configurations resolve (T-UI-143..145, #42).** Written from SPEC 6 (usability: "no link leads to a 404 or 403 page"), SPEC 10 (every job's runs on one screen), SPEC 11 (an incident for every listed result, whatever the cause), issue #42 and the Wave C-UI contract of 2026-10-10 ("every run link on History, the Run Dashboard and Incidents resolves (HTTP 200) ... the link uses the resolved job's own URL"); no src/main knowledge. A run link is an anchor whose percent-decoded path below the Jenkins root matches `job/.../<n>`; the expected URL is core's `Run#getUrl()` (`job/mx/X=a/1/`, premise asserted), compared after percent-decoding. The viewer is the administrator, so SPEC 6's plain-text rule for a job the viewer cannot read does not apply. The jobs are activated through the request flow (`BatchControlFixtures.activateAsAdmin`, D-46) because `buildAndAssertStatus` submits a cause-less build. Each row checks its guard first (the freestyle job, the folder job and the matrix parent, which resolve today) and then collects every problem on every page into one message. *Not covered:* a Maven module, because `maven-plugin` is not on the test class path (pom.xml belongs to release-manager; Request to release-manager if the owner wants it covered). Red on fe83a6d: all three rows fail for the configurations only, with "no link to mx/X=a#1 at its own URL job/mx/X=a/1/ (run links on the page: [.../job/mx/job/X=b/1/, .../job/mx/job/X=a/1/, .../job/mx/1/, .../job/ops/job/in-x/1/, .../job/fs-x/1/])" and ".../job/mx/job/X=a/1/ answers 404" on History, the dashboard, the incident detail pages and the Incidents list.
