Rows are identified by the request ids linked from `table[data-batch-control-list=pending|ended]` (as T-UI-102). Both directions are checked on each page, and the behavioural check (the kept list still shows its page 2 after following the link) is asserted next to the href check. *Fixture note:* the activations rows file their ACTIVATE requests on one job and fall back to a fresh job only if the service refuses another pending request there (on fe83a6d it accepts several), because each job save took 1 to 2 s on the test machine; the row does not measure whether one job may hold several pending ACTIVATE requests. *Not covered:* `activePage` (it would need more than one page of active windows or approved-but-not-started requests); the same rule applies and the fix is expected to keep it as well. Red on fe83a6d: all three rows fail with "on batch-control/<page>/?pendingPage=2 the ended pager link /jenkins/batch-control/<page>/?endedPage=2 drops pendingPage=2" and "following ... moved the pending list off its page 2", and the mirror; the guards pass.
361. **History filter dropdowns, readable status labels and status colour badges (T-UI-250..269j, Wave D D2, #18.3, #18.2).** Written from the Wave D contract (D2, frozen 2026-10-10), issue #18 and pages rendered on origin/main (d80e5fe); no src/main knowledge. (1) *Dropdowns.* On main the filter form held free-text `result` (placeholder "SUCCESS") and `status` (placeholder "OPEN") fields on every kind. The rows require `select` elements styled as core's `jenkins-select` (the class on the select, `jenkins-select__input`, or on a wrapper up to the form), first option `Any` with an empty value, option values the enum names. Which results the Result dropdown lists is not in the contract: the rows require SUCCESS, UNSTABLE, FAILURE and ABORTED and that every value is a `hudson.model.Result` name (NOT_BUILT may or may not be listed). The option texts are not pinned (they may be labels). Changes offer neither filter ("Result is offered for runs and incidents, Status for incidents and requests"). (2) *Kept input.* The hand-edited values `WEIRD<b>x</b>` and `bogus"q` check that the extra option's value is exactly the typed text, in an element and in an attribute; the page answered 200 on main for both. (3) *Labels.* The hook `data-batch-control-status` already exists on main on some list rows (the activations ended list carries `data-batch-control-status="REJECTED"` with the raw text `REJECTED`), so the rows require, per page, at least one hooked element per status whose visible text does not contain the raw name, the contract's example wording where it gives one, and no raw name as a word in any table of the page (filter forms are not tables, so dropdown option texts are not judged). APPROVED reads "Approved, waiting to run" only on a run request page; grant and activation APPROVED wording is left to the owner's review. (4) *Every constant.* T-UI-259 calls `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.ui.StatusLabels.of(Enum<?>)` reflectively (expected API, ui-dev) so the test tree compiles before it exists; the enums are `RequestStatus` (run, grant and activation requests share it), `IncidentStatus` and `CauseType`. If the screens label another enum (for example a grant window state), it must be added to the list. (5) *Changed existing tests.* `ActivationPageGapTest` T-GAP-357 read "REJECTED" in the ended row's text; it now requires the row's `data-batch-control-status="REJECTED"` element to show a readable label (red on main: the text is `REJECTED`). `DiscoverOnlyRequestScreenTest` T-SEC-26 read "OPEN" in the incident page text; it now requires the `OPEN` hook with a readable label (red on main). `HistoryUsabilityTest` T-10-11 (the Rebuild row) read only the absence of the raw `APPROVED_REQUEST`, which a label would make vacuous; it now also rejects the label "Approved request" and the hook in the Rebuild's row (found by its run link), and checks, when hooks exist, that the approved run's row carries `APPROVED_REQUEST` (green on main). (6) *Red on origin/main (d80e5fe).* T-UI-250..252: "the result (status) filter must not be a free-text field any more: <input name="result" ... placeholder="SUCCESS" type="text" ...>". T-UI-253/254: "the result filter must be a dropdown (select), was: <input name="result" ...>". T-UI-255..258: "the status PENDING (OPEN, APPROVED_REQUEST) must be shown in an element carrying data-batch-control-status=...". T-UI-259: "expected API: io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.ui.StatusLabels.of(Enum<?>) -> String (ClassNotFoundException)". All guards (CSV, filter tokens, JSON summary) pass on main. (7) *Colour badges (T-UI-260..268; contract "D2 colour badges", #18.2, decided by the owner 2026-10-14).* Written from that contract and from pages rendered on this branch (8f4d38c8); no src/main knowledge. *What a badge is.* Every element that carries a `RequestStatus` or `IncidentStatus` name in `data-batch-control-status` must have the class `batch-control-status` and the constant's tone in `data-batch-control-tone` (PENDING warning, APPROVED info, EXECUTED success, REJECTED danger, CANCELLED/EXPIRED/INVALIDATED neutral; OPEN danger, ACKNOWLEDGED warning, RESOLVED success), and whatever has the class or a non-empty tone must be such an element with both: a result, a run cause or a window state is not a badge. The hook may stay on the element that carries it today (a `span`, or the `td` itself in the ended rows of the grants and activations lists) or move to a `span` inside the cell; a second hooked or badge element in the same row is a duplicate (T-UI-267). *Unchanged text.* The badge's whole text content (white space collapsed) must be `StatusLabels.of(constant)` or the wording the screen had on this branch before the badges: `Approved, waiting to run` for APPROVED, `<label> by <user>` and `Expired without a decision` in the grants list. An icon with text, a prefix or the tone as a word fails; an icon without text is not judged. *Screens and statuses.* Run requests are produced in all seven statuses, window requests in their five, activation requests in six, incidents in three; EXPIRED is reached with the replaced clock (`BatchClock.setForTest`, filed 61 minutes ago under a pending timeout of one hour) and one expiry pass, never by waiting. The lists show a status only in their ended tables (the pending and active tables have no status column), so APPROVED and PENDING are judged on the request pages and in History. The incident page's history table shows one status per transition; those rows are badges too. *Stylesheet (T-UI-265).* On this branch the plugin's stylesheet is linked only by pages that render a short id or a scope (`adjuncts/<hash>/io/jenkins/plugins/batchcontrol/ui/batch-control.css`); the run request, activation request and incident pages, the incidents list and History > Incidents do not link it. The row takes every `link rel=stylesheet` whose URL contains `batchcontrol` or `batch-control` as the plugin's and the others as core's, and reads them over HTTP. A tone's rules are the rules (also inside `@media`) whose selector holds `[data-batch-control-tone="<tone>"]` (quotes optional): the stylesheet must select the tone by the attribute the contract defines. "Uses core's theme variable" is measured as: among the variables the tone's rules use, followed through the plugin's own custom properties, one is not defined by the plugin, is defined in a stylesheet of core the page links, and its name contains `warning`, `accent` (info), `success`, `error` or `destructive` (danger), `secondary` (neutral). The pairing of info with accent and neutral with secondary text is this test's reading of the contract's list ("warning, success, error/destructive, accent and secondary text"). Named colours (`white`, `orange`) are not detected. *Guards.* T-UI-263, T-UI-264 and T-UI-266 hold before and after the feature. The JSON summary legitimately has a `success` count, so its guard forbids `warning`, `info`, `danger`, `neutral` and `tone` as words and any tone as a string value. A status filter value is upper-cased by the page (`status=warning` is kept as `WARNING`) and matches nothing. *Not measured here, verified in e2e:* the contrast of badge text against badge background is at least 4.5:1 in the light and in the dark theme; each tone's badge is visibly different from the plain cell around it and the badge is a pill inside the cell, not the painted cell; the page raises no Content-Security-Policy violation for inline styles (the rows only check the absence of `style` attributes and elements on and around the badge; the tab bar and several cells of these pages carry `style` attributes today, which the contract does not cover). *Red at 8f4d38c8:* T-UI-260..262 "the element showing PENDING (EXPIRED, OPEN) must be a badge, with the class \"batch-control-status\""; T-UI-265 "links no stylesheet of the plugin" for the five pages above and "no rule styles the class .batch-control-status", "no rule selects [data-batch-control-tone=...]" for the five tones; T-UI-267 "found 1 status element(s) and 0 element(s) with the class"; T-UI-268 "expected API: io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.ui.StatusLabels.tone(Enum<?>) -> String (NoSuchMethodException)". T-UI-250..259 are unchanged and green. The assertions past the first red one were run once against the rendered pages with the class and the tone added to the DOM in the test (not committed): T-UI-260..262 and T-UI-267 passed, and the stylesheet checker accepted a sample that takes the five tones from `--warning-color`, `--accent-color`, `--success-color`, `--error-color` and `--text-color-secondary` and refused hard-coded, misspelt and swapped ones. (8) *Approved, but no longer in effect (T-UI-269, T-UI-269a; contract point 8, decided by the owner 2026-10-14).* Written from that decision and from pages rendered on this branch at ui-dev's implementation (9a976729, where T-UI-250..268 are green); no src/main knowledge. *The exception.* In the Ended table (`table[data-batch-control-list=ended]`) of the grants list and of the activations list, an element carrying `data-batch-control-status="APPROVED"` must have the tone `neutral`; this is the one exception to "the tone follows the constant" of point (7). On the request pages, in History and in every other table APPROVED stays `info`, and `StatusLabels.tone(APPROVED)` stays `info` (T-UI-268 unchanged). The shared checks of T-UI-260..267 ("every status element is a badge with its tone", "only statuses are badges") apply the exception by where the element is: the page path ends in `batch-control/grants/` or `batch-control/activations/` and the element is inside the Ended table. *Accepted wordings.* For APPROVED in those tables the badge text may also be what the cell reads today: `Expired`, `Revoked by <user>`, `Revoked (<reason>) by <user>` (the reason of a window ended by its item's deletion is `its item was deleted`, ARCHITECTURE 4) and `Approved (superseded)`. ui-dev asked that the superseded wording be accepted as badge text; it is. The two rows pin the exact wording of their fixtures as the badge's whole text ("text unchanged from today"). *Grants (T-UI-269).* At 9a976729 the cells of ended windows are plain text without a hook (before it they carried `data-batch-control-status="APPROVED"`); the row requires the hook back, on the cell or on one element inside it. Three ways a window ends are produced: the expiry time passes (the window is granted with the clock replaced 61 minutes back, 30 minutes long, then one expiry pass), `POST batch-control/grants/<window id>/revoke` by an administrator, and the deletion of its item. The Active table has no status column, so the open window's row has no badge (the one-badge-per-row count would show an extra one). *Activations (T-UI-269a).* SPEC 6a does not use the word "superseded"; it is the screen's word (note 279, T-GAP-357). The reachable path is SPEC 6a's "an approved hold marks the job not activated" and "approval marks the job activated": an approved ACTIVATE is replaced by an approved HOLD, and that HOLD by a second approved ACTIVATE; both replaced requests are in the Ended table and read `Approved (superseded)`, the last one is in the Active table. No other path is assumed. *Red at 9a976729:* T-UI-269 "the grants list, Ended, the window on exp-x: the row must show how the approved request ended (\"Expired\") in one element carrying data-batch-control-status=\"APPROVED\", found 0 status element(s)"; T-UI-269a "the activations list, Ended, the ACTIVATE that a HOLD replaced: an approved request that is no longer in effect is neutral in the Ended table ... expected: <neutral> but was: <info>". The guards inside both rows (APPROVED `info` on the request pages) pass. Both rows passed once against the rendered pages with the hook, class and neutral tone set in the DOM by the test (not committed), with T-UI-255..267 still green. *Verified in e2e, not here:* the neutral badge of an ended approval is visibly different from the `info` badge of an approval in effect, in both themes. *Ids:* T-UI-270..284 belong to D3 on another branch, so the second row is T-UI-269a (method `t_ui_269a_...`). (9) *Incident results and result labels (T-UI-269b..269i; owner decisions of 2026-10-14 on D2, #18.2/#18.3).* Written from those decisions and from pages rendered on this branch (f2e150bc, read as HTML only); no src/main knowledge. *Decision 1, the Incidents Result filter offers only results that can open an incident.* The option values of the `?kind=incidents` Result dropdown are exactly ``, FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED; the order is this test's choice, pinned by T-UI-269b, and follows SPEC 11 (FAILURE and UNSTABLE by default, ABORTED the one that may be added). SUCCESS and NOT_BUILT are absent. ABORTED is offered whatever `incidentResults` holds, so incidents recorded under an earlier setting stay searchable (T-UI-269c). At f2e150bc the incidents list has no Result filter; T-UI-269b checks it only if one appears. This supersedes point (1) for incidents ("the rows require SUCCESS, UNSTABLE, FAILURE and ABORTED"): T-UI-251 no longer says "the Result dropdown as T-UI-250" and its test no longer requires SUCCESS. History > Runs is unchanged (T-UI-250); T-UI-269b's guard reads the owner's "still offers every result" literally and requires all five results there, NOT_BUILT included, which T-UI-250 leaves open. A typed `result=SUCCESS` or `result=NOT_BUILT` on incidents keeps T-UI-253's rule for a value outside the list (selected, one extra option, value as typed); whether it filters the table is not pinned (T-UI-253 does not say). *Decision 2, readable result labels, as text and not as badges, on six places.* The incidents list, the incident page's Result row, History > Incidents, History > Runs, the dashboard and the run request page's Build table (Build / Result / Started / Duration). The labels are the dropdown's option texts at f2e150bc: SUCCESS `Success`, UNSTABLE `Unstable`, FAILURE `Failed`, NOT_BUILT `Not built`, ABORTED `Aborted`. T-UI-250 and point (1) left the option texts open; this mapping is now pinned for the dropdowns as well (T-UI-269b) and for the cells (T-UI-269e..269g). The result cell's whole text must be the label. Neither the cell nor anything inside it may have the class `batch-control-status` or a `data-batch-control-tone` attribute, which point (7) already required of a result. Whether the cell carries `data-batch-control-status` is not pinned. *A build with no result (T-UI-269h).* Neither SPEC nor this matrix said how a running build is shown. At f2e150bc the request page's Build table reads `IN PROGRESS` with an empty Duration, and the dashboard and History > Runs do not list the run until it completes. Owner decision of 2026-10-14 (after the first draft of this point): the Result cell of a running build reads exactly `In progress`, plain text and not a badge; the empty Duration and the absence from the dashboard and History > Runs are today's behaviour, accepted by the owner and kept as guards, checked before the label. The same decision accepted the T-UI-251 and T-SEC-26 changes, the order FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED and NOT_BUILT being required on runs. Red at 3feb57a5 for T-UI-269h: "a build with no result yet reads 'In progress' ... expected: <In progress> but was: <IN PROGRESS>", with both guards passing. The running build is held by a gated build step and released in a `finally`, never waited for with a sleep. *Guards.* `incidents.csv` and `runs.csv` keep the raw names (T-UI-269i). *Changed existing test.* `DiscoverOnlyRequestScreenTest` T-SEC-26 read `FAILURE` in the incident page text; it now requires the row headed Result to read `Failed`. *Red at f2e150bc:* T-UI-269b "History > Incidents, incidentResults default: SUCCESS cannot open an incident and must not be offered: [, SUCCESS, UNSTABLE, FAILURE, NOT_BUILT, ABORTED]" (the runs guard before it passes); T-UI-269d "besides the one kept value the dropdown offers Any, FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED only ... was [, UNSTABLE, FAILURE, NOT_BUILT, ABORTED]"; T-UI-269e/269f/269g "the result must be shown as a readable label, not the raw enum word: 'FAILURE'" ('SUCCESS'); T-SEC-26 "expected: <Failed> but was: <FAILURE>". Green: T-UI-269c, T-UI-269i, T-UI-250..254 (T-UI-269h was a green guard until the `In progress` decision; see above). The not-a-badge check and the cell lookup past the first red assertion were run once with the label assertion disabled (not committed): all 24 result cells of T-UI-269e..269g were found, none is a badge, each reads the raw name. *Not here:* the e2e geometry check (row heights) is relaxed by the same decisions and belongs to e2e; no row-height assertion is added. *Ids:* T-UI-270..284 belong to D3, so the rows continue the letter suffix of T-UI-269a. *The Incidents introduction follows `incidentResults` (T-UI-269j; owner decision of 2026-10-14).* At 56698c10 `batch-control/incidents/` opens with "Failed and unstable builds are registered automatically as incidents." under every setting, ABORTED included. The rule: the opening names the configured results by their labels, lower case after the first word, always in the order FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED, joined with commas and a final "and"; the rest of the paragraph is unchanged. The owner gave the wording for the default, [FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED], [FAILURE] and [ABORTED, FAILURE]; the row also checks [UNSTABLE, ABORTED] and [ABORTED], which follow from the same rule. The sentence appears on no other screen at 56698c10 (History > Incidents and the overview were read), so it is pinned on the incidents list only. *Not pinned:* an empty `incidentResults`, because SPEC does not define it. At 56698c10, storing an empty list through the configuration's setter leaves the previous value in place, so the page cannot be reached with an empty setting through the setter. *Escaping* is not measured: only result names can be stored (T-CFG-04 refuses `FAILURE, BOGUS`), so no user text reaches the sentence. *Red at 56698c10:* "the incidents list with incidentResults [FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED]: ... expected: <Failed, unstable and aborted builds are registered automatically as incidents. ...> but was: <Failed and unstable builds are registered automatically as incidents. ...>"; the default setting before it passes. *Verified in e2e (e2e-tester's request, recorded here):* e2e verifies T-UI-269b..269i in `r27/labels_filters.py` sections I and L. The fixed English result labels are also checked in de-DE, fr-FR and ja-JP browsers, and the crawls now flag a raw result word in a result cell. Decision 1's geometry rule (the badge stays inside its cell, and no new sideways scroll appears) replaced the 768 px row-height check in `r27/status_badges.py` section G (F-1, accepted by the owner). *Further owner decisions of 2026-10-14, recorded without a new row:* the run request page keeps its status `Executed` while the request's build is still running. The clipped kept `SUCCESS` option in the narrow Result select (T-UI-269d: a typed `result=SUCCESS` on incidents) is accepted. *T-UI-269j in e2e (recorded at the coordinator's request, 2026-10-15):* `e2e/r27/labels_filters.py` section N verifies T-UI-269j. An admin saves each setting through the real Batch Control configuration form, and the check asserts the stored value. The settings checked are the default, [FAILURE, UNSTABLE, ABORTED], [FAILURE], [ABORTED, FAILURE], [UNSTABLE, ABORTED] and [ABORTED]. The paragraph is read as admin and as an auditor who holds only ViewHistory. Restoring the setting afterwards is asserted. The check fails on the build before 7419858f and passes from 7419858f on. *Out of D2's scope:* the configuration form still accepts SUCCESS and NOT_BUILT in `incidentResults`. This is tracked as bug #91, to be fixed separately, and no D2 row covers it. *D3 supersedes the layout part of T-UI-269e/269f (owner decision of 2026-10-15; note 362 point 10).* D3 removes the Job and Result columns from the dashboard, History > Runs, the incidents list and History > Incidents. On those tables the two rows now read the result in the Run cell of the run's row, found by its run link: the label must be an element's visible whole text, with the same exact labels, no-badge rule and no-raw-word rule. They are red until D3 is in. The incident page's Result row (T-UI-269e) and the request page's Build table (T-UI-269g/269h) are unchanged.
350. **The diff of a large changed configuration allocates linearly (T-09-90..92, #35).** Written from SPEC 9 (CONFIGURE records carry a unified diff; recording is on while either switch is on), SPEC 6 (non-functional) and the #35 contract (linear allocation on the saving thread; the diff stays correct; the "too large" behaviour beyond the existing cap is unchanged). Measured with `com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean#getThreadAllocatedBytes` on the test thread around `setDescription`, which saves on that thread (a `SaveableListener` runs inside the save). The plugin's share is the recorded save minus the same save while both switches are off, so Jenkins' own XStream cost is excluded; each measured save follows a warm-up save of the same size. Measured on main (8a0f954, JDK 21): recorded 76.2 MB, unrecorded 7.1 MB, plugin share 69.1 MB for 4,000 lines (an (m+1) x (n+1) int table is about 64 MB at this size). Threshold 16 MB, the contract's figure: a linear diff leaves the plugin's share at the measured linear overhead of about 5 MB, so 16 MB has a margin of about three times and is still four times below main. 4,000 lines rather than the contract's example of 5,000 because on main a configuration of about 4,800 lines or more is already beyond the existing cap and gets the "Diff too large to store (N lines) ..." note (probe at 4,400 lines: real diff, about 100 MB on the thread; at 4,800: the note), so 5,000 lines cannot be red; T-09-92 pins that note at 6,000 lines.
351. **A user without RequestGrant writes no GRANT_REQUEST_BLOCKED record (T-08-260/261, #44).** Written from SPEC 2 (the five permissions), SPEC 8 and LIMITATIONS 29 (with change control off a window request is refused with a message plus a GRANT_REQUEST_BLOCKED record), CLAUDE.md (the permission check comes first in a state-changing web method) and the #44 contract. Red on main (8a0f954): a1 (Approve only) gets HTTP 400 and one record "a permission window for 'job-k' could not be requested: change control is off" naming a1. T-08-261 is green on main and pins "whatever the switch". The contract's Manage-only user is not a row: BatchControl/Manage implies RequestGrant (USER-GUIDE "`Manage` ... implies the other four", DECISIONS P-02, note 269), and on main a user holding only Manage passes `hasPermission(RequestGrant)` and gets the same 400 and record as u1. Refusing that user with 403 would contradict the documented implication, so that half of the contract is reported to the main session for a ruling instead of being tested.
352. **A re-run of a marked run is marked while change control is off (T-02-188, #1.1, security-31 S-31-01).** Written from SPEC 2's D-58c line ("a re-run of a marked run (an administrator's included) is marked too"; no switch condition, unlike the guarding line, which says "while change control is on"), DECISIONS D-58c ("before and after the review"), CLAUDE.md's switch rule (the marker is an invisible action, so carrying it changes no Jenkins behaviour; the refusal itself stays gated on the switch, which the row's guard pins: with the switch off the re-runs build) and the #1 contract. The marker is observed through its effect only: once change control is on again, a non-administrator's re-run of #3/#4 is refused and recorded. Red on main (8a0f954): alice's Pipeline Rebuild of #3 builds (next build number 6, expected 5) and nothing is recorded. Run control stays off, so with change control off both switches are off, as in S-31-01.
353. **A carried marker's record names the re-runner and the original replayer (T-02-189, #1.2, security-31 S-31-02).** Written from SPEC 2's D-58c line (the record of a marked run names the user, the run and the grant), DECISIONS D-58c, security-31 S-31-02 ("carry the original user in the inherited marker ... the J#3 record names bob as the original replayer and the administrator as the re-runner, and does not say that the administrator's permission came from a window") and the #1 contract ("the record names the replayer correctly and does not call an administrator a grant-only replayer"). The second half already holds on main since DEF-40 (T-02-82 pins it; this row repeats it as a guard with the narrower pattern `'admin', whose permission`), so the red half is the lost original replayer: on main (8a0f954) the record of #3 is "Run #3 was started by 'admin' as a re-run of run #2, whose script was replayed under a permission window; it carries the same mark ..." with user admin and no mention of bob. The row asserts `'bob'` (quoted, as the records quote user ids) in the detail and leaves the wording free.
354. **Marked runs are listed under the current name after a restart (T-02-190, #1.3, security-31 S-31-03).** Written from SPEC 2's D-58b/D-58c lines ("the review surfaces list such runs"; guarding follows renames and moves), DECISIONS D-58a (1) and (4), security-31 S-31-03 and the #1 contract ("after a rename and a restart, the index lists the runs under the current name"). The list is the Manage Jenkins monitor read as in T-GAP-319..321: a list item per listed item with its name in `code`, its marked runs as links in a nested list (only the item's own nested `ul` is read, not the outer list). Red on main (8a0f954): after the restart `K` is listed (its changed state is stored with the grant and follows the rename) but its row has no run link, while the unrenamed `L` keeps `job/L/2/`. S-31-03's second case (a re-created job with a recycled name listing another job's run ids) is not part of the contract and is not a row.
355. **A stale listed name can be marked reviewed from the list (T-02-191, #1.4, security-30 S-30-06, security-31 S-31-04).** Written from SPEC 2's D-58b line (the state ends only through the explicit "Mark as reviewed" action), SPEC 6 usability and the #1 contract ("an entry for a stale or renamed item can still be marked reviewed from the monitor"). A review control is an element of the row with a `data-url` naming `markReviewed` (the confirmation link the other rows use on main, `data-post="true"`) or a form posting to `markReviewed` with an `item` field; either shape passes, and the control must name the listed item (`item=gone`). The stale name is made as in T-GAP-245 (the directory removed while Jenkins is down); T-GAP-245 already shows that a hand-made POST for that name works on main, so the red part is only the missing control: on main (8a0f954) the row is `<li><code>gone</code></li>`.
356. **An unresolved re-run source is recorded as unresolved for anonymous too (T-02-192, #1.5, security-32 S-32-01).** Written from SPEC 2's D-58c line ("a re-run whose source cannot be resolved is refused"), SPEC 6 (a refused Replay writes a TRIGGER_BLOCKED record naming the switch that blocked it), security-32 S-32-01 and the #1 contract ("it uses the same unresolved wording (`unresolvedSource`) as for a person"). The unresolved source is a Replay cause whose build was deleted, as in T-GAP-257. "build #?" is not asserted either way: the person wording on main contains it too. Only one anonymous submission is made because unattended refusals are merged per job and cause kind per hour (SPEC 6). SYSTEM is not a row: on main (8a0f954) a SYSTEM submission with an unresolvable source (a deleted-source Replay cause, or a replay flow action without a cause) is not refused at all and writes no record, which agrees with D-58c (only an Overall/Administer holder may re-run; SYSTEM holds it), so the contract's SYSTEM half cannot be made red without contradicting D-58c.
357. **The folder self-grant 403 names no job page and says Configure must be held directly (T-02-193, #1.6, security-32 S-32-03).** Written from SPEC 2's D-48 line (the 403 message), the D-58b line (Mark as reviewed needs native Item/Configure or Overall/Administer, "not by a grant"), SPEC 6 usability and the #1 contract. "Held directly" is read as one sentence (split at `.`, `;` or `:`) containing both "configure" and "directly"; the rest of the wording is free. The job half is a guard only (the contract asks for the folder variant); whether the job text should also say "directly", as S-32-03 (b) suggests, is not asserted. Red on main (8a0f954): the folder and the job get the same text, which ends "... or on the job's Batch Control page (a user with Configure permission on it and Batch Control/Request)". The wording lives in `ui/` or resources, so the fix is ui-dev's.
358. **A stale approver change on a decided request names its status (T-03-94, #1.7, e2e-05 EX-01).** Written from SPEC 3 (the requester changes the designated approvers while the request is PENDING; D-26, D-37), SPEC 6 usability (a refusal says why in plain words; the field-level form refusal is for a wrong field, and here no field is wrong), e2e-05 EX-01 and the #1 contract ("a plain message that names the request's current status"). The message is read from the answer's `role="alert"` elements, the convention of this plugin's refusals (`ApproverFormFixtures#alerts`), because the request page around it shows the status in its detail table ("Status REJECTED"), so the whole page would pass on main. The status word is matched case-insensitively against `RequestStatus#name()` as the service reports it after the decision; the HTTP code is any 4xx (400 or 409 both pass). Red on main (8a0f954) at the run request: 400 with the alert "Nothing was submitted. Correct the fields marked below and submit again; what you entered has been kept." The grant and activation cases follow in the same method (e2e-05 saw the same answer for both).
359. **An identical pending run request is not created twice (T-05-204..206, #1.9, e2e-05 UX-3, owner decision D-88 of 2026-10-10).** Written from the #1 contract's item 9 (D-88 is the owner's ruling of 2026-10-10 as frozen in the contract; it is not in docs/DECISIONS.md yet and SPEC has no rule on duplicates, so there is nothing to conflict with), SPEC 4, SPEC 7 (the requester cancels a PENDING request), SPEC 13 (a new request notifies its designated approvers) and DECISIONS D-84 for telling a script from a browser. Browser: `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8`; script: `Accept: application/json` (no `text/html`, no `*/*`). The notice is matched case-insensitively as the contract words it ("An identical request of yours is already pending"), on the page the 3xx leads to, fetched with the same session. Notifications come from a test `BatchControlNotifier` into `NotificationCapture`; "no second notification" is the count of REQUEST_CREATED after the quiet period (1.5 s, a bounded wait for a delivery that must not happen, not an expiry). Red on main (8a0f954): the identical browser and script submissions each create a second PENDING request. The contract covers run requests only; grant and activation requests are not rows. *Amended for D-88 (2026-10-17).* Four earlier tests submitted the same run request twice while the first was still pending and expected a second request; under D-88 the second is refused as identical (they failed on fix2/1 at dff2b858 and at 1cd39073). They keep their intent. `RequestFormEncodingTest` T-05-139, T-05-140 and T-05-141 check the encoding of the reason (and NOTE): u1 cancels the guard's request before the identical submission, so exactly the same text is still sent. `MultiApproverTest` T-03-32 (b, the real form) checks the stored approver set and its order: its second form submission uses another reason. T-05-206 already pins that a different reason, or a cancelled first request, lets a new request through. *Second round (2026-10-17, fork CI run 39028312127).* Six more tests submitted an identical pending request and were amended in the same way. JsonSubmissionDefaultsTest T-05-147 and RerunFallbackLinkTest T-11-15/T-11-20 now cancel the earlier request (shared helper `ApproverFormFixtures.cancelRunRequest`). PagerParameterTest T-UI-146 and PagerRealJenkinsTest T-UI-149 number their pending reasons. TypedParameterIntegrityTest T-05-137 gives its service guard another value. A static sweep of src/test found no other case. It looked at repeated identical create/submit calls in a method, at helpers with a fixed reason called more than once, and at loops that create requests. Every other candidate creates distinct requests, or decides or cancels each request before the next.
364. **The incident results setting accepts only FAILURE, UNSTABLE and ABORTED (T-11-32..36, #91, owner decisions of 2026-10-17).** Written from SPEC 11 (`incidentResults`: default [FAILURE, UNSTABLE]; ABORTED may be added), the SPEC 5 table, SPEC 2 (the global configuration round-trips through JCasC), issue #91 and the owner decisions; no src/main knowledge. (Note 363 is taken on t2/d4, so this note is 364.) (1) *Refusal.* The field checks and both form saves refuse SUCCESS and NOT_BUILT, as they refuse a name that is not a build result, and nothing is saved. The rows check the field check's error and the unchanged stored value, not the wording of the message. (2) *Stored values from before the upgrade.* "Stored before the upgrade" is produced by editing the `incidentResults` element of the saved `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol.config.BatchControlGlobalConfiguration.xml` and calling `load()`, Jenkins' own read path; a restart is not needed for the rule. The allowed names keep their stored order. "One warning" means exactly one WARNING record from `io.jenkins.plugins.batchcontrol` whose formatted message names the dropped names, across `load()` and two reads of the setting. (3) *JCasC.* The row uses the `incidentResultsText` attribute, as T-GAP-252 does for the duration options. Whether an apply holding SUCCESS is refused or cleaned is not pinned: both satisfy "the same rule". (4) *Red on main (d2c4a3c1).* T-11-32: "checkIncidentResults must answer an error next to the field for 'SUCCESS' ...: <div/>". T-11-33: "the System page with FAILURE, SUCCESS: nothing may be saved ... but was: <[FAILURE, SUCCESS]>" (the guard saves pass). T-11-34/35: "must log exactly one warning naming the dropped names, got []". T-11-36: "a JCasC apply must not bring SUCCESS or NOT_BUILT into the setting: [FAILURE, SUCCESS, NOT_BUILT]" (the guard apply passes).
365. **Reject asks for confirmation first (T-UI-292, T-UI-293, issue #93, owner review 2026-10-18).** Written from issue #93 and the owner's review of PR #102; no src/main knowledge. (1) *The dialog.* Pressing Reject with a comment opens core's confirmation dialog (`window.dialog.confirm`, the same dialog `l:confirmationLink` uses) before anything is posted. The dialog carries the sentence already on the page: "Rejection is final for this request; a rejected request cannot be reopened." Cancel or Escape dismisses it and posts nothing; the request stays PENDING. Confirming posts the form to the Reject button's formaction (`.../reject`); the crumb is sent as a hidden field. (2) *Blank comment skips the dialog.* When the comment is blank the server refuses the rejection anyway, so the dialog would only add a click: the button submits directly and the server's comment-required error shows next to the box. (3) *Approve is untouched.* The Approve button never asks for confirmation and still posts with a single click. (4) *Tests.* `RejectConfirmationTest` stubs `window.dialog.confirm` (HtmlUnit has no real browser dialog) and was committed failing first: the dialog-text assertion failed against the old wording and the blank-comment test failed because the dialog opened. The dialog itself, in a real browser, is covered end to end by `e2e/r27/decision_tables.py` section R, which runs in CI as part of the r27-decision-tables unit. The new class is listed in the `[run approval and mail]` group of `.github/test-shards.txt`. The tests are not tagged `core` (note 330: UI wording and interaction are not core). (5) *Existing tests and drivers.* `DecisionAreaFixtures.decide()` auto-confirms the dialog (WebClient.setConfirmHandler returning true, plus a stub resolving core's `dialog.confirm`), so `DecisionAreaTest`, `FormRefusalUsabilityTest` and `RequestInputGapTest` keep pressing Reject as before. The e2e drivers that press Reject (`e2e/r27/decision_tables.py` press(), `browser_decide` in `e2e/r19/lib.py` and `e2e/r24/lib.py`, `e2e/r14/actions.py`) confirm the dialog after pressing Reject.


## red-team 시나리오 제외 사유 (red-team-01, 매트릭스 행 미추가)

| RT | 제외 사유 |
|---|---|
| RT-04 (FOLDER prefix 오판) | 기존 행과 중복: T-SEC-03(unit, `team/batch` vs `team/batch-other` 경계 판정)과 T-08-11(integration, 폴더 안/밖 통합 검증)이 동일 공격을 커버. POC C에서도 검증됨. 새 엣지 없음. Since D-71 the scope is ITEM (exact match), and T-SEC-03 also asserts the items inside the folder out of scope (note 260). |
| RT-08 (다계정 자가 결재) | 자동 테스트 불가(설계 범위 밖). 플러그인은 계정↔실인 매핑을 알 수 없다 — 조직 통제(IdP 계정 위생) 영역. 비고 12의 README 문서화 요청으로 대체. |
| RT-09 (권한 상실 결재자) | 기존 행과 중복: T-03-03이 "목록 등재 + Approve 권한 상실 → 결재 거부"를 그대로 커버. 부수 위험(요청 PENDING 고착)은 T-07-01(pendingTimeout 만료)로 회수 검증됨. 지정 시점 차단은 SPEC이 요구하지 않음(결재 시점 검사만 명시). |
| RT-12 (잡 이름 경로 탈출·초장문) | 기존 행 확장으로 흡수: 경로 탈출(`../`)은 T-SEC-04가 이미 커버, 시나리오가 추가한 실질 엣지(제어문자·255자 초과 이름)를 T-SEC-04의 Given/Then에 병합했다. 별도 행 불필요. |
| security-08 S-07 (computed-folder children not name-restricted) | Not a defect to test: D-40a and SPEC item 8 keep indexing-created children outside the restriction and send it to LIMITATIONS. |
| security-08 S-13 (CLI name outliving its command on a pooled thread) | Not reproducible from outside: it needs `handleException` itself to throw, which no public CLI input causes. T-RT-02 keeps the blocking assertion and now carries a footnote pointing at these rows; the P-04 proposal is settled by D-30
- **D-31 coverage (notes 38, 39)**: the new-job default is covered by T-08-19..24 (the default applies whoever creates the job and through whichever path — New Item form, REST `createItem`, CLI `create-job`, copy, Job DSL seed, and a plain user inside a grant window, with T-08-24 asserting the administrator and the user outcomes are equal), T-08-25 (run control off forces nothing — the falsifiability guard) and the automation safety net T-08-26..29 (timer, upstream and SCM causes still build the new job; only the human paths are refused). T-RT-05 keeps the D-17 grant-window case and now carries a footnote saying D-31 widened its scope. Two D-31 questions SPEC leaves open are deliberately unasserted and recorded in note 39: an explicit `approvalRequired=false` supplied at creation time, and retroactivity for jobs that already existed.
- **D-34 coverage (note 46)**: creating a job no longer puts it into service. The three-switch default is covered by T-08-30 (New Item form), T-08-31 (REST `createItem` with a cron — and the refused firing, the behavioural core), T-08-32 (CLI `create-job`), T-08-33 (the upstream door), T-08-35 (a copy of a live cron job) and T-08-36 (a Job DSL seed run), with T-08-34 as the falsifiability guard (run control off locks nothing). The release path is T-08-26/27 (rewritten: they used to assert that a *newly created* job builds from a timer/upstream, the contract D-34 reverses), the width of the lock is bounded by T-08-28 (the SCM cause still passes) and its intended effect by T-08-29 (the human path stays refused). T-RT-05's cron assertion is restored — its original R-2 demand was exactly D-34 — and D-32's computed-child exclusion survives unchanged in T-10-07. Five questions SPEC leaves open (an explicit switch value in the creation payload, the unlock being gated only while change control is on, copies, the silence of an unattended refusal, and approving the activation itself) are deliberately unasserted and recorded in note 46.
- **Screen-contract coverage (note 40)**: the approval screen's recent-run window (ui-dev, commit `d6c0878`) is covered by T-UI-01 (the 5/10/20/50 allow-list and the default of 5), T-UI-02 (**the value is trimmed before the allow-list is consulted**, so a padded allowed value such as `runs=10 ` is honoured as 10 and only a value that is still off the list after trimming falls back to 5, always silently and with no error page — owner ruling 2026-09-26: trimming a hand-typed query parameter is ordinary web input handling, so `10 ` is an allowed value and not an unsupported one; T-UI-02 initially asserted the opposite and was the assertion that was too wide, not a product defect), T-UI-03 and T-UI-04 (both P0 — no `runs` value discloses a run of a job the viewer may not read or of a job that has been deleted, so the window cannot be used around P-09) T-UI-05 (the post-approval notice is bound to `APPROVED` + `executedRunId == null`, measured through the `batch-control-approved-notice` id ui-dev keeps as a test hook, so the row asserts the notice itself and not merely the state it hangs off) and T-UI-06 (note 43). These rows freeze an implementation-defined screen contract rather than a SPEC acceptance criterion; whether it should become one is left to a human, and the rows are dropped with the feature if the answer is no.
- **P-03 and D-33 coverage (notes 44, 45 — the last two open P0/P1 rows of Phase 5)**: T-SEC-07 was the only empty P0 row in the matrix ("pending P-03 decision"); with the owner's ruling (keep masked storage, accept that an approved run cannot reproduce the secret) it now pins the guarantee **and** the limitation through the browser request form, with a non-sensitive parameter of the same job as the false-positive guard on every surface (request record, detail screen, store files, all four CSV exports, dashboard, launched build), and T-SEC-19 pins the same guarantee on the recording path that never goes through the request screen. T-E2E-06 was failing e2e because it demanded a notice inside a screen D-33 forbids the plugin from touching; it now asserts that the denial screen is core's own and that the expiry guidance plus re-request link live on `/batch-control/grants/`, staying at the e2e layer for the reasons in note 45 (its automatable core is already T-08-17/18).

329. **Paged lists render completely in a real Jenkins (T-UI-149, #45).** The first #45 fix resolved a plugin class from a Jelly tag (`j:invokeStatic`); the web application class loader cannot see plugin classes, so in a real Jenkins every page with a list over 50 rows was cut off in the first table (HTTP 200, partial HTML, log `JellyTagException ... Could not load class`). JenkinsRule flat class path hides this; only RealJenkinsExtension sees it (as T-UI-46, note 191). Written from the brief and note 327; no src/main knowledge. 52 rows per list assume a page size of 50 (note 327 measured 50).
330. **The `core` tag: the tests ci.jenkins.io runs (jenkinsci/batch-control-plugin#80).** The ci.jenkins.io administrators asked us to stop overloading ci.jenkins.io, and the maintainer split the work (2026-10-10): GitHub Actions keeps running the whole suite on every pull request (Linux JDK 21 and 25, Windows JDK 21); ci.jenkins.io runs plain `buildPlugin` on Linux JDK 25 and Windows JDK 21 with only the tests tagged `@Tag("core")` (a pom profile owned by release-manager applies `groups=core` only when the build runs on Jenkins). An untagged test is not optional: it still gates every pull request on GitHub Actions; the tag only chooses what ci.jenkins.io repeats. No row, ID, priority or test file of the matrix changes. *What `core` means.* A test is `core` when its failure means a central guarantee is broken: (a) an approval-required job cannot run without an approval through any entry point SPEC 6 names (UI build, REST/remote API, CLI, scripted or Pipeline triggers, rebuild/rerun, retry), an approved run is queued exactly once, and unattended causes pass only through the 6a activation gate; (b) requester and approver permission checks and the self-approval rules on the state-changing endpoints of run, activation and grant requests (SPEC 2, 3, 5, 7), a permission window confers only its action on its item and ends on time (SPEC 8), and the per-item authorization guard (D-35b, D-35c, D-58); (c) store durability and recovery: no partial or unreadable file is left (atomic writes), the Windows file replacement and sharing retry (notes 292, 293), recovery after a failed write or a torn line, persistence across a restart (SPEC 4); (d) a history record for each state change (SPEC 1, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12); (e) with a switch off, Jenkins behaves as without the plugin (SPEC 1); (f) the security basics: POST-only, crumb and permission checks on `do*`, 403/404 for users without the permission, escaping of user input, secrets never in plaintext (SPEC 6 non-functional, SPEC 12). Not `core`: UI layout and wording, CSV formatting, paging, dashboard limits, help text, notification content, RealJenkinsExtension and stress or race-loop rows (`GrantSwitchOffRaceTest`), and gap rows that repeat a core row. *Rule for new tests.* Tag a new test `core` only when it guards one of the criteria (a)-(f) and the budget allows it: the summed class time of the core set stays at or below about 110 minutes serial (about 25-30 % of the suite, near 30 minutes on 4 forks, so a Windows agent stays well under an hour). A tagged method costs its class time divided by the number of tests in the class; class times come from the GitHub JDK 21 shards of main. Prefer one representative test per guarantee to every variant; when the budget is reached, untag a variant before tagging a new test. Put the tag on the class when every test in it is core, otherwise on the methods; use only `org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag` with the name `core`; tagging never changes test logic. A core test that is split, renamed or moved keeps its tag. *Selection* (class times from GitHub run 38040984926, JDK 21 shards; "class" = tag on the class, otherwise "k of n" tagged methods with the matrix IDs and their share). 360. **Request pages are titled with their subject; the strategy revert moves into Advanced (T-UI-230..239, Wave D D1, #18.4, #18.7).** Written from the Wave D contract (D1, frozen 2026-10-10), issue #18, core 2.568.3's `lib/layout/copyButton.jelly` and `lib/form/advanced.jelly`, and pages rendered on origin/main (d80e5fe); no src/main knowledge. (1) *Titles.* The run, grant and activation request pages were titled `Run Request <id>`, `Grant Request <id>`, `Activation Request <id>` / `Hold Request <id>` (title, `h1`, last breadcrumb and its `tooltip`). The rows require exactly `Run request: <job full name>`, `Grant request: <scope full name>`, `Activation request: <job>`; for a HOLD request either `Activation request: <job>` or `Hold request: <job>` is accepted, because the contract names only the first and a HOLD page was titled "Hold Request" before. The `<title>` is compared after removing core's ` - Jenkins` suffix. (2) *ID row.* The contract says the id stays on the page in an `ID` row with `l:copyButton`; core renders that as `<button class="... jenkins-copy-button ..." text="<id>">`, so the rows look for a `th` reading `ID` and, in its `td`, the id as text and such a button. The rows require the ID row on all three pages ("apply the same pattern"). (3) *Escaping.* Core refuses `?*/\%!@#$^&|<>[]:;` in item names, so `<` cannot reach a title through a name; `q"x'y{z}` exercises text and attribute escaping (a broken `tooltip` attribute would not read back the exact text; which pages carry that attribute, and the check added for every other attribute, are in (10)). (4) *Revert placement.* `f:advanced` renders `button.advanced-button` and a hidden `div.advancedBody`; core's script moves the body's rows out when the button is pressed, so T-UI-234 asserts the control is inside `advancedBody` before and outside it, displayed, after. "The end of the Batch Control section" is checked as: no named setting (`_.`) of the closest `section` follows the control. The rows look at both `manage/configure` and `manage/batch-control-configuration/` (T-UI-25 found the revert on the latter for the administrator). (5) *Changed existing test.* `ConfigAuditTest.offersRevert` (T-UI-25) read the revert from the visible text and from `href`/form actions only; the confirmation link carries its endpoint in `data-url` (`href="#"`), so once the control is hidden inside Advanced the premise "the administrator is offered the revert" would fail and the negative half would pass vacuously. It now also reads `data-url`/`formaction` and the DOM's text content (hidden included): stricter for the Manage holder, unchanged for the administrator. (6) *Red on origin/main (d80e5fe).* T-UI-230..233: `expected: <Run request: ops/batch-x> but was: <Run Request a7aa...>` (and the grant, activation and escaped-name equivalents). T-UI-234/235: "the revert control must be inside core's Advanced control ... it sits in: div.setting-main < div.jenkins-form-item.tr < section.jenkins-section < ...". Guards pass; ConfigAuditTest stays green on main. (7) *The title of a window whose item was renamed or moved (T-UI-236, T-UI-237; added after the e2e audit of D1).* Rows T-UI-230..235 never renamed an item, so they could not see that the new title kept the name the window was approved for. SPEC 8 line 172 (D-74): "a window applies to its item, not to a name ... the window follows it"; line 173 (D-75): "the grant pages, the grants list and the expiry notice show the item's current full name only to a viewer (or recipient) with Item/Read on it; anyone else sees the approved name with a fixed note that the item was moved and its new location is not visible to them. Administrators see the current name." The title, heading and breadcrumb are part of the grant page, so they follow the same rule as its Scope row (T-SEC-96, T-SEC-114). The two rows use the fixture of those rows (Batch Control matrix strategy, `vault-q9` blocking inheritance with Item/Read for admin only) on top of this class's `ops` folder, because a window's following and a viewer's Item/Read are what the rows are about; requests are filed and approved through the forms, renames and moves go through core's `confirmRename` and the folders plugin's `move/move` as the administrator, and each step asserts as a premise that the window is still active and names the new full name. Readers and non-readers are separate rows so that each has its own result: T-UI-236 is the positive half, T-UI-237 the D-75 guard that the fix of T-UI-236 (8e15754f) had to keep (a title that simply printed the window's current scope would have made it red; it stayed green, see (11)). T-UI-237 has two kinds of non-reader: n1, a BatchControl/Manage holder with Item/Read on nothing, for the plain rename (the brief's case: a viewer who opens the page and may not read `ops/batch-y`); and u1, a1 and m1, who lose Item/Read when the item is moved into `vault-q9` (the D-75 rows' case). For u1, a1 and m1 the row requires exactly the approved name `ops/batch-x`, as SPEC says, although they could read the intermediate `ops/batch-y`; it does not assert that `batch-y` is absent from their pages, only `vault-q9`. "Not shown" is measured as in note 275: on the three titles and on the raw HTML of the answer, which also covers a `tooltip` or any other attribute. The request page is addressed by the request's id, as in T-UI-231; the row does not open a second URL for the window. Not asserted by these two rows: the grants list and the expiry notice (T-SEC-96/97 cover them). Not asserted by any integration row and verified in e2e instead ((12)): a window on an item below a renamed folder, the title after a Jenkins restart, and a window that has ended. (8) *A pending request does not follow (T-UI-238).* D-74 and D-75 speak of windows. A PENDING request has none, and SPEC 8 line 176 says "approval is refused when no item exists at that name any more", so the request stays a request for the name it was made for and its title keeps that name after the item is renamed. The row asserts the title only; that the approval is then refused is the subject of T-08-117 (deleted item) and is not repeated here. It runs on the class's MockAuthorizationStrategy, as T-UI-231 does. (9) *What the Manage holder sees in place of the revert (T-UI-239; added after the e2e audit of D1).* On origin/main (d80e5fe) the Batch Control configuration page told a user without Overall/Administer "Only a Jenkins administrator can change the authorization strategy." among the settings. D1 at first moved the whole entry into `f:advanced`, so until a0c99bca m1 got an Advanced button whose body held that sentence and nothing m1 could use. T-UI-235 did not see this: it asserts only that no revert control and no revert caption are in m1's page. The row requires the sentence outside `div.advancedBody` (found as the innermost element whose text holds the exact sentence), no `button.advanced-button` in any `section` of the main panel that holds a Batch Control setting, and, with JavaScript on and nothing pressed, the sentence's element displayed (HtmlUnit `isDisplayed`, which was false inside the hidden body before a0c99bca). The three are reported together (`assertAll`). m1 is refused `manage/configure` (403, no Overall/Manage), so the row looks at `manage/batch-control-configuration/` only. The administrator's entry stays in Advanced (T-UI-234). Holders of Overall/Manage and Overall/SystemRead, who open `manage/configure` without Overall/Administer, are not in any integration row; they are verified in e2e ((12)). (10) *The breadcrumb's tooltip (T-UI-230..233 reworded).* The rows said "the breadcrumb's `tooltip` carries the same text" and the test looped over the `[tooltip]` elements of the last breadcrumb. What the pages fetched by these tests (JenkinsRule, JavaScript off, core 2.568.3) carry, observed on this branch: no `tooltip` for a last breadcrumb of 24, 25 or 26 characters (`Run request: ops/batch-x`, `Run request: ops/q"x'y{z}`, `Grant request: ops/batch-x`) and one, on the `span` inside the `li`, for 27 and 29 characters (`Grant request: ops/q"x'y{z}`, `Activation request: ops/act-x`). So the loop compared a tooltip on the ACTIVATE page of T-UI-232 and on the grant page of T-UI-233 and compared nothing in T-UI-230, T-UI-231 and on the run page of T-UI-233, while the rows claimed it for all. This differs from the brief for this change, which said core sets the attribute only in the browser, on a breadcrumb the layout cuts, and that the loop therefore never compares anything; the test author did not read core to find which rule it is, the lengths above are what was rendered. The rows now state the clause as a condition ("where the last breadcrumb carries a `tooltip` it reads the same text") and say per row whether the integration test compares one; the tooltip of a breadcrumb that a real browser cuts is verified in e2e (unit `r27-titles-revert`, checks "D1 #18.4 tooltip: ... shown cut"; see (12)). In the test the loop is kept (`assertTooltipIfAny`, commented as biting only when a tooltip is present) and returns how many it compared; T-UI-233 asserts as a premise that the grant page's breadcrumb carries exactly one, so the attribute escaping of that row cannot silently stop being checked if core changes the length rule. Added to T-UI-233 because the run page has no tooltip: on both pages no attribute name holds a piece of `q"x'y{z}` and an attribute value that holds a piece of it holds the whole name, which is what an unescaped quote inside an attribute would break. Green on this branch. (11) *Red, then green, on ui/d1-request-titles, `mvn -q test -Dtest='PageTitleIdRowTest,RevertPlacementTest'`.* When the rows were added (ee4ac361, run on 78782e40) two were red: T-UI-236 (`u1's <title> ... expected: <Grant request: ops/batch-y> but was: <Grant request: ops/batch-x>`) and T-UI-239 (three failures: the sentence sat in `div.advancedBody`; the section had an `Advanced` button; with JavaScript the sentence was not displayed). T-UI-230..235, T-UI-237 and T-UI-238 were green then and are guards. T-UI-236 is green since 8e15754f ("title a grant request page with the item its Scope row names") and T-UI-239 since a0c99bca ("show a Manage holder the administrator-only sentence without Advanced"); no file under `src/test` changed between ee4ac361 and 917b703c, so the rows that were red are the rows that are green, unweakened. Re-run by the test author on 917b703c: PageTitleIdRowTest 7 tests (T-UI-230..233, T-UI-236..238) and RevertPlacementTest 3 tests (T-UI-234, T-UI-235, T-UI-239), 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. No row of this note is expected red any more. (12) *Verified in e2e, not by an integration row (e2e-27; a real Jenkins 2.568.3, the image of `e2e/Dockerfile`, read in Chromium).* The unit, section, step and check names below were read by the test author in `e2e/r27/titles_revert.py`, `e2e/r27/title_restart.py`, `e2e/r27/revert_permissions.py` and the unit list of `e2e/ci/shard.py`; that the checks pass is the result of the e2e audit, the test author did not run the drivers. (a) *A window on an item below a renamed folder* follows, and its page is titled with the new full name: unit `r27-titles-revert`, section X. (b) *The title after a Jenkins restart*: `e2e/r27/title_restart.py`, run as the steps `r27-title-restart-before` and `r27-title-restart-after` (the first and the last step of the unit `r16-durable`, whose own steps restart Jenkins in between; the driver's premise is another JVM start time). After the restart the requester, approver-1 and the administrator, who may read the renamed item, read `Grant request: <current name>`; approver-disc, who may open the page but holds no Item/Read, reads the approved name with the "moved" note and the new name is nowhere in the page's HTML (T-UI-236 and T-UI-237 after a restart). (c) *A window that has ended*: `r27-titles-revert`, section W. Renamed while open and then revoked, expired, or ended by the deletion of its item: the title names the item the Scope row names for the same viewer, as while the window was open. Renamed only after the window had ended (revoked or expired): not followed, a window follows its item only while it applies, so the title and the Scope row keep the name the window ended with and the later name is in neither. (d) *A second rename and a move into a folder only administrators read*: `r27-titles-revert`, section X (T-UI-236 and T-UI-237 assert the same on HtmlUnit; section X repeats it in a browser, adds the Scope row for every viewer and, for the viewer who may not read the item, the answers of the page's `contextMenu`, `childrenContextMenu` and `api/json`). (e) *The breadcrumb's tooltip, cut by a real browser*: `r27-titles-revert`, the checks named "D1 #18.4 tooltip: the ... page's last breadcrumb is shown cut and its tooltip carries the full title unchanged" (every e2e item name ends in `-nightly-settlement` so that the breadcrumb is cut); see (10) for what the integration rows compare. (f) *Holders of Overall/Manage and Overall/SystemRead never get the revert*, with or without BatchControl/Manage (four accounts, none with Overall/Administer): unit `r27-revert-permissions` (`e2e/r27/revert_permissions.py`): nothing of the revert in their pages, no Advanced button, the administrator-only sentence displayed where the section is shown to them (T-UI-239), a crumbed POST of the revert answered 403. (g) *A branch job of a multibranch project as the subject*: `r27-titles-revert`, section B. A CONFIGURE window request and a run request on a branch job are accepted and their pages are titled with the job's full item name, the URL-encoded branch name included (e.g. `Run request: .../feature%2Fr27-odd`); an ACTIVATE and a HOLD request on a branch job are refused at submission (HTTP 400, nothing stored; SPEC 6a: the computed folder carries the activation and takes the request). *Still not covered anywhere, integration or e2e:* an organisation folder (or one of its children) as the subject of a request; the tooltip of a short breadcrumb, because core adds none (the e2e guard and (10) only observe that there is none); any browser other than Chromium. (13) *T-UI-233 on Windows (added after the first Windows CI run of D1).* On GitHub Actions `windows-latest` (JDK 21) the row ended in an error, not a failure: `InvalidPathException: Illegal char <"> ...` when the fixture created `ops/q"x'y{z}`. An item's directory is named after it and NTFS forbids `"`, so the item cannot exist there; every other method of PageTitleIdRowTest and RevertPlacementTest passed on Windows, and none of them uses a name NTFS refuses (`ops`, `batch-x`, `batch-y`, `batch-z`, `act-x`, `hold-x`, `vault-q9`, the users, request ids as path segments of URLs only). The test was changed, not the product. The name is now chosen in one place, `PlatformFixtures.itemName("q\"x'y{z}")`, the idiom of note 291 (2) (`HOSTILE_ITEM_NAME` goes through the same method): a probe creates a directory whose name holds `"`; where that works the name is kept, where it does not every `"` becomes `'`. Of the characters NTFS forbids (`< > : " / \ | ? *`) the double quote is the only one core's name check allows, so it is the only one replaced; `'`, `{` and `}` are legal for both. So the row runs with `q"x'y{z}` on Linux and macOS and with `q'x'y{z}` on Windows. Both are 8 characters: `Grant request: ops/q'x'y{z}` is 27 characters like the original, the row now asserts that length as a fixture, and the premise of (10) (exactly one tooltip on the grant page's breadcrumb) is asserted on every platform as before. *What runs on Windows:* everything, with the Windows name: the three titles of both pages read the name exactly (nothing double-escaped), the grant page's tooltip reads it exactly, the ID rows, and the attribute check (no attribute name holds a piece of the name; an attribute value holding its head `q'x` or its tail `y{z}` holds the whole name). *What does not run on Windows:* anything with a double quote. HTML attributes are normally written in double quotes, and an unescaped `'` does not end such an attribute, so on Windows the attribute check can only catch a break-out of a single-quoted attribute; that an unescaped `"` does not cut a double-quoted attribute is checked with `q"x'y{z}` on Linux and macOS only, and in e2e on a Linux Jenkins (unit `r27-titles-revert`, section E, whose item is `r27-d1/q"x'y{z}...`). This leaves no Windows behaviour unchecked through an item name: a Jenkins home on NTFS cannot hold an item with that character. *One change to the attribute check, needed by the Windows name.* A link to the item holds the name as core writes it into a URL (`hudson.Util.rawEncode`): `q%22x'y%7Bz%7D`, and for the Windows name `q'x'y%7Bz%7D`. Core leaves `'` as it is, so the Windows form starts with the head `q'x` although it is the whole name, and the first run with the Windows name failed on `<a href="/jenkins/job/ops/job/q'x'y%7Bz%7D/">` ("the attribute holds only a piece of the item name"), a correct link. The check therefore takes the URL form of the name out of a value before it looks for pieces (premise asserted: that form ends in `y%7Bz%7D` and holds no `"` and no `y{z}`). The URL form of `q"x'y{z}` holds neither its head `q"x` nor its tail `y{z}`, so with the original name the check finds exactly what it found before; nothing was weakened there. *Running the Windows variant without Windows.* `-Dbatchcontrol.test.ntfsItemNames=true` (`PlatformFixtures.NTFS_ITEM_NAMES_PROPERTY`) makes `itemName` answer the NTFS variant on any platform; unset or `false` the probe decides, so the default is the platform, and the property can only take the double quote away. The row prints the name it used (`T-UI-233 fixture: the item is named ...`). Run on macOS on this branch: `mvn -q test -Dtest='PageTitleIdRowTest,RevertPlacementTest'`: 7 + 3 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, name `q"x'y{z}`; the same with `-Dbatchcontrol.test.ntfsItemNames=true`: 7 + 3 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, name `q'x'y{z}`; with the property ItemScopeUiTest (9) and MoveRefusalPageTest (4), the users of `HOSTILE_ITEM_NAME`, are green too. *Not verified:* the row on a real Windows; this change was not run there by the test author, the next Windows CI run is the evidence.
